```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, ref } from 'vue'

const scroller = ref<HTMLElement>()
const second = ref<HTMLElement>()
const useSecond = ref(false)
onMounted(() => {
  if (scroller.value) {
    scroller.value.scrollTop = 240
    scroller.value.dispatchEvent(new Event('scroll'))
  }
})
</script>

<template>
  <div class="back-top-demo">
    <p>Scroll inside this panel. The button appears at 120px.</p>
    <mp-button @click="useSecond = !useSecond">Switch target {{ useSecond ? 'B' : 'A' }}</mp-button>
    <div class="back-top-demo__frame">
      <div ref="scroller" class="back-top-demo__scroll">
        <p v-for="row in 30" :key="row">A · Scroll content {{ row }}</p>
      </div>
      <div ref="second" class="back-top-demo__scroll">
        <p v-for="row in 30" :key="row">B · Scroll content {{ row }}</p>
      </div>
      <mp-back-top
        :target-container="() => (useSecond ? second : scroller)"
        :popup-container="false"
        :visible-height="120"
        :right="16"
        :bottom="16"
        aria-label="Back to top"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>

}
```

The examples use isolated local containers. Omit `target-container` to listen to the page, not the nearest scrollable ancestor. A selector that is invalid or missing hides the button; use a reactive getter for a container mounted asynchronously. `popup-container` controls where the button renders, not what scrolls.

## Lifecycle and edge cases

### Scheduling Lifecycle

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target-container` | Scroll target; omitted means page | Scheduling Lifecycle |
| `popup-container` | Render target; false renders locally | Scheduling Lifecycle |
| `duration` | Animation duration in ms; 0 is immediate | Scheduling Lifecycle |
| `easing` | Built-in curve or normalized progress function | Scheduling Lifecycle |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/back-top/example/demos/en-US/scheduler-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const first = ref()
const second = ref()
const active = ref(true)
const alternate = ref(false)
let retained
const capture = (instance) => {
  if (instance) {
    retained = instance
  }
}
const lower = () => {
  if (first.value) {
    first.value.scrollTop = 300
  }
  if (second.value) {
    second.value.scrollTop = 300
  }
}
</script>
<template>
  <div style="position: relative">
    <mp-button @click="lower">Scroll down / 滚动到底部</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="alternate = !alternate">Switch target / 切换目标</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="active = !active">Activate / 停用与激活</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="retained?.scrollToTop()">Retained command / 保留命令</mp-button>
    <p>Start an animation, switch or deactivate before completion. Old work must not resume.</p>
    <div ref="first" style="height: 100px; overflow: auto"><div style="height: 500px">Target A</div></div>
    <div ref="second" style="height: 100px; overflow: auto"><div style="height: 500px">Target B</div></div>
    <KeepAlive>
      <mp-back-top
        v-if="active"
        :ref="capture"
        :target-container="() => (alternate ? second : first)"
        :popup-container="false"
        :duration="1000"
        easing="linear"
      />
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Easing and errors

duration must be finite, nonnegative milliseconds; zero scrolls immediately. Invalid durations produce Vue prop validation warnings in development and retain the immediate-completion runtime fallback. The easing presets are linear, quartOut and easeInOutCubic; invalid names warn and fall back to quartOut. A custom function receives progress from 0 to 1: finite results are clamped to 0–1, while nonfinite or nonnumeric results use the current linear progress. Promises are not awaited. Thrown errors propagate unchanged to the calling environment; that frame schedules no further animation, and scrollToTop can retry. No click success or extra error event is fabricated.

## API

### BackTop Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target-container` | Scroll target; omitted means page | `string \| HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement \| null \| undefined)` | `—` |
| `popup-container` | Render target; false renders locally | `string \| HTMLElement \| false` | `body` |
| `visible-height` | Inclusive scroll threshold in px, numeric strings accepted | `number \| string` | `200` |
| `duration` | Animation duration in ms; 0 is immediate | `number` | `200` |
| `easing` | Built-in curve or normalized progress function | `'linear' \| 'quartOut' \| 'easeInOutCubic' \| ((progress: number) => number)` | `'quartOut'` |
| `right` | Right offset; number in px, string accepts CSS units | `number \| string` | `—` |
| `bottom` | Bottom offset; number in px, string accepts CSS units | `number \| string` | `—` |
| `elevation` | Shadow level; true uses level 2 | `boolean \| number` | `true` |
| `aria-label` | Accessible name | `string` | `'Back to top'` |

When `popup-container=false`, the button is positioned absolutely; give its containing block `position: relative`. Repeated clicks replace the previous animation; changing target, deactivation and unmount cancel queued work. Reduced-motion preference skips animation. Horizontal scroll position is preserved.

### BackTop Events / Slots / Methods

- `click(event: MouseEvent)`: emitted once per activation.
- Default slot: noninteractive text or icons. The root is already a native button; do not nest another Button or link.
- `scrollToTop()`: scrolls the current target without emitting an additional click.
- Keyboard: Tab focuses the visible button; Enter / Space activates it. Hidden buttons are not focusable.

## Types

```ts
import type { BackTopProps, BackTopInstance, BackTopTarget, BackTopEasing } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
```

### Imports and event types

The subentry default component and the named components from the subentry and root are the same component. Props includes actual listener parameters. Events remain notifications and do not await returned Promises. Use only the documented instance methods.

```ts
import BackTop, { BackTop as NamedBackTop } from '@maple-design/ui-vue/back-top'
import { BackTop as RootBackTop } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import type { BackTopProps, BackTopInstance } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import type { BackTopProps as SubBackTopProps } from '@maple-design/ui-vue/back-top'
const options: BackTopProps = { onClick: (event: MouseEvent) => event.preventDefault() }
```

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-back-top-background` | `var(--mp-sys-color-surface-raised)` | `background` |
| `--mp-back-top-bottom` | `40px` | `bottom` |
| `--mp-back-top-button-border-radius` | `50%` | `border-radius` |

| `--mp-back-top-focus-offset` | `2px` | `outline-offset` |
| `--mp-back-top-focus-width` | `2px` | `outline` |
| `--mp-back-top-font-size` | `var(--mp-sys-font-size-md)` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-back-top-hover-background` | `var(--mp-sys-color-state-hover)` | `background` |
| `--mp-back-top-icon-size` | `20px` | `height`, `width` |
| `--mp-back-top-right` | `40px` | `right` |
| `--mp-back-top-text-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-brand)` | `color` |
| `--mp-back-top-z-index` | `var(--mp-z-index-local-sticky)` | `z-index` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-back-top-background: var(--mp-sys-color-surface-raised);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

## Usage notes

### Configuration

All public Badge variables and defaults:

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->
Numeric `content` supports finite nonnegative values. Zero appears only when `show-zero` is true; dot mode and the `content` slot follow the same rule. Strings are displayed verbatim, including `0`. Negative and non-finite numbers are hidden. `max=0` disables truncation and an invalid maximum falls back to 99. Offsets accept finite negative values; invalid offsets fall back to `0`. In floating mode positive offsets move inward from the anchored edge, while positive vertical offsets at side midpoints move downward. Inline mode ignores horizontal offset and applies vertical offset as a block margin selected by start/end. A provided default slot counts as a host even when empty. The `content` slot overrides the default badge but remains subject to `show` and numeric zero visibility.

### Badge Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------: |
| description | Fallback description text | `string` | `-` |
| content | Badge content | `number \| string` | `-` |
| max | Maximum displayed numeric badge value. Numeric content above this value is shown as `${max}+`. | `number` | `99` |
| dot | Display a dot | `boolean` | `false` |
| offset-x | Horizontal offset; ignored in inline mode | `number` | `0` |
| offset-y | Vertical offset | `number` | `0` |
| color | Custom color; outline uses it for border and text | `string` | `-` |
| text-color | Content text color | `string` | `-` |
| mode | Layout mode | `'floating' \| 'inline'` | `floating` |
| position | Physical corner or left/right midpoint inside the host box, default top-right. Only used in floating mode; RTL does not mirror it | `'top-right' \| 'top-left' \| 'bottom-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `top-right` |
| inline-position | Inline badge at the logical start or end of the host content, default end. Only used in inline mode | `'start' \| 'end'` | `end` |
| size | Size | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `md` |
| status | Semantic status | `SemanticStatus`<br>`'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `danger` |
| show | Show the badge | `boolean` | `true` |
| show-zero | Show numeric zero | `boolean` | `false` |
| variant | Appearance | `'outline' \| 'default'` | `default` |

### Badge Events

No component-specific events.

### Badge Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---- |
| default | Fallback description text | - |
| content | Content displayed inside the badge | - |

### Badge Methods

No public methods.

### Usage notes

Props and slots match across platforms. Without a default slot and with an empty description, the badge renders independently inline. Omitting content displays a dot. Each library reads text direction from its own configuration and supplies its own theme colors and CSS prefix.
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

## Types

```ts
type SemanticStatus = 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'tertiary'
type BadgeVariant = 'default' | 'outline'
type BadgeMode = 'floating' | 'inline'
type BadgePosition = 'top-right' | 'top-left' | 'bottom-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'left' | 'right'
type BadgeInlinePosition = 'start' | 'end'
type BadgeSize = 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'
```

## CSS Variables

Filled badge text follows Button: primary, info, success, warning, danger and secondary use `content-on-dark`; tertiary uses `content-on-dark` in light mode and `content-on-bright` in dark mode. Default notification badges use red backgrounds and white text; the neutral background remains `#e0e0e0`.

Colored outline text and borders follow Button, using the matching `content-brand`, `content-info`, `content-success`, `content-warning` and `content-danger` semantic roles; secondary and tertiary outlines use `content-secondary` for readability. `variant-outline-bg-color` works for every status and defaults to transparent. The `color` prop overrides outline text and border; `text-color` overrides text further. Both preserve control through the background variable. Recheck contrast after customizing foreground or background.

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-badge-bg-color: rgb(var(--mp-danger-7));
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

### Color override boundaries

The bg-color fallback and danger fill use red backgrounds with white text: danger level 7 in light mode and level 4 in dark mode. Fixed neutral light gray and secondary/tertiary gray levels are intentional component colors. Override the border-color isolation ring to match the host surface. Callers must ensure contrast for custom color/text-color values.

Document: llms/en-US/breadcrumb.md

<!-- Source: src/breadcrumb/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/breadcrumb -->

# Breadcrumb

The current page uses primary text color with normal font weight and `aria-current="page"`. Plain text has no interaction feedback. Links, click actions and dropdown triggers use brand color, pointer cursor, hover / pressed feedback and a visible keyboard focus outline. Click actions support Enter and Space. Keep the last item as plain text unless an action is explicitly supplied.

On touch devices, interactive items have a minimum 44 × 44px target. Press feedback clears after release; mouse hover styles do not stick. The default ellipsis is static; use a focusable button in the more-icon slot with a Tooltip to reveal omitted paths.

The default navigation landmark and ellipsis labels follow the current locale. Set aria-label on the root to customize the landmark name.

### Intro

Identify the page location in a hierarchy and navigate upward when needed. The API aligns with Cedar Design Web core features (`routes` / `max-count` / separator slots). Affix positioning is not included for mobile.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/breadcrumb/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-breadcrumb>
    <mp-breadcrumb-item>Home</mp-breadcrumb-item>
    <mp-breadcrumb-item>Channel</mp-breadcrumb-item>
    <mp-breadcrumb-item>News</mp-breadcrumb-item>
  </mp-breadcrumb>
</template>
```

## Content and presentation

### Route Configuration

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routes` | Route data (used when default slot is empty) | Route Configuration, Dropdown, Max Count |
| `max-count` | Max visible normal items, excluding more; `0` means unlimited | Max Count |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Pass breadcrumb data via `routes`. Ancestor paths render as native links; the current page remains text. Customize with `#item-render`.

Example source: src/breadcrumb/example/demos/routes-mode.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-breadcrumb :routes="routes" @click.prevent />
    <mp-breadcrumb :routes="routes">
      <template #item-render="{ route, routes, paths }">
        <span v-if="route === routes[routes.length - 1]">{{ route.label }}</span>
        <mp-link v-else :href="paths.join('/')" @click.prevent>
          {{ route.label }}
        </mp-link>
      </template>
    </mp-breadcrumb>
    <mp-breadcrumb :routes="routes">
      <template #item-render="{ route, routes }">
        <span v-if="route === routes[routes.length - 1]">{{ route.label }}</span>
        <RouterLink v-else :to="route.to">
          {{ route.label }}
        </RouterLink>
      </template>
    </mp-breadcrumb>
  </mp-space>
</template>

<script lang="ts">
import { RouterLink } from 'vue-router'

export default {
  components: { RouterLink },
  setup() {
    const routes = [
      {
        path: '/',
        to: { query: { breadcrumb: 'home' } },
        label: 'Home',
      },
      {
        path: '/channel',
        to: { query: { breadcrumb: 'channel' } },
        label: 'Channel',
      },
      {
        path: '/news',
        to: { query: { breadcrumb: 'news' } },
        label: 'News',
      },
    ]
    return { routes }
  },
}
</script>
```

### Dropdown

Example source: src/breadcrumb/example/demos/dropdown.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-breadcrumb :routes="routes" @click.prevent @select="handleSelect" />
    <span v-if="selectedPath">Selected: {{ selectedPath }}</span>
    <mp-breadcrumb>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>Home</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item :droplist="droplist"> Channel </mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>News</mp-breadcrumb-item>
    </mp-breadcrumb>
    <mp-breadcrumb>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>Home</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>
        <template #droplist>
          <mp-menu-option>Option 1</mp-menu-option>
          <mp-menu-option>Option 2</mp-menu-option>
          <mp-menu-option>Option 3</mp-menu-option>
        </template>
        Channel
      </mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>News</mp-breadcrumb-item>
    </mp-breadcrumb>
  </mp-space>
</template>

<script lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

export default {
  setup() {
    const selectedPath = ref('')
    const handleSelect = (route: { path: string }) => {
      selectedPath.value = route.path
    }
    const routes = [
      {
        path: '/',
        label: 'Home',
      },
      {
        path: '/channel',
        label: 'Channel',
        children: [
          { path: '/goods', label: 'Goods' },
          { path: '/wallet', label: 'Wallet' },
        ],
      },
      {
        path: '/news',
        label: 'News',
      },
    ]
    const droplist = [
      {
        path: '/goods',
        label: 'Goods',
      },
      {
        path: '/wallet',
        label: 'Wallet',
      },
    ]
    return { routes, droplist, selectedPath, handleSelect }
  },
}
</script>
```

### Max Count

Limit visible items with `max-count`. Overflow is collapsed into an ellipsis. Customize with `#more-icon`.

Example source: src/breadcrumb/example/demos/max-count.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-breadcrumb :max-count="3">
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>Home</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>Sub Home</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>All Channel</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>Channel</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>News</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>Post</mp-breadcrumb-item>
    </mp-breadcrumb>
    <mp-breadcrumb :routes="maxRoutes" :max-count="3" @click.prevent>
      <template #more-icon="{ omittedItems }">
        <mp-tooltip :trigger="['hover', 'focus', 'click']" :content="omittedLabel(omittedItems)">
          <mp-button html-type="button" variant="text" class="more-trigger" aria-label="查看隐藏路径">
            <m-icon-more aria-hidden="true" />
          </mp-button>
        </mp-tooltip>
      </template>
    </mp-breadcrumb>
  </mp-space>
</template>

<script lang="ts">
import type { BreadcrumbRoute } from '../../types'

const omittedLabel = (items: BreadcrumbRoute[]) => items.map((item) => item.label).join(' / ')

export default {
  setup() {
    const maxRoutes = [
      { path: '/', label: 'Home' },
      { path: '/sub-home', label: 'Sub Home' },
      { path: '/all-channel', label: 'All Channel' },
      { path: '/channel', label: 'Channel' },
      { path: '/news', label: 'News' },
      { path: '/post', label: 'Post' },
    ]
    return { maxRoutes, omittedLabel }
  },
}
</script>

<style scoped>
.more-trigger {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  min-width: 44px;
  min-height: 44px;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  color: inherit;
  background: transparent;
  cursor: pointer;
}
</style>
```

### Link & Click

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

      <mp-breadcrumb-item>News</mp-breadcrumb-item>
    </mp-breadcrumb>

      <mp-breadcrumb-item @click="record('Channel')">Channel</mp-breadcrumb-item>
      <mp-breadcrumb-item>News</mp-breadcrumb-item>
```

For routes with children, the parent remains a link and a separate button opens the menu. Selecting a child emits select(route, event) from the root; the application decides whether to navigate. Listen on individual manually composed BreadcrumbItem components for their select events.

## API

### Breadcrumb Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `separator` | Range separator | _string \| number_ | `/` |
| `max-count` | Max visible normal items, excluding more; `0` means unlimited | _number_ | `0` |
| `routes` | Route data (used when default slot is empty) | _BreadcrumbRoute[]_ | `-` |

### Breadcrumb Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| select | Emitted when a built-in dropdown child is selected in routes mode | `route: BreadcrumbRoute, event?: Event` |

The `more-icon` slot receives omitted route data only in routes mode. With manually composed default-slot items, omittedItems is empty; count, start and end still describe the omitted range.

### BreadcrumbItem Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `separator` | Separator; overrides parent | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `href` | Link URL | _string_ | `-` |
| `droplist` | Dropdown menu content | _BreadcrumbRoute['children']_ | `-` |
| `dropdown-props` | Menu props; open, onUpdate:open and onSelect are managed by the component | _MenuProps_ | `-` |

### BreadcrumbItem Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | Fired on click (not for collapsed item) | `event: MouseEvent` |
| `select` | Fired when a built-in dropdown item is selected | `route: BreadcrumbRoute, event?: Event` |

### BreadcrumbItem Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | Breadcrumb content | `-` |
| `separator` | Custom separator; overrides parent | `-` |
| `droplist` | Custom dropdown menu | `-` |

### Breadcrumb Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | Breadcrumb children | `-` |
| `separator` | Custom separator | `-` |
| `item-render` | Custom render in `routes` mode | `route` `routes` `paths` |
| `more-icon` | Custom ellipsis icon | `omittedItems` `count` `start` `end` |

## Types

```ts
interface BreadcrumbRoute {
  label: string
  path: string
  children?: BreadcrumbRoute[]
}
```

## Usage notes



- A nonempty `routes` array takes precedence over the default slot; an empty array falls back to the slot. Default route rendering links all items except the last, which has `aria-current="page"`. `item-render` controls links itself.
- Separator precedence: child slot → child prop → parent slot → parent prop. `0` and an empty string are supported.
- `max-count` is a nonnegative integer; 0 means unlimited. A value of 1 acts as 2 to preserve the first and current items. Positive fractions are rounded down and clamped to at least 2; negative or nonfinite values act as 0. Invalid values produce a development warning. Collapsing occurs only when the total exceeds the effective count plus 1; the overflow position does not trigger omitted items’ clicks, links or dropdowns.
- Built-in dropdown selection emits `select(route, event)`. Indices and separators update with dynamic insertion, removal, reordering and SSR.
- Custom attributes apply to the breadcrumb item content node.

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-breadcrumb-icon-color: var(--mp-breadcrumb-item-inactive-color);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Browser Adaptation

### Browser compatibility and acceptance

Maple primarily targets mobile environments: the latest two stable iOS Safari and Android Chrome versions, plus the Android System WebView, WeChat and embedded app browsers used by the product. Minimum OS and engine versions require native-device evidence; an Android OS version or desktop mobile emulation is insufficient.

Viewport conversion and desktop touch emulation address layout and input modes. Native acceptance additionally covers touch gestures, IME/autofill, software keyboards, popup positioning and scroll locking, orientation/address-bar changes, safe areas, file upload and camera entry points. Automated Chromium/Firefox/WebKit results are recorded separately from native Safari, WeChat and app WebView acceptance.

At the repository root, run `pnpm check:compatibility`, create the native template with `pnpm compatibility:native:init`, and validate native evidence with `pnpm check:compatibility:release`. The shared policy lives in the sibling design-ui repository at `standards/browser-compatibility.md`. Environments without evidence remain pending.


### Intro

The component library provides mobile and desktop adaptations,
scheme `touch-emulator` is used for mobile terminal adaptation,
scheme `touch-emulator` is used for mobile terminal adaptation.

### Mobile Adaptation

#### CSS Unit Adaptation

The component library design is based on the `375px` width design draft. 
It is recommended to use [postcss-px-to-viewport](https://github.com/evrone/postcss-px-to-viewport) to convert `px` units into `vw` units to achieve mobile terminal adaptation.
Create `postcss.config.js` under the `Webpack/Vite` project root path And do the following configuration `375px -> 100vw`.

```shell
# playground-ignore
# npm
npm i postcss-px-to-viewport -D

# yarn
yarn add postcss-px-to-viewport -D

# pnpm
pnpm add postcss-px-to-viewport -D
```

```js
// playground-ignore
// postcss.config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: {
    'postcss-px-to-viewport': {
      viewportWidth: 375,
      unitPrecision: 6,
      unitToConvert: 'px',
      viewportUnit: 'vmin',
      fontViewportUnit: 'vmin',
      propList: ['*'],
    }
  }
}
```

#### Theme Unit Adaptation (Viewport)

Because the theme is mounted at runtime and is not affected by postcss, the component library provides a utility tool `Themes.toViewport` for adaptation. The theme returned by the function will use the `375px -> 100vmin` rule by default.

```js
import { Themes } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const viewportTheme = Themes.toViewport(Themes.maple.dark)
```

You can also make changes to the conversion rules

```js
import { Themes } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const viewportTheme = Themes.toViewport(Themes.maple.dark, {
  // defaults 375
  viewportWidth: 750,
  // defaults 'vmin'
  viewportUnit: 'vw',
  // defaults 6
  unitPrecision: 4,
})
```

#### Theme Unit Adaptation (Rem)

Similar to the Viewport solution

```js
import { Themes } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const remTheme = Themes.toRem(Themes.maple.dark)
```

Or customize

```js
import { Themes } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const viewportTheme = Themes.toRem(Themes.maple.dark, {
  // defaults 16
  rootFontSize: 32,
  // defaults 6
  unitPrecision: 4,
})
```

### Desktop Adaptation

Because component library interaction events are developed using `touch` events, `mouse` events on the desktop side are not supported.
It is recommended to use `@maple-design/touch-emulator-vue` to set `touch -> mouse` for desktop adaptation.

```shell
# playground-ignore
# npm
npm i @maple-design/touch-emulator-vue
# yarn
yarn add @maple-design/touch-emulator-vue
# pnpm
pnpm add @maple-design/touch-emulator-vue
```

```js
// playground-ignore
import '@maple-design/touch-emulator-vue'
```

# Button

Disabled colors depend on the variant: colored solid fills use a lighter status background; text and outline remain transparent with muted status text; tonal keeps its light background. Neutral buttons use disabled neutral colors. Custom color/text-color is suspended while disabled; hover/active feedback and elevation are suppressed.

Both libraries use the same implementation and examples; package prefixes, themes and registration stay local.

## Basic examples

### Eight statuses

Example source: src/button/example/demos/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const statuses = ['default', 'primary', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'info', 'success', 'warning', 'danger'] as const
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space wrap size="12px">
    <mp-button v-for="status in statuses" :key="status" :status="status">{{ status }}</mp-button>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Appearance and states

### Variants, statuses and sizes

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | Appearance; inherits from the button group when omitted, otherwise outline | Variants, statuses and sizes, Custom colors |
| `size` | Size; inherits group, otherwise md | Variants, statuses and sizes, Five sizes |
| `status` | Semantic color; inherits group, otherwise default | Variants, statuses and sizes |
| `disabled` | Disabled; inherits group, explicit false overrides | Disabled buttons and links |
| `component` | Root tag; link attributes fall through | Disabled buttons and links |
| `loading` | Loading; blocks activation and navigation | Disabled buttons and links |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->

Choose a variant and size to compare eight semantic colors. Filled buttons suit primary actions; text and outline suit secondary actions. The few variant, size and background options are shown directly with button-style RadioGroups. Form/FormItem provide standard field layout; Card carries the background comparison.

Example source: src/button/example/demos/variants.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const variant = ref('default')
const size = ref('md')
const background = ref('navy')
const variants = ['default', 'text', 'outline', 'tonal']
const sizes = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl']
const statuses = ['default', 'primary', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'info', 'success', 'warning', 'danger']
const backgrounds = [
  { label: 'Navy / 深蓝', value: 'navy', color: '#17224B' },
  { label: 'White / 白色', value: 'light', color: '#FFFFFF' },
  { label: 'Light gray / 浅灰', value: 'muted', color: '#F5F5F5' },
  { label: 'Dark gray / 深灰', value: 'dark', color: '#252525' },
]
const cardBackground = computed(() => backgrounds.find((item) => item.value === background.value)?.color)
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" block align="stretch" :size="16">
    <mp-form layout="vertical" size="sm">
      <mp-form-item label="Variant" field="variant">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="variant" :options="variants" aria-label="Button variant" variant="button" />
      </mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item label="Size" field="size">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="size" :options="sizes" aria-label="Button size" variant="button" />
      </mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item label="Background" field="background">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="background" :options="backgrounds" aria-label="Button background" variant="button" />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-card
      class="button-variant-card"
      :data-background="background"
      :elevation="false"
      :style="{ '--mp-card-background': cardBackground }"
    >
      <mp-space wrap>
        <mp-button v-for="status in statuses" :key="status" :status="status" :variant="variant" :size="size">{{
          status
        }}</mp-button>
      </mp-space>
    </mp-card>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Five sizes

Horizontal buttons and inputs of the same size share the default height and font size within each platform. Cedar heights are 24/28/32/36/44px; Maple heights are 32/40/48/56/64px. Horizontal button padding is 8/12/16/20/24px per side, with a 6px icon-label gap. Stacked buttons keep their separate content-based height. Component-level overrides remain independent.

Example source: src/button/example/demos/size.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const sizes = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <mp-space v-for="size in sizes" :key="size" align="center" wrap :size="12">
      <span>{{ size }}</span>
      <mp-input :size="size" :aria-label="`Input ${size}`" placeholder="Input" style="width: 140px" />
      <mp-button :size="size">Button</mp-button>
      <mp-button :size="size"
        ><template #icon><m-icon-search /></template>Search</mp-button
      >
    </mp-space>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Icons and layout

### Icons and label layouts

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | Semantic color; inherits group, otherwise default | Icons and label layouts |
| `variant` | Appearance; inherits from the button group when omitted, otherwise outline | Icons and label layouts |
| `size` | Size; inherits group, otherwise md | Icons and label layouts |
| `stacked` | Stack icon and text; inherits group when omitted | Icons and label layouts |
| `round` | Round button | Icons and label layouts |
| `block` | Full available width | Block buttons |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->

Use built-in icons to compare icon-only, inline and stacked labels across four variants and five sizes. Stacked buttons grow with content and keep at least 8px of top and bottom padding. Omit the default slot for icon-only buttons; round controls shape and stacked controls label layout.

Example source: src/button/example/demos/icons.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const sizes = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const
const variants = ['default', 'text', 'outline', 'tonal'] as const
const layouts = ['icon', 'inline', 'stacked'] as const
const size = ref<(typeof sizes)[number]>('md')
const variant = ref<(typeof variants)[number]>('tonal')
const items = [
  { status: 'default', icon: 'plus', label: 'Add' },
  { status: 'primary', icon: 'reply', label: 'Reply' },
  { status: 'info', icon: 'info-circle', label: 'Info' },
  { status: 'success', icon: 'check', label: 'Confirm' },
  { status: 'warning', icon: 'delete', label: 'Delete' },
  { status: 'danger', icon: 'close', label: 'Close' },
] as const
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <mp-form layout="vertical" size="sm">
      <mp-form-item label="Variant" field="variant">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="variant" :options="variants" aria-label="Icon button variant" variant="button" />
      </mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item label="Size" field="size">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="size" :options="sizes" aria-label="Icon button size" variant="button" />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-space v-for="layout in layouts" :key="layout" direction="column" :size="8">
      <span>{{
        layout === 'icon'
          ? 'Icon only / 纯图标'
          : layout === 'inline'
            ? 'Icon and text / 横排图文'
            : 'Stacked / 上下堆叠'
      }}</span>
      <mp-space wrap>
        <mp-button
          v-for="item in items"
          :key="item.label"
          :status="item.status"
          :variant="variant"
          :size="size"
          :stacked="layout === 'stacked'"
          :round="layout === 'icon'"
          :aria-label="item.label"
        >
          <template #icon>
            <m-icon-plus v-if="item.icon === 'plus'" />
            <m-icon-reply v-else-if="item.icon === 'reply'" />
            <m-icon-info-circle v-else-if="item.icon === 'info-circle'" />
            <m-icon-check v-else-if="item.icon === 'check'" />
            <m-icon-delete v-else-if="item.icon === 'delete'" />
            <m-icon-close v-else-if="item.icon === 'close'" />
          </template>
          <template v-if="layout !== 'icon'" #default>{{ item.label }}</template>
        </mp-button>
      </mp-space>
    </mp-space>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Forms and events

### Form control size comparison

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | Size; inherits group, otherwise md | Form control size comparison |
| `variant` | Appearance; inherits from the button group when omitted, otherwise outline | Form control size comparison |
| `html-type` | Native button type | Native form, focus and touch events |
| `focusable` | Allow sequential Tab focus; does not prevent programmatic focus | Native form, focus and touch events |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->

Compare Input, Button, Select, date/time fields and other single-line controls at the same size. Field variants share the height scale; Button uses outline here. DatePicker/TimePicker are panels; this example uses Date/Time fields. The example includes selected and clearable values, removable tags and long multiple selections. Select/Cascader keep the same size height with tag-nowrap. Long tag text uses ellipsis while removal icons remain available; tags scroll horizontally while clear and arrow controls stay outside the scrolling area. Hover, focus or tap truncated tag text to read its full content; dismiss with an outside click or Escape without changing the selected value. Restore values after clearing to repeat the comparison. Multiline text and wrapping multiple selections can grow with content.

Example source: src/field-decorator/example/demos/control-sizes.vue


### Native form, focus and touch events

Example source: src/button/example/demos/native-events.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('Editable')
const submissions = ref(0)
const event = ref('Use Tab or Enter')
</script>
<template>
  <mp-form style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px" @submit="submissions++" @reset="value = 'Editable'">
    <mp-input
      v-model="value"
      aria-label="Example field"
      placeholder="Example field"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 280px"
    />
    <mp-button html-type="submit">Submit</mp-button>
    <mp-button html-type="reset">Reset</mp-button>
    <mp-button :focusable="false">Skip Tab</mp-button>
    <mp-button @focus="event = 'focus'" @blur="event = 'blur'" @click="event = 'click'">Event target</mp-button>
  </mp-form>
  <p aria-live="polite">Submissions: {{ submissions }}; {{ event }}</p>
</template>
```

## Loading and action feedback

### Loading animations, layouts and sizes

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loading` | Loading; blocks activation and navigation | Loading animations, layouts and sizes, Loading indicator appearance |
| `loading-size` | Indicator size; xs/sm/md/lg/xl map to 12/14/16/18/20px; numbers are px; follows button size when omitted; not used in line mode | Loading animations, layouts and sizes, Loading indicator appearance |
| `loading-type` | Spinner animation; same as Loading.type; not used in line mode | Loading animations, layouts and sizes |
| `loading-mode` | Inline, covering, or bottom progress line; line only uses loading-color | Loading animations, layouts and sizes |
| `loading-color` | Loading indicator color | Loading indicator appearance |
| `ripple` | Click ripple | Ripple and elevation feedback |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Choose a loading layout and indicator size to compare five animations. Click a select arrow to open its menu, then choose an option to close it. Loading buttons keep their label and prevent repeated actions.

Example source: src/button/example/demos/loading.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const stacked = ref(false)
const mode = ref('default')
const size = ref('md')
const modes = ['default', 'fill', 'line']
const sizes = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl']
const types = ['circle', 'wave', 'cube', 'rect', 'disappear']
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <mp-form layout="vertical" size="sm">
      <mp-form-item label="Layout" field="mode">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="mode" :options="modes" aria-label="Loading mode" variant="button" />
      </mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item label="Size" field="size">
        <mp-radio-group
          v-model="size"
          :disabled="mode === 'line'"
          :options="sizes"
          aria-label="Loading size"
          variant="button"
        />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="stacked">图文堆叠（stacked）</mp-checkbox>
    <p v-if="mode === 'line'">
      line 使用底部进度线，loading-type 和 loading-size 不适用；可通过 loading-color 调整颜色。
    </p>
    <mp-space wrap
      ><mp-button
        v-for="type in mode === 'line' ? ['line'] : types"
        :key="type"
        loading
        :stacked="stacked"
        :loading-type="mode === 'line' ? 'circle' : type"
        :loading-mode="mode"
        :loading-size="size"
        ><template #icon
          ><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
            <path d="M8 1v14M1 8h14" stroke="currentColor" /></svg></template
        >{{ type }}</mp-button
      ></mp-space
    >
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Controlled loading and failure recovery

Example source: src/button/example/demos/controlled-loading.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const saving = ref(false)
const failing = ref(false)
const message = ref('点击保存，观察业务控制的 loading / Click Save to start')
const delay = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800))
async function save() {
  if (saving.value) {
    return
  }
  saving.value = true
  try {
    await delay()
    message.value = '保存完成 / Saved'
  } finally {
    saving.value = false
  }
}
async function recover() {
  if (failing.value) {
    return
  }
  failing.value = true
  try {
    await delay()
    throw new Error('模拟请求失败 / Simulated failure')
  } catch (error) {
    message.value = (error as Error).message
  } finally {
    failing.value = false
  }
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12">
    <p>
      click 支持 async 回调；业务通过 loading 展示等待，在 finally 中恢复。Async click handlers own their loading state.
    </p>
    <mp-space wrap :size="12">
      <mp-button :loading="saving" @click="save">保存 / Save</mp-button>
      <mp-button :loading="failing" @click="recover">失败与恢复 / Failure recovery</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p aria-live="polite">{{ message }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Icons and content follow reading order; stacked content remains top to bottom without mirroring custom graphics. ButtonGroup uses its direction for horizontal arrangement, joined borders and end radii; individual buttons may override text direction. Single buttons retain full radii, and vertical groups keep top-to-bottom order. Native Tab, Enter and Space remain available; ordinary groups do not intercept arrow keys. Disabled and loading behavior is unchanged.

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->

### Button Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| status | Semantic color; inherits group, otherwise default | `SemanticStatus`<br>`'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `undefined` |
| variant | Appearance; inherits from the button group when omitted, otherwise outline | `default / text / outline / tonal` | `undefined` |
| size | Size; inherits group, otherwise md | `xs / sm / md / lg / xl` | `undefined` |
| html-type | Native button type | `button / submit / reset` | `button` |
| component | Root tag; link attributes fall through | `button / a` | `button` |
| round | Round button | `boolean` | `false` |
| block | Full available width | `boolean` | `false` |
| loading | Loading; blocks activation and navigation | `boolean` | `false` |
| loading-type | Spinner animation; same as Loading.type; not used in line mode | `circle / wave / cube / rect / disappear` | `circle` |
| loading-mode | Inline, covering, or bottom progress line; line only uses loading-color | `default / fill / line` | `default` |
| loading-size | Indicator size; xs/sm/md/lg/xl map to 12/14/16/18/20px; numbers are px; follows button size when omitted; not used in line mode | `ComponentSize / number`<br>`ComponentSize: 'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `undefined` |
| loading-color | Loading indicator color | `string` | `currentColor` |
| disabled | Disabled; inherits group, explicit false overrides | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| ripple | Click ripple | `boolean` | `true` |
| focusable | Allow sequential Tab focus; does not prevent programmatic focus | `boolean` | `true` |
| autofocus | Native autofocus | `boolean` | `false` |
| text-color | Custom text color | `string` | `undefined` |
| color | Custom background or variant base color | `string` | `undefined` |
| elevation | Shadow for the default variant; true means 1, false disables it, and numbers are rounded and clamped to 0–24; controlled by the group when grouped | `boolean / number` | `false` |
| stacked | Stack icon and text; inherits group when omitted | `boolean` | `undefined` |

### Button Events

| Event | Arguments and behavior |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| click | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |

`click` is a notification event. The component does not process listener return values or switch loading automatically. Business code controls `loading` and should restore it in `finally` after asynchronous work. Disabled or loading links have their effective `href` removed.

### Button Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------- | -------------------------------- | ---- |
| default | Button label; retained while loading | — |
| icon | Leading icon; above label when stacked | — |

### Button Methods

No custom public methods.
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

### ButtonGroup Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| status | Default semantic status for child buttons; individual buttons may override it | `SemanticStatus`<br>`'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | default |
| size | Default child button size; individual buttons may override it | xs / sm / md / lg / xl | undefined |
| variant | Default child appearance; adjacent buttons join using their effective variants, including mixed variants | default / text / outline / tonal | outline |
| color | Default custom child color; individual buttons may override it | string | undefined |
| text-color | Default child text color; individual buttons may override it | string | undefined |
| disabled | Default disabled state; an explicit child false overrides group true | boolean | false |
| stacked | Stack child icon and text vertically by default; a child may explicitly override with false | boolean | false |
| vertical | Vertical group layout, independent of button content stacking | boolean | false |
| elevation | Shadow for the entire group; true means 1 and numbers are normalized to 0–24; applies only to the default variant when the group is enabled | boolean / number | false |

The root defaults to `role="group"`. Supply `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the action group needs a name. Native attributes can override role. Ordinary groups retain native Tab / Enter / Space handling without arrow-key focus management.

**Inheritance:** explicit child status, size, variant, color, text-color, disabled and stacked values take precedence. The group always owns elevation; individual button elevation is ignored. Nested groups use their nearest group's configuration and defaults without automatically accumulating outer disabled state.

### ButtonGroup Events

No custom events. `@click` forwards a native root event and may receive descendant bubbling; listen to each Button's click for its action. The group does not collect event Promises or manage tasks or selection.

### ButtonGroup Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Joined styling supports directly adjacent Button DOM nodes under the group root | — |

**Composition:** extra DOM wrappers, surrounding text and other controls are outside the joined appearance contract. Wrapped buttons may inherit configuration but do not receive the same joined styling. The group owns outer radii and does not preserve a standalone round button's circular appearance. Use Space for separate buttons or mixed content. In narrow areas, business code chooses scrolling, shorter labels or vertical layout; groups do not wrap automatically.

### ButtonGroup Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| buttonGroupProvider | Reactive group configuration with readonly ComputedRef fields; elevation is boolean / number and other fields match the Props |

No additional group action methods.

## Types

ButtonProps、ButtonVariant、ButtonLoadingMode、ButtonInstance、ButtonGroupProps、ButtonGroupInstance。

## CSS Variables

Button exposes 58 appearance tokens. `{status}-color` controls the solid background, `{status}-foreground-color` controls text/outline/tonal foreground, and `{status}-tonal-color` controls soft backgrounds. `solid-text-color` and `solid-state-layer-color` are shared by semantic statuses; default/tertiary foregrounds and primary/tertiary state layers retain theme-specific roles.

Sizes use xs/sm/md/lg/xl. Font sizes, transition duration, focus width/offset and stacked-height increments reuse system variables. Button groups and stacked buttons share border-radius. Four state opacity variables preserve hover/active differences. loading-duration controls only the bottom progress line; Loading controls other loading animations. Internal variables and fixed animation geometry are not public customization points.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-button-border-radius: var(--mp-sys-radius-md);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

Document: llms/en-US/card.md

<!-- Source: src/card/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/card -->

# Card

Source changes synchronously invalidate render generations. Close, row direction, newer work, deactivation or disposal prevent old nextTick/timer/double-frame continuations from changing newer phases. Render/timer deliveries consume once. Recheck lifecycle/request/node after geometry hooks to reject reentrant disposal. Suspension cancels both timers and retained close/click input is inert; activation starts a fresh phase from current props without replay, and initial KeepAlive activation does not duplicate the wait.

## Basic examples

```vue
      description="Keep the team informed."
      top-divider
      bottom-divider

      <template #footer><mp-button status="primary">View details</mp-button></template>
    </mp-card>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

```vue
<script setup>

const __demoAppearance = __demoReactive({ variant: 'default', size: 'md' })
const demoCompareFields = [
  { name: 'variant', values: ['default', 'outline', 'tonal'] },
  { name: 'size', values: ['sm', 'md'] },
]
const demoCompareAxis = demoRef('variant')
const demoComparedOptions = demoComputed(
  () => demoCompareFields.find((field) => field.name === demoCompareAxis.value)?.values ?? [],
)

__demoAppearance['elevation'] = 2
demoCompareFields.push({ name: 'elevation', values: [0, 2, 6] })
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <mp-form layout="vertical">
      <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="variant">

          aria-label="variant"
          :options="[
            { label: 'default', value: 'default' },
            { label: 'outline', value: 'outline' },
            { label: 'tonal', value: 'tonal' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </mp-form-item>

        <mp-radio-group

          aria-label="size"
          :options="[

          size="sm"
        />
      </mp-form-item>

        ><mp-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['elevation']"

            { label: '0', value: 0 },
```

### Composing Tabs and nested cards

Enable `swipeable` to switch tabs with horizontal touch gestures in the content area. The table uses `data-tabs-no-swipe` to preserve horizontal scrolling; swipe outside the table to switch tabs.

Maple has no TypographyTitle component; group headings use native headings.

Compose Card, Tabs and vertical Space. Compact outlined cards group each panel; wide tables scroll within their own container on small screens. The industry panel uses section headings without extra cards.

## Lifecycle and edge cases

### Floating scheduler lifecycle

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `floating` | Floating expansion state; supports v-model:floating | Floating scheduler lifecycle |
| `ripple` | Click ripple | Floating scheduler lifecycle |
| `floating-duration` | Floating expansion transition duration in ms | Floating scheduler lifecycle |
| `title` | Title | Floating scheduler lifecycle |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/card/example/demos/en-US/scheduler-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const active = ref(true)
const mounted = ref(true)
const floating = ref(false)
const ripple = ref(true)
const duration = ref(250)
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <mp-button @click="floating = !floating">Float / 浮起与回落</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="active = !active">Activate / 停用与激活</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="mounted = !mounted">Mount / 卸载与挂载</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="ripple = !ripple">Ripple wait / 涟漪等待</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="duration = duration ? 0 : 250">Duration / 零与默认时长</mp-button>
    <p>
      Toggle floating rapidly, suspend during500ms ripple wait or layout settlement, then activate. Old tasks must not
      reset a newer phase. Underlying doubleRaf frames are not physically canceled.
    </p>
    <KeepAlive v-if="mounted">
      <mp-card
        v-if="active"
        v-model:floating="floating"
        :ripple="ripple"
        :floating-duration="duration"
        title="Floating lifecycle / 浮起生命周期"
      >
        Card content / 卡片内容
        <template #floating-content>
          <mp-button @click.stop="floating = false">Collapse / 回落</mp-button>
          <mp-button @click.stop="active = false">Deactivate / 停用</mp-button>
          <mp-button @click.stop="mounted = false">Unmount / 卸载</mp-button>
        </template>
      </mp-card>
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

The same scenarios, parameters and interactions as Cedar. Only component prefixes differ; themes and site shells remain independent.

## Reading direction

Title, content and actions follow reading order. Default floating actions sit at inline end; images and custom slots are not mirrored.

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->
`row-reverse` reverses the horizontal cover and body order, with reading direction still following the container. Collapsed `floating-content` keeps its nodes and state but is inert to keyboard and assistive technology; it becomes interactive when expanded. Floating is available only in column direction.

The expanded Card keeps its DOM position and native form ownership. Browsers with Popover API support can display it in the top layer, above transformed or clipping ancestors. An existing native modal or open popover in the same document takes precedence until it closes or is removed. The Card checks open shadow roots and its own shadow tree. Hosts manage layers inside other closed shadow roots. When top-layer display is unavailable or opening is canceled, the Card uses fixed positioning within its existing layout. When focus is inside an expanded Card, Escape requests closing unless an inner control has already handled the key; a nested topmost popup handles Escape first. When a button outside the Card opens it in the browser top layer, focus moves to the expanded panel if the button still has focus and the Card is the topmost layer. Pressing Escape on the panel returns focus to the opener. A child control that already has focus keeps it. In the browser top layer, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through the expanded Card and library overlays above it. The expanded panel has the group role. After the top-layer Card finishes opening, background controls become inert. Library overlays above the Card and detectable native top layers remain interactive. Closing or unmounting the Card releases the background and preserves author-supplied `inert`. If a background web component creates a shadow root after isolation starts and immediately opens a native popover, set `popover` on the host and call the host’s `showPopover()`. This lets the Card release the host before opening and isolate it again after closing. Use Dialog when modal dialog semantics are required.

When focus is in a native dialog opened with `showModal()`, Escape goes to the dialog. A `cancel` handler can keep the dialog open, and the Card stays expanded.

Pressing Escape inside an expanded Card dismisses an open native auto or hint popover first. This also applies when focus remains on its trigger.

When focus remains inside the expanded content or on the close button, closing attempts to return focus to the control used before expansion. If focus has moved elsewhere, it is not moved back. During the expansion delay, focusing the expanded content displays it immediately without waiting for the fade-in animation. Expanded content and the close button that are still hidden and unfocused during this delay are excluded from the accessibility tree; focusing either displays them immediately.

If the opener is inside an external closed Shadow Root, Card cannot access the internal control directly. The host must delegate focus or the application must restore focus. `delegatesFocus` can forward host focus into the root, but does not guarantee the original control when several controls are present.

When customizing the title, set `aria-labelledby` to the ID of its text element. For example, use `aria-labelledby="order-title"` on the Card and `<h2 id="order-title">Order details</h2>` in the header slot. This keeps a nearby action button out of the panel name. If the panel has no visible heading, supply `aria-label`.

The default close button uses the current locale's close label; override it with `close-button-aria-label`. `floating-duration` is a finite nonnegative number of milliseconds; 0 disables the delay and invalid values fall back to 250. With reduced motion enabled, opening and closing do not wait for ripple or transition animations; changing the preference during an animation also takes effect.

### Card Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | Appearance | `default / outline / tonal` | `outline` |
| size | Density; omitted value follows platform rules below | `sm / md` | `undefined` |
| direction | Order of cover and body, default column; supports row, column and row-reverse. Does not position the card itself | `row / column / row-reverse` | `column` |
| hoverable | Hover styling | `boolean` | `false` |
| title-style | Title row styles | `CSSProperties` | `undefined` |
| title | Title | `string` | `undefined` |
| subtitle | Subtitle | `string` | `undefined` |
| description | Description | `string` | `undefined` |
| top-divider | Top divider | `boolean` | `false` |
| bottom-divider | Bottom divider | `boolean` | `false` |
| image-src | Cover image URL; cover slot takes precedence | `string` | `undefined` |
| image-fit | Cover image fit | `fill / contain / cover / none / scale-down` | `cover` |
| image-height | Image height; numbers use px | `string / number` | `undefined` |

| aria-labelledby | ID of the visible heading in a custom title or header slot. | `string` | `—` |
| close-button-aria-label | Accessible name of the default close button | `string` | `—` |

### Card Methods

No public methods.

### Usage notes

Props, event arguments and slots match. Cedar inherits the global size when size is omitted: xs/sm map to sm, all others to md. Maple falls back to md. Pass size explicitly for identical density. Themes and CSS prefixes remain platform-specific.
Use the Loading directive to compose a loading overlay on Card.

## CSS Variables

Regular/filled backgrounds and borders use `surface-default`, `surface-muted` and `border-default`. Titles, body and secondary text use `content-primary`, `content-tertiary` and `content-secondary`. Expanded floating buttons use `content-primary`; text and icons on dark close buttons use `content-on-dark`.

### Sizing and motion

Use `--mp-card-content-row-margin` for horizontal content spacing. Card supports only sm / md sizes. `--mp-card-animation-duration` defaults to `var(--mp-sys-motion-duration-slow)` and `--mp-card-animation-easing` to `var(--mp-sys-motion-easing-standard)`. Reduced motion disables Card transitions.

# Carousel

Autoplay interval is business playback cadence (business-clock), not CSS duration. Autoplay remains off by default; true uses3000ms, with existing numeric/config intervals and hover/focus/hidden pause rules. Cancellation/replacement invalidates old playback work; delivery consumes once before navigation. Retained inactive/disposed next/prev/to, keyboard and wheel cannot navigate or intercept input. Activation creates fresh observer/event bindings; detached deliveries cannot use a newer active state to reschedule.

### Multiple Slides Per View

The demo shows 2.5 items and lets you drag or toggle acceptance and looping. Current is the parent-accepted page index starting at 1, Proposal records requests, and Changes counts change notifications. When updates are rejected, a request or change does not mean the model changed. Accepted updates allow dragging in either direction; disabling looping prevents crossing the ends.

Example source: src/carousel/example/demos/multi-slides.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const current = ref(1)
const proposal = ref(1)
const changes = ref(0)
const accept = ref(true)
const loop = ref(true)
function update(value) {
  proposal.value = value
  if (accept.value) {
    current.value = value
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <section class="multi-slides-demo">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="accept" edit-mode="direct">Accept changes / 接受切换</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="loop" edit-mode="direct">Loop / 循环</mp-checkbox>
    <p role="status">Current: {{ current }} · Proposal: {{ proposal }} · Changes: {{ changes }}</p>
    <mp-carousel
      class="carousel"
      :slides-per-view="2.5"
      :space-between="10"
      :model-value="current"
      :loop="loop"
      draggable
      keyboard
      @update:modelValue="update"
      @change="changes++"
    >
      <mp-carousel-item v-for="i in 6" :key="i">
        <div class="carousel-custom-slide">{{ i }}</div>
      </mp-carousel-item>
    </mp-carousel>
  </section>
</template>

<style lang="less" scoped>
.carousel {
  height: 160px;
}

.carousel-example {
  height: 160px;
}

.carousel-item {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.carousel-custom-slide {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background: #4a90d9;
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 24px;
  font-weight: bold;
}

.carousel-custom-indicators {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 10px;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  display: flex;
  gap: 4px;
}

.carousel-custom-indicator {
  width: 20px;
  height: 20px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
  color: #fff;
  font-size: 12px;
  border-radius: 50%;
}

  background: #4a90d9;

  height: 20px;

</style>
```

### auto-sized

Reverse cards reorders the same uniquely keyed cards (their distinct widths are the Demo keys). Current is positional, not a business-card identity: slide number 2 changes from 220px to 180px without changing the index or event count. Drag left to slide number 3, restore order to show 180px there, then drag right to slide number 2. Reordering alone emits no change. Arbitrary insertion/sorting, identity-following selection, reordering during a held gesture and physical touch remain unverified.

When the active fifth card is removed, parent Current stays 5 without another change; the view clamps it to the remaining fourth card and centers that card. A subsequent left drag wraps to 1 and updates the model once. Applications that need immediate parent-index correction must update current themselves. Arbitrary reordering and deletion during a held gesture remain unverified.

Empty temporarily removes every card: navigation is disabled and dragging emits no change. Turning it off restores the configured cards without switching. Clearing and restoring from slide number 1 allows a subsequent right drag to wrap to the last item. This does not cover nonzero out-of-range controlled indices or clearing during a held gesture.

Clearing from slide number 4 retains the parent Current and change count. Restoring centers the last card; the next left drag wraps to 1 and emits once. Empty content does not force the controlled parent value to 0. Active-card deletion, arbitrary invalid indices and clearing during a held gesture remain unverified.

Extra card appends a 200px fifth item without changing a valid current index or incrementing Changes. Drag right from the first item to reach it, then right again to the original last item before removing the extra card. The index and count stay unchanged; dragging left then wraps across the restored four-item boundary. This covers removing an inactive final item, not deleting the active item, arbitrary reordering, or changes during a held gesture.

Drag to the last item, then enable Wider cards (80px added per item) and the 300px viewport. Resizing does not change the model or increment Changes: the current 340px card recenters, and a left drag can wrap to the first item. Restoring both switches recenters again. This paragraph describes ResizeObserver updates after a completed gesture, not resizing while holding a drag.

Items have different widths. Dragging keeps the current item centered and can loop across either end. Current shows the accepted page index starting at 1; Changes counts change notifications.

Example source: src/carousel/example/demos/auto-sized.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const current = ref(1)
const changes = ref(0)
const wider = ref(false)
const compact = ref(false)
const extra = ref(false)
const empty = ref(false)
const reversed = ref(false)
const widths = computed(() => {
  const items = empty.value ? [] : [140, 220, 180, 260, ...(extra.value ? [200] : [])]
  return (reversed.value ? items.reverse() : items).map((width) => width + (wider.value ? 80 : 0))
})
</script>

<template>
  <section class="auto-sized-demo">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="wider" edit-mode="direct">Wider cards / 加宽卡片</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="compact" edit-mode="direct">300px viewport / 窄容器</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="extra" edit-mode="direct">Extra card / 增加末项</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="empty" edit-mode="direct">Empty / 清空项目</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="reversed" edit-mode="direct">Reverse cards / 反转顺序</mp-checkbox>
    <p role="status">Current: {{ current }} · Changes: {{ changes }}</p>
    <mp-carousel
      v-model="current"
      slides-per-view="auto"
      :space-between="12"
      height="180px"
      :style="{ width: compact ? '300px' : '100%' }"
      centered-slides
      draggable
      @change="changes++"
    >
      <mp-carousel-item v-for="width in widths" :key="width" :style="{ width: width + 'px' }">
        <div class="carousel-demo-panel">{{ width }}px</div>
      </mp-carousel-item>
    </mp-carousel>
  </section>
</template>
<style scoped>
.carousel-demo-panel {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  height: 100%;
  background: #e0e7ff;
  color: #312e81;
}
</style>
```

### Indicator style and position

All indicator presets use the same three local slides and active-slide model. Click an indicator or a navigation arrow in any specimen: every specimen changes to the same slide. The first group compares dot, line and slider; the second compares top and outer positions. The grid stacks on narrow screens.

<details>
<summary>Configuration details and limits</summary>

#### Indicator Types

Use `indicator-type` for `dot`, `line`, or `slider`. Hide indicators with `indicator`.

</details>

Example source: src/carousel/example/demos/indicator-comparison.vue


### Transition effects

Change adjacent slides to compare fade, card and slide effects independently of autoplay and input methods.

<details>
<summary>Configuration details and limits</summary>

#### Fade Effect

Use the indicator buttons to switch pages. Inactive slides become transparent and inert. All slides overlap in one grid cell, keeping the active slide at the viewport width rather than splitting the track into columns.

#### Card Effect

The active slide uses full scale and opacity; neighboring slides are scaled down and dimmed. Previous/next buttons retain native keyboard activation.

</details>

Example source: src/carousel/example/demos/effect-comparison.vue

## Playback and interaction

### Forbid Loop

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `height` | Container height; numbers are px | Autoplay, controlled, interactive-content |
| `keyboard` | Scoped arrow/Home/End navigation | Keyboard Control, controlled, interactive-content |
| `auto-play` | Autoplay configuration | Autoplay, Autoplay with Hover to Pause |
| `draggable` | Mouse dragging, independent of touch | controlled、interactive-content |
| `loop` | Loop without duplicating instances | Forbid Loop |
| `trigger` | Indicator trigger | Trigger with Hover |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->

### Autoplay

The demo uses a 2000ms interval. Displayed slide numbers start at 1; API indices remain one-based. Toggle playback off/on to stop/resume. Focus inside the carousel also pauses playback.

Enable autoplay with `auto-play`. `true` uses a 3000ms interval; a number is the interval in milliseconds.

Example source: src/carousel/example/demos/en-US/autoplay.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const current = ref(1)
const playing = ref(true)
const changes = ref(0)
const sources = ['cat.jpg', 'cat2.jpg', 'cat3.jpg']
</script>

<template>
  <section class="carousel-autoplay-demo">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="playing" edit-mode="direct">Autoplay</mp-checkbox>
    <p role="status">Current slide：{{ current }}；Changes：{{ changes }}</p>
    <mp-carousel
      v-model="current"
      height="180px"
      :auto-play="playing ? 2000 : false"
      @focusin="playing = false"
      @change="changes += 1"
    >
      <mp-carousel-item v-for="(source, index) in sources" :key="source">
        <img class="carousel-autoplay-demo__image" :src="source" :alt="'Demo image ' + (index + 1)" />
      </mp-carousel-item>
    </mp-carousel>
  </section>
</template>

<style scoped>
.carousel-autoplay-demo__image {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
  pointer-events: none;
}
</style>
```

### Mousewheel Control

Wheeling over the carousel changes slides without scrolling the outer page. With loop enabled, moving backward from the first slide selects the last. This is separate from touch dragging.

```vue
function update(value) {
  proposal.value = value
  if (accept.value) {
    current.value = value
  }
}
</script>
```

## Lifecycle

### Scheduler lifecycle

Changing content, restarting navigation or unmounting cancels pending slide movement. Autoplay timing is independent of CSS transitions.

Example source: src/carousel/example/demos/en-US/scheduler-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const active = ref(true)
const mounted = ref(true)
const current = ref(1)
const playing = ref(false)
const moves = ref(0)
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <mp-button @click="playing = !playing">Autoplay / 自动播放</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="active = !active">Activate / 停用与激活</mp-button>
    <mp-button @click="mounted = !mounted">Mount / 卸载与挂载</mp-button>
    <p>
      Current / 当前: {{ current }}; changes / 通知: {{ moves }}. Suspend during autoplay or loop settlement, then
      activate. Old work must not replay.
    </p>
    <KeepAlive v-if="mounted">
      <mp-carousel
        v-if="active"
        v-model="current"
        :auto-play="playing ? { interval: 1000 } : false"
        :move-speed="600"
        :height="180"
        keyboard
        mousewheel
        @change="moves++"
      >
        <mp-carousel-item v-for="item in 3" :key="item">Slide / 幻灯片 {{ item }}</mp-carousel-item>
      </mp-carousel>
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

### Intro

Displays a collection of items that can be scrolled and swiped. Demos match Cedar Design Web; `effect` and `centered-slides` are shared.

## Usage notes

### Looping and autoplay

Each slide always has one component instance. Ordinary previous/next navigation recycles positions after the departing slide exits. Multi-slide or centered jumps that would require one slide in two positions settle immediately without animation, cloning interactive content or queuing unlimited transitions. Fewer items than visible slides are not cloned to fill space. Accessible names follow global Locale; explicit label props take precedence.

Native root listeners such as `keydown`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`, `focusin` and `focusout` run alongside internal navigation and autoplay pause handling. Native `.once` listeners fire once for the root element lifetime.

`space-between` also accepts valid CSS lengths such as percentages and `calc()`. Multi-slide layout uses unscaled CSS pixels, so ancestor scaling does not change the gap-to-slide proportion.

If a focused slide becomes inaccessible through navigation or removal, focus moves to the carousel container. Focus in a still-visible slide or outside the carousel is preserved. The container is programmatically focusable but is not in the Tab order unless `keyboard` is enabled; an explicit `tabindex` remains under caller control.

The autoplay example sets `auto-play=false` on focus entry and provides an external switch for an explicit restart. The component itself only pauses temporarily while focus is inside; playback resumes on blur. This differs from the WAI-ARIA APG recommendation to stop on focus until the user explicitly restarts, and is not a claim of full APG conformance; applications requiring that behavior should control playback state. Reduced motion disables transitions but does not by itself stop automatic navigation.

Slide numbers start at 1; finite fractions are truncated toward zero and then wrapped or clamped according to `loop`. Finite `move-speed` values use non-negative milliseconds; non-finite values use the CSS transition duration. The root is a named region and default indicator buttons have localized slide names and current state; their container has no separate group name. `line` and `slider` share the same default bar dimensions; `slider` can grow into available container space and is not draggable.

## API

### Value and default value

Use ordinary `v-model`. `modelValue` is the current slide number, starting at 1. `defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled state only on creation; later changes do not reset it. An explicit bound value takes precedence. Initialization does not emit `update:modelValue`.

### Carousel Props

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
