### Model and interaction
Public slide numbers start at 1. Controlled actions emit update:model-value, then change(slideNumber, previousSlideNumber, isManual), and do not move until the parent accepts current. External assignments do not emit change. Method option event:false suppresses only change, not the model proposal. isManual is true for user actions and false for autoplay.

loop moves existing children across boundaries without cloning component instances. Without looping or centering, the final viewport is clamped to avoid empty space; selection can move within the final visible group without moving the track. Partly visible slides remain accessible; fully offscreen slides are inert. fade displays one slide. auto uses explicit CarouselItem width horizontally or height vertically; vertical mode requires a container height. Only CarouselItem children, including those inside Vue Fragments, count as slides; comments and ordinary elements do not.

auto-play=true uses 3000ms and pauses on hover; a number sets milliseconds without hover pausing; an object configures interval/hoverToPause. Focus within, dragging, hidden documents/ancestors and KeepAlive deactivation always pause playback. Reduced-motion preferences are respected. Interactive children such as inputs/buttons keep native behavior; mark custom interactive areas with data-carousel-no-drag. show-arrow=hover also shows arrows on keyboard focus.

### Carousel Events
| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| update:model-value | slideNumber: number |
| change | slideNumber: number, previousSlideNumber: number, isManual: boolean |

### Carousel Slots
| Slot | Prop |
| --- | --- |
| default | CarouselItem |
| prev / next / indicator | { slideNumber, length, hovering, prev, next, to, resize } |

### Carousel Methods
| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| prev / next | (options?: CarouselToOptions) => void |
| to | (slideNumber: number, options?: CarouselToOptions) => void |
| resize | () => void |

CarouselItem has no own props, events or methods. Its default slot supplies slide content.

<!-- Source: src/cascader/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/cascader -->

# Cascader

In multiple mode, the inline dropdown contains options only; the field owns selected values, removal and clearing. The popup editor retains the selected-items summary and clear action, and commits its draft on confirmation.

When cascading multiple selections, toggling a parent affects only selectable descendants; already selected disabled descendants are retained.

Clicking a checkbox only toggles selection; clicking the option label or expansion arrow opens the next level. Multiple selection uses the Checkbox component. In cascading mode, a parent displays the indeterminate state when some selectable descendants are selected.

## Reading direction

Inherits source dir. Child columns, expansion icons and separators follow reading direction. Horizontal keys enter loaded children or return to the parent in the visible direction, skipping disabled children; vertical keys retain logical order. Search preserves native horizontal caret editing. Path and multiple-value arrays are not reversed. Clearing the last value while closed resets navigation before reopening.

`empty-value` / `emptyValue` sets the model value produced by clearing. It accepts a value in the component model type or a zero-argument factory. Omission preserves the existing default; use `() => undefined` to distinguish omission from returning undefined. Arrays are shallow-copied on every clear; selected items that cannot be cleared remain. It does not redefine emptiness, alter Form reset defaults or treat 0/false as universally empty.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In confirmation mode, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model. Without confirmation, clearing commits directly.

The `options` prop accepts an array or `(query, { signal }) => array/Promise`. The component manages loading, cancellation and stale-result isolation; failures emit load-error. Single/multiple groups initialize with an empty-string query, searchable fields reload when the query changes, and root loading for tree fields remains independent of existing load-more child loading.

### Form control size comparison

Compare selected, clearable and nowrap multiple values with Input and Button. Long labels use ellipsis; removal icons stay available and the tag row scrolls horizontally without moving clear or arrow controls.

Example source: src/field-decorator/example/demos/control-sizes.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const sizes = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const
const variants = ['outline', 'filled', 'standard'] as const
const disabled = ref(false)
const readonly = ref(false)
const error = ref(false)
const size = ref<(typeof sizes)[number]>('md')
const variant = ref<(typeof variants)[number]>('outline')
const options = [
  { value: 'beijing', label: 'Beijing' },
  { value: 'shanghai', label: 'Shanghai' },
]
const cascaderOptions = [{ value: 'china', label: 'China', children: options }]

const inputValue = ref('Beijing')
const textareaValue = ref('Textarea value')
const selectValue = ref('beijing')
const cascaderValue = ref('beijing')
const selectMultiple = ref(['beijing', 'shanghai'])
const cascaderMultiple = ref(['beijing', 'shanghai'])
const selectOverflow = ref(['long', 'beijing', 'shanghai'])
const cascaderOverflow = ref(['long', 'beijing', 'shanghai'])
const selectedOptions = [
  ...options,
  {
    value: 'long',
    label:
      'A very long selected option label for overflow comparison — full text preview keeps the selected value unchanged.',
  },
]
const selectedCascaderOptions = [{ value: 'china', label: 'China', children: selectedOptions }]
```

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `path-mode` | Return a complete path instead of a node value | Multiple cascade, Picker multiple, List multiple |
| `placeholder` | Placeholder | Multiple cascade, Picker multiple, List multiple |
| `options` | Tree options; leaf values must be unique in scalar mode; paths distinguish branches | Multiple cascade, Picker multiple, List multiple |
| `multiple` | Multiple selection; enables search by default | Multiple cascade, Picker multiple, List multiple |
| `show-tags` | Show tags; false displays separated text | Multiple cascade, Picker multiple, List multiple |
| `edit-mode` | Field presentation; inherits FormItem / Form when omitted. | Picker multiple, List multiple |

### Presentation and commit rules

Inline commits immediately. Popup and dialog edit a draft for both single and multiple values. Confirm publishes once; cancel, overlay dismissal, Escape and presentation changes discard edits. External model replacements win over drafts. Search is inside the editor and keeps the existing filtering, search event and lazy loading API.

### Manage selected items

Multi-select panels include a selection summary and Clear. Cedar shows removable tags above list options. Maple opens selected-item details from the count row, with per-item removal and a way back to options. Popup/popover and dialog use the same behavior. Removal and Clear edit the draft; Cancel restores the value and Confirm publishes it. Disabled items remain selected, and confirmation locks selection actions. The panel Clear action is independent of the field clear icon.

### Panel data and customization

Compare panel options, selection and custom content. Select a node or clear the selection and inspect the displayed value; panel behavior is separate from the field opening protocol.

Example source: src/cascader/example/demos/panel-review.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import type { CascaderOption } from '../../types'

const value = ref<string | number | (string | number)[] | (string | number)[][]>()
const multiple = ref(false)
const pathMode = ref(false)
const empty = ref(false)
const loads = ref(0)
const options = computed(() =>
  empty.value
    ? []
    : [
        {
          value: 'frontend',
          label: '前端',
          children: [
            { value: 'vue', label: 'Vue', isLeaf: true },
            { value: 'react', label: 'React', isLeaf: true },
          ],
        },
        { value: 'backend', label: '后端', children: [{ value: 'node', label: 'Node.js', isLeaf: true }] },
        { value: 'lazy', label: '异步节点', isLeaf: false },
      ],
)
watch([multiple, pathMode], () => {
  value.value = multiple.value ? [] : undefined
})
function loadMore(option: CascaderOption, done: (children: CascaderOption[]) => void) {
  loads.value++
  done([{ value: `${option.value}-child`, label: '异步子节点', isLeaf: true }])
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-space>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="multiple">面板多选</mp-checkbox>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="pathMode">完整路径</mp-checkbox>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="empty">空数据</mp-checkbox>
      <mp-button @click="value = multiple ? [] : undefined">清空面板选择</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <mp-cascader-panel
      v-model="value"
      :options="options"
      :multiple="multiple"
      :path-mode="pathMode"
      :load-more="loadMore"
    >
      <template #empty><mp-tag>子面板空状态</mp-tag></template>
    </mp-cascader-panel>
    <p role="status">面板值：{{ JSON.stringify(value) }}；加载回调：{{ loads }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Configuration and composition

### Typed passthrough configuration

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `edit-mode` | Field presentation; inherits FormItem / Form when omitted. | Typed passthrough configuration, Copying and editing |
| `options` | Tree options; leaf values must be unique in scalar mode; paths distinguish branches | Typed passthrough configuration, Copying and editing |
| `trigger-props` | Menu Trigger props; field owns open state | Typed passthrough configuration |
| `open-trigger-target` | Pointer opening area: field includes the whole field; icon uses only the suffix trigger. Clear/remove actions are excluded; explicit keyboard opening and controlled open remain available. | Copying and editing |
| `filterable` | Enable search | Copying and editing |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Use `CascaderTriggerOptions` from `@maple-design/ui-vue` for opt-in boundary checking. Published wide prop types and runtime precedence remain unchanged. Visibility, disabled state and owned updates belong to the host. Top-level popupContainer wins when defined (including false), otherwise the existing nested fallback applies. Select/Cascader keep nested overrides for existing presentation defaults, including unmountOnClose. Date/DateRange filter owned state, rules and listeners; their interaction/offset settings and mobile unmountOnClose are fixed by the renderer.

Example source: src/cascader/example/demos/passthrough-options.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { CascaderTriggerOptions } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const open = ref(false)
const triggerOptions: CascaderTriggerOptions = { placement: 'top-start', popupOffset: 8, popupContainer: false }
const options = [{ value: 'fruit', label: '水果', children: [{ value: 'apple', label: 'Apple' }] }]
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" fill>
    <mp-button @click="open = !open">{{ open ? '关闭面板' : '打开面板' }}</mp-button>
    <mp-cascader
      v-model:open="open"
      edit-mode="direct"
      :options="options"
      :trigger-props="triggerOptions"
      aria-label="透传配置示例"
    />
    <p role="status">顶层 open：{{ open }}；嵌套配置：向上展开并调整偏移。</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Copying and editing

Use open-trigger-target to control pointer opening independently. In icon mode, clicking, focusing and typing do not automatically open the panel. input-editable / filterable still controls editing or search. The suffix button, explicit keyboard commands and controlled open can open it.

## Async loading and value resolution

### Callback lazy loading

Example source: src/cascader/example/demos/load-more.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, shallowRef } from 'vue'
import type { CascaderOption } from '../../types'

const roots = () => [{ value: 'root', label: 'Remote group', isLeaf: false }]
const options = ref<CascaderOption[]>(roots())
const requests = shallowRef<((children?: CascaderOption[]) => void)[]>([])
const stale = shallowRef<((children?: CascaderOption[]) => void)[]>([])
const status = ref('展开 Remote group 后选择返回结果 / Expand Remote group, then settle below')
const loadMore = (_option: CascaderOption, done: (children?: CascaderOption[]) => void) => {
  requests.value = [...requests.value, done]
}
function settle(success: boolean) {
  const callbacks = requests.value
  requests.value = []
  callbacks.forEach((done) => done(success ? [{ value: 'leaf', label: 'Loaded child', isLeaf: true }] : undefined))
  status.value = success
    ? '子项已返回 / Children received'
    : 'done() 结束等待，可重新展开重试 / Retry by expanding again'
}
function replace() {
  stale.value = [...stale.value, ...requests.value]
  requests.value = []
  options.value = roots()
  status.value = '已替换数据，旧回调失效 / Data replaced; old callbacks are invalid'
}
function settleOld() {
  stale.value.forEach((done) => done([{ value: 'stale', label: 'Stale child', isLeaf: true }]))
  stale.value = []
  status.value = '旧请求已返回，不应出现 Stale child / Old responses must not add Stale child'
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="lg">
    <mp-cascader
      :options="options"
      edit-mode="direct"
      :load-more="loadMore"
      placeholder="展开远程分组 / Expand remote group"
    />
    <mp-cascader-panel :options="options" :load-more="loadMore" />
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button :disabled="!requests.length" @click="settle(true)">返回子项 / Resolve</mp-button>
      <mp-button :disabled="!requests.length" @click="settle(false)">结束并重试 / Retry</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="replace">替换数据 / Replace data</mp-button>
      <mp-button :disabled="!stale.length" @click="settleOld">返回旧请求 / Resolve old</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p role="status">{{ status }}</p>
    <p>
      load-more 使用 done(children) 成功、done() 结束等待；返回值不作为子项。loadMore uses a callback; its return value
      does not supply children.
    </p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Async device labels

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| `edit-mode` | Field presentation; inherits FormItem / Form when omitted. | Async device labels |
| `options` | Tree options; leaf values must be unique in scalar mode; paths distinguish branches | Async device labels |
| `loading` | Loading state; blocks selection and confirmation | Async device labels |
| `path-mode` | Return a complete path instead of a node value | Async device labels |
| `filterable` | Enable search | Async device labels |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing; preserve disabled selections | Async device labels |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/cascader/example/demos/en-US/async-devices.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const editMode = ref<'direct' | 'popup'>('popup')
const value = ref(['factory', 'device-2'])
const options = ref<Record<string, unknown>[]>([])
const loading = ref(false)
async function load() {
  loading.value = true
  try {
    options.value = await Promise.resolve([
      {
        id: 'factory',
        name: 'Factory',
        nodes: [
          { id: 'device-1', name: 'Device one' },
          { id: 'device-2', name: 'Device two' },
          { id: 'device-3', name: 'Unavailable device', disabled: true },
        ],
      },
    ])
  } finally {
    loading.value = false
  }
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" align="stretch" :size="16">
    <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="Presentation">
      <mp-radio-group
        v-model="editMode"
        aria-label="Presentation"
        :style="{ width: '200px' }"
        :options="[
          { label: 'inline', value: 'inline' },
          { label: 'popup', value: 'popup' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </mp-form-item>
    <mp-button @click="load">Load device tree</mp-button>
    <mp-cascader
      v-model="value"
      :edit-mode="editMode"
      :options="options"
      :loading="loading"
      path-mode
      filterable
      clearable
      :field-names="{ label: 'name', value: 'id', children: 'nodes' }"
      placeholder="Choose a device path"
    />
    <p>Committed path: {{ value }}. Labels resolve automatically after the tree loads.</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Intro

Cascading selection via dropdown menu or bottom popup picker.

Single selection uses the built-in check icon on the right. Multiple selection uses Checkbox controls: no checked descendants is unchecked, some is indeterminate, and all selectable leaf descendants is checked. Disabled leaves are excluded from select-all. With checkStrictly, parent and child selections are independent. Selections in confirmation editors remain drafts until confirmation.

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

### Lazy-loading completion and errors

When an expandable option has unloaded children, Enter, Space, or the forward arrow starts lazy loading and displays its pending state. The forward arrow moves into children only if focus remains on the input or option that received the key. Search results do not expand children.

`loadMore(option, done)` keeps a callback-only contract in the field and standalone panel. Call `done(children)` to accept children or `done()` to end waiting and allow retry. Only the first callback is accepted; return values, including a resolved Promise, do not replace `done`. A synchronous loader exception releases waiting and reaches Vue's `errorCaptured` / application `errorHandler`. The `load-error` event remains specific to the `options` data source; it does not report `loadMore` exceptions. Handle asynchronous callback-based request failures in business code and call `done()`.

Replacing options (including nested mutations), field names, or the loader invalidates old work and cached lazy children. Unmount/deactivation invalidates pending callbacks; an old result cannot change a replacement node or clear a newer wait.

## Usage notes

### Editing mode
Use `edit-mode` to choose direct editing or a mobile editor panel.

### Editing and confirmation
This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `popup` and opens an editor when the value area is clicked. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open an editor through the field value trigger. Single selection commits on choice by default; need-confirm enables a draft and confirmation. Multiple selection defaults to confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards an uncommitted draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

`before-commit({ value, previousValue }, done, { signal })` can reject an overlay save. FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps the editor open on failure. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. Use `#read="{ value, text }"` to customize display. See the full field comparison in Form.

Field editing uses edit-mode: Cedar supports direct/click/dblclick, and Maple supports direct/popup. The old menu/list/picker editing values are not retained. Popup editors reuse the existing option index, search, asynchronous loading and virtual-list algorithms.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Search fields
`searchFields` / `search-fields` is a readonly `('label' | 'value')[]`, defaulting to `['label']`. Multiple fields use OR matching, case-insensitive by default. `['value', 'label']` searches codes and names; fieldNames maps semantic fields to business fields. An empty array matches no items for a nonempty query. Values are compared as strings; object traversal, object values and pinyin matching require a custom callback. A custom callback takes precedence and decides case handling itself. Remote results use the existing protocol for disabling local filtering. Cascader retains path semantics and checks the configured fields on each path node.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

Refresh can retry the component-owned asynchronous option source before the editor opens, using the existing AbortSignal, loading, and load-error protocol without opening the editor; static arrays do not create extra requests.

### Selection actions during loading
While manual loading or the current candidate request is active, selection fields preserve existing values and pause selection, clearing and tag removal. Blocked actions neither notify nor submit a model. Search text remains editable and disabled/readonly are not changed; set them separately to prevent searching.

Deferred editor clearing and confirmation are unavailable while loading; cancellation and closing remain available. Actions return to their normal state after both the manual flag and current request finish, still respecting disabled options. Loading on free-text fields such as Input and AutoComplete continues to allow text editing and clearing.

option({ data }) receives normalized CascaderOptionInfo; data.raw is the original option and data.path is the normalized root-to-current path. label({ data }) receives the field display item key/value/label/closable/tagProps. arrow-icon({ focus, menuOpen }) receives the real field focus and open state. read({ value, text }) retains null/undefined and the original model shape.

Public types include CascaderBaseValue, CascaderOptionInfo, CascaderReadScope, CascaderEmits, CascaderSlots and CascaderExpose from the root and cascader entry points. Standalone CascaderPanel accepts option arrays and does not own a root candidate loader.

## API

In direct mode, the hierarchical popup is a named dialog containing column menus. The root menu uses the localized selection prompt. Each submenu is named after its full parent path, including when its parent row scrolls out of the virtual window. With the popup open and the input focused, press ArrowDown to enter an enabled menu item, then use the arrow keys to navigate the hierarchy. A panel branch's `aria-expanded` reflects whether its child column is actually displayed; focus or hover alone does not mark it expanded. Leaves have no `aria-expanded`. Selectable leaves and selectable strict-mode branches in a single-select hierarchical menu use `menuitemradio` and `aria-checked`; expansion-only branches remain `menuitem`, and selectable items in a multiple-select hierarchy expose unchecked, checked, or mixed state. Tab enters or leaves the menu, arrow keys move focus, and Space toggles selection. Clicking the checkbox also toggles selection. Custom slot controls retain their own tab stops. Single-select hierarchical panels have one Tab entry; arrow keys move between columns and options, while Tab or Shift+Tab leaves the menu. With virtualization, the entry remains among rendered options; custom interactive controls in option slots manage their own focus. Search results do not declare hidden submenus. Direct single-select search uses `listbox` and `option`, with the input referencing the popup and active item; editor single-select search uses `menuitemradio` and `aria-checked`, with one Tab entry. Hovering another option does not move that entry while an option owns focus. Multiple-select search retains checkboxes. Direct multiple-select search uses a named dialog by default; ArrowDown from the open input focuses the first enabled checkbox, and Space toggles it. Explicit popup roles or external relationships remain caller-controlled. After hydration, same-root popups use ID references. Browsers with ARIA element reflection can also associate the input with a popup in an ancestor root (such as the document body) and its active single-select option. For sibling or descendant shadow roots, render the popup in the input’s root to establish the relationship. On the server, inline popups receive automatic ID references. For teleported popups, the component determines the available relationship after hydration. For direct single- or multiple-select search inside Shadow DOM, set `:popup-container="false"` to render the popup inline in the same root as the input, allowing the automatic `aria-controls` relationship and, for single selection, `aria-activedescendant`. Inline rendering can be affected by ancestor clipping and stacking; verify the actual layout and test with assistive technology. In multiple-select editor search, ArrowDown in the search input focuses the first enabled result checkbox; focus stays in the input if none is available. In direct single-select search, the popup icon adds no Tab stop; click it or press ArrowDown in the input to open.

When options are added or removed at the end of a virtual column, options still within the rendered range retain their nodes and focus. Switching parents does not reuse the previous column's scroll position. Options can unmount when removed or outside the virtual window; business code should retain any long-lived input state used by slots.

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Cascader Props

Use `v-model`, `v-model:open` and `v-model:input-value` for controlled state. Clear values are `''` for single selection and `[]` for multiple selection. Select uses `undefined` when an actual empty-string option exists.

### Cascader Events / Methods

In direct mode, Arrow Down requests opening when the field is closed. Once opened, the first enabled option becomes active if no option is already active and focus remains in the field, including when options arrive asynchronously. Losing focus, closing, or interacting again cancels the pending activation. A controlled `open` changes only when the parent accepts the request.

When a menu option has focus, Enter or Space activates it. Search inputs and nested checkboxes keep their own keyboard behavior. In a multiple-selection editor, search results form a named group; Tab reaches each checkbox and Space or Enter toggles it.

- `keydown(event)`: keyboard event from the field, candidate menu, or editor panel; `preventDefault()` suppresses internal keyboard handling.

- `update:modelValue`, `change(value)`: emitted on commit, not while editing a draft.
- `update:open`, `open-change(open)`: request an expanded-state change.
- `update:inputValue`, `input-value-change(text)`, `search(text)`: search state.
- `focus(event)`, `blur(event)`, `clear(event)`: native field events; only the field owner notifies Form.
- `load-error(error)`: current options source failure notification; listener Promises are not collected.
- Methods: `focus()`, `blur()` and `refresh(): Promise<void>`; refresh does not open the editor.

### Slots and option data

Use `label({ data })` for custom `selected` labels; `selected` replaces the whole selection area. Also supports `prefix`, `suffix`, `clear-icon({ clear })`, `arrow-icon`, `loading-icon`, `search-icon`, `empty`, and `option({ data })`.

Option `label` is searchable plain text. Use `render` or the `option` slot for custom `option` content, and `format-label` or `label` slot for selected content. Values identify selections; labels never do. `disabled` blocks selection/removal, and `tagProps` customizes selected tags.

Buttons, links, input controls, list options, tree nodes, grid cells, elements with non-negative tabindex, audio/video with controls and nested Cascaders inside custom options manage their own clicks without selecting the outer option; ordinary content remains selectable. When `role` contains multiple tokens, the first role supported by the component determines click ownership. A standalone panel inside Shadow DOM moves option focus within its own root when using arrow keys. A click canceled with `preventDefault` does not trigger an option action, and continues to bubble according to DOM rules.

`CascaderPanel` (`mp-cascader-panel`), also `Cascader.CascaderPanel`, works independently as a Menu panel without input/popup. Supports options, modelValue/defaultValue, multiple, pathMode, checkStrictly, fieldNames, loadMore, disabled, expandTrigger and expandChild. Events are update:modelValue/change; empty customizes empty state.

### CascaderPanel Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------: |
| path-mode | Return a complete path instead of a node value | `boolean` | `false` |
| multiple | Multiple selection; enables search by default | `boolean` | `false` |
| model-value **(v-model)** | Bound value | `string\| number\| Record<string, any>\| (    \| string    \| number    \| Record<string, any>    \| (string \| number \| Record<string, any>)[]  )[]\| undefined` | `-` |
| default-value | Default value (uncontrolled state) | `string\| number\| Record<string, any>\| (    \| string    \| number    \| Record<string, any>    \| (string \| number \| Record<string, any>)[]  )[]\| undefined` | `'' \| undefined \| []` |
| options | Tree options; leaf values must be unique in scalar mode; paths distinguish branches | `CascaderOption[]` | `[]` |
| expand-trigger | Menu / List expansion: click or hover | `string` | `'click'` |
| check-strictly | Allow parent selection; unlink parent/child checks | `boolean` | `false` |
| load-more | Load children asynchronously; call done(children), or done() to allow retry | `(  option: CascaderOption,  done: (children?: CascaderOption[]) => void) => void` | `-` |
| field-names | Customize fields in `CascaderOption`; when option `value` is an object, `value` is also used as the key property | `CascaderFieldNames` | `-` |
| expand-child | Expand to first child | `boolean` | `false` |

### CascaderPanel Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------ | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| change | Emitted when the selected value changes | value: `string \| number \| (string \| number \| (string \| number)[])[] \| undefined` |

### CascaderPanel Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------ | :------------------: | ---- |
| empty | Content displayed when no options are available | - |

Async search should clear old candidates when requests start and accept only the latest current-query response. `update:input-value` can react immediately; `loading` and `filter-option` can display remote results. Popup arrows/Enter operate current candidates; confirmation mode saves with the bottom button, while immediate single selection commits on choice. Validation failure in confirmation mode preserves drafts, confirmation locks editing/closing, and Form reset closes Popup and aborts submission. Closing/reset invalidates request ownership. See Form’s unified field-presentation examples.

Follow-up acceptance testing (not yet completed): use real screen readers, such as VoiceOver and NVDA, with supported browsers to verify spoken field names, hierarchical navigation and expansion state, search and selection, single and multiple selection, virtual lists, and form errors.

# Cell

### Intro

The cell is a single display item in the list. `title` renders the main text; the default slot overrides it when provided.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/cell/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-cell title="这是单元格" />
  <mp-cell title="标题会被默认插槽覆盖">自定义单元格内容</mp-cell>
</template>
```

## Content and presentation

### Icons, descriptions and dividers

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `border` | Whether to show border | Icons, descriptions and dividers, Use As List Item |
| `title` | Main title; overridden by the default slot | Icons, descriptions and dividers |
| `description` | Cell description | Icons, descriptions and dividers |
| `ripple` | Whether to enable the water wave effect | Use As List Item |
| `border-offset` | Border offset | Use As List Item |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Compare leading icons, supplementary descriptions and row separators according to information hierarchy.

<details>
<summary>Configuration details and limits</summary>

#### Show Icon

The examples render `<m-icon-fire />` in the `#icon` slot. The Resolver imports it on demand without manual imports or registration. The string API `icon="fire"` only resolves icons already registered in the app; string values do not trigger the Resolver.

#### Show Description

The leading icon, title/description text block, and trailing content are vertically centered. Cell manages spacing and alignment for the icon slot; place the icon directly in the slot without internal CSS classes.

</details>

### Use As List Item

Example source: src/cell/example/demos/list.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const items = ref([
  {
    name: 'Vue2',
    icon: 'star-fill',
    enabled: false,
  },
  {
    name: 'Vue3',
    icon: 'heart-fill',
    enabled: false,
  },
  {
    name: 'React',
    icon: 'close-circle-fill',
    enabled: false,
  },
])
const handleClick = (item) => {
  item.enabled = !item.enabled
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-paper :elevation="2">
    <mp-cell
      v-for="(item, index) in items"
      :key="item.name"
      ripple
      :action-aria-label="`查看${item.name}`"
      :border="index !== items.length - 1"
      :border-offset="0"
      @click="handleClick(item)"
    >
      {{ item.name }}

      <template #icon>
        <m-icon-star-fill v-if="item.icon === 'star-fill'" />
        <m-icon-heart-fill v-else-if="item.icon === 'heart-fill'" />
        <m-icon-close-circle-fill v-else />
      </template>

      <template #extra>
        <mp-switch v-model="item.enabled" @click.stop />
      </template>
    </mp-cell>
  </mp-paper>
</template>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Icons, labels, values and extra content follow reading order, with logical start/end spacing. Explicit device safe-area and physical-position contracts do not reverse.

## API

`clickable` gives the main content button semantics, focus and Enter/Space activation. When omitted it follows `ripple`; explicit false omits the main action semantics. Use `action-aria-label` when the content does not name the action. `extra` is separate and can contain independent controls; their clicks bubble by default, so use `.stop` for independent actions. Do not nest interactive controls in the main content of an actionable cell. `title-class` and `description-class` affect only their default nodes; slot content owns its styles. Numeric `border-offset` must be finite; negative values and zero are valid, while invalid numbers use default spacing.

### Cell Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----- | -------------- | -------- | ---------- |
| `title` | Main title; overridden by the default slot | _string_ | `-` |
| `icon` | Registered left-icon name | _string_ | `-` |
| `description` | Cell description | _string_ | `-` |
| `border` | Whether to show border | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `border-offset` | Border offset | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `icon-class` | Extra class for the leading icon container, for both the icon prop and slot | _string_ | `-` |
| `title-class` | Title className | _string_ | `-` |
| `description-class` | Description className | _string_ | `-` |
| `extra-class` | Extra className | _string_ | `-` |
| `ripple` | Whether to enable the water wave effect | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `clickable` | Enable the main action; follows ripple when omitted | `boolean` | `—` |
| `action-aria-label` | Accessible name of the main action | `string` | `—` |

### Cell Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | Triggered when the cell is clicked | `event: Event` |

### Cell Slots

| Name | Description | Prop |
| ----- | -------------- | -------- |
| `default` | Main content; overrides title | `-` |
| `icon` | Custom left-icon area | `-` |
| `description` | Description content | `-` |
| `extra` | Extra of cell | `-` |

# Checkbox

Standalone Checkbox modelValue is a boolean checked state, or an array of selected option values in array mode. The value prop identifies this option; it is not the checked state. CheckboxGroup modelValue is the selected values array. defaultValue initializes uncontrolled state only and does not write into the parent.

### Intro

Basic demos follow the site language without changing business values or selection. Group demos cover accepted/rejected updates, readonly state and asynchronous option labels; removing options does not clear the model. Use `direction="column"` on the outer Space and `orientation="vertical"` on the choice group itself.

A group of options for multiple choices.

## Reading direction

Checkbox labels and groups follow source dir without reversing value arrays. Space keeps its toggle meaning; disabled and readonly behavior remains effective. Changing direction does not select or clear options.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/checkbox/example/demos/en-US/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive, toRefs } from 'vue'

const values = reactive({
  value: false,
  value2: false,
  value3: false,
  value4: false,
  value5: false,
  value6: [],
  value9: [],
  value10: false,
  value11: [],
  group: null,
  indeterminate: true,
  optionsValue: [],
  fieldValue: [],
})

  value,
  value2,
  value3,
  value4,
  value5,
  value6,
  value9,
  group,
  value10,
  value11,
  indeterminate,
  optionsValue,
  fieldValue,
} = toRefs(values)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-checkbox v-model="value">Current value: {{ value }}</mp-checkbox>
```

### Group state and readonly

A defined `model-value` is controlled: rejected updates do not change the selection. `default-value` initializes uncontrolled state only. Only Group emits `update:model-value → change(value, event?)` and notifies FormItem once; children do not duplicate these notifications.
Group inherits `disabled`, `readonly` and `error` from the form when omitted. An explicit `false` overrides the form; children cannot bypass a locked group.

Example source: src/checkbox/example/demos/en-US/group-state.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const accepted = ref(['a'])
const proposed = ref([])
const readonly = ref(false)
const options = [
  { label: 'Device A', value: 'a' },
  { label: 'Device B', value: 'b' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <div>
      <p>Uncontrolled: default-value initializes only</p>
      <mp-checkbox-group :default-value="['a']" :options="options" />
    </div>
    <div>
      <p>Controlled: parent accepts updates {{ accepted }}</p>
      <mp-checkbox-group v-model="accepted" :options="options" :readonly="readonly" />
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="readonly = !readonly">{{ readonly ? 'Unlock' : 'Read only' }}</mp-button>
    </div>
    <div>
      <p>Parent rejects updates; proposals only {{ proposed }}</p>
      <mp-checkbox-group :model-value="[]" :options="options" @update:model-value="proposed = $event" />
    </div>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Options and value model

### Standalone values and methods

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `value` | Option identity | Standalone values and methods, Set State Value |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value | Standalone values and methods |
| `readonly` | Readonly; inherits Form when omitted | Standalone values and methods |
| `disabled` | Disabled; inherits Form when omitted | Standalone values and methods |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Checkbox boolean models emit booleans. Array models add/remove the option value without mutating the input array. indeterminate is presentation-only and must be derived by the application.
Use `default-value` only to initialize uncontrolled state. Rejected controlled proposals preserve the current selection. The event order is `update:model-value → change(value, event?)`; imperative calls have no native event.
Methods are `toggle(checked?: boolean)`, `focus(options?)` and `blur()`. Disabled controls cannot select or focus; readonly controls can focus but cannot change value. Enter on keydown and Space on keyup activate only the local control. Repeated Enter is ignored; blur/deactivation cancels pending Space activation.

Example source: src/checkbox/example/demos/en-US/control-value.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const control = ref()
const value = ref(false)
const selected = ref([0])
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>Boolean models emit booleans; array models use value as the option ID. Current value:{{ value }}</p>
    <mp-checkbox ref="control" v-model="value">Enable notifications</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="control?.toggle()">Toggle selection</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="control?.focus()">Focus</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="value = false">Reset</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p>Array model:{{ selected }}</p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="selected" :value="0">Number 0</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="selected" :value="false">Boolean false</mp-checkbox>
    <p>
      Read-only controls can receive focus; disabled controls cannot be edited. Enter/Space activates only this control.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox :default-value="true" readonly>Read only</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox :default-value="true" disabled>Disabled</mp-checkbox>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Option data and labels

Both libraries accept primitive options or objects. `field-names` maps `label/value/disabled/readonly/indeterminate`; read-only options remain focusable but cannot change the value. Checkbox indeterminate is presentation only.
The `label` slot receives `{ data, checked }` and takes precedence over a label render function `(data, checked) => VNodeChild`. Data is normalized and retains business fields; source objects are not mutated. Missing labels fall back to the value's text.
Providing `options` replaces the default slot, including `[]`; omit it to use the default slot. Values must be strings, finite numbers or booleans; missing/invalid values and duplicate values of the same type are skipped (first occurrence wins). `false`, `0`, `''` and `'0'` remain distinct. Option changes never rewrite the model.
CheckboxGroup uses `ChoiceValue[]`; `max` is a number (use `:max="2"`).

Example source: src/checkbox/example/demos/en-US/option-data.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { h, ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref<Array<string | number | boolean>>(['locked'])
const fields = { value: 'id', label: 'name', disabled: 'unavailable', readonly: 'locked' }
const options = ref([
  { id: false, name: 'Boolean false' },
  { id: 0, name: 'Number zero' },
  { id: '', name: 'Empty string' },
  { id: 'locked', name: 'Read-only option', locked: true },
  { id: 'disabled', name: 'Disabled option', unavailable: true },
])
const renderOptions = [
  {
    value: 'render',
    label: (_data: unknown, checked: boolean) => h('strong', checked ? 'Selected' : 'Rendered label'),
  },
]
</script>

  <section class="option-demo">
    <p>Field mapping and label slots. Read-only options can receive focus; disabled options cannot be edited.</p>
    <mp-checkbox-group v-model="value" :options="options" :field-names="fields" orientation="vertical">
      <template #label="{ data, checked }">{{ data.label }} {{ checked ? '✓' : '' }}</template>
    </mp-checkbox-group>
    <p>Current value: {{ JSON.stringify(value) }}</p>
    <mp-button @click="value = []">Clear</mp-button>
    <p>
      Labels also support render functions. Omitting options uses the default slot; passing [] renders an empty group.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox-group :options="renderOptions" />
  </section>
</template>

}
```

### Group bulk methods

Both libraries expose `checkAll()` and `inverseAll()`, returning a detached array. They operate on mounted, editable children only and preserve selected disabled, read-only or unloaded values. A duplicate value is locked if any child with that value is locked.
`checkAll` preserves the existing model order and appends missing values in current DOM order; `inverseAll` removes editable selected values before adding previously unselected values. Both enforce `max` without pruning external over-limit values.
Controlled groups return proposals and require parent updates; rejected proposals are not saved. Disabled/read-only groups return a copy of the current value. Actual changes notify `update:model-value → change(value, undefined) → FormItem` once; no-op calls stay silent.
Reordering, mounting, unmounting and KeepAlive activation are read correctly; call methods after `nextTick` when the rendered children change.

Example source: src/checkbox/example/demos/en-US/group-methods.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { CheckboxGroupInstance } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const group = ref<CheckboxGroupInstance>()
const value = ref<Array<string | number | boolean>>(['remote', 'locked', 'a'])
const reverse = ref(false)
const proposal = ref<Array<string | number | boolean>>([])
const options = [
  { value: 'a', label: 'Task A' },
  { value: 'b', label: 'Task B' },
  { value: 'c', label: 'Task C' },
  { value: 'locked', label: 'Read-only, selection preserved', readonly: true },
  { value: 'disabled', label: 'Disabled, excluded from bulk changes', disabled: true },
]
</script>

<template>
  <section class="group-methods-demo">
    <p>
      Select up to 4 values, including the unloaded remote value. Bulk operations preserve read-only and unloaded
      selections.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox-group
      ref="group"
      v-model="value"
      :options="reverse ? [...options].reverse() : options"
      :max="4"
      orientation="vertical"
    />
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="proposal = group?.checkAll() ?? []">Check all</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="proposal = group?.inverseAll() ?? []">Invert</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="reverse = !reverse">Reverse option order</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p>Current value: {{ JSON.stringify(value) }}</p>
    <p>Returned proposal: {{ JSON.stringify(proposal) }}</p>
  </section>
</template>

<style scoped>
.group-methods-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 12px;
}
.group-methods-demo p {
  margin: 0;
}
</style>
```

## Control and slot customization

### Native controls and appearance

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `unchecked-color` | Unchecked color | Modify The Icon And Color, Custom control slot |
| `checked-color` | Checked color | Modify The Icon And Color, Custom control slot |
| `name` | Native input name within the group | Native controls and appearance |
| `indeterminate` | Indeterminate state; highest style precedence | Native controls and appearance |
| `aria-label` | Accessible group name | Native controls and appearance |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value | Native controls and appearance |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Both libraries use independently copied native checkbox and label bodies. Tab focuses, Space/Enter toggles. A readonly control stays focusable; a disabled control is not focusable. The native input exposes the mixed state through its `indeterminate` property after hydration; the component manages the native checked state and ignores a supplied `aria-checked`. The server-rendered first view cannot guarantee that assistive technologies receive the mixed state. A label click triggers one activation. Use aria-label when no visible label is supplied; name is forwarded to native inputs and inherited from the group.

The icon-size prop is a pixel number or CSS length string, not a ComponentSize preset. The default control size is 14px in Cedar and 24px in Maple. Instance colors apply to ordinary states; error and disabled colors take precedence. The checkbox slot overrides the whole visual control (including the group's checkbox slot), while checked-icon, unchecked-icon and indeterminate-icon replace only each icon. These slots are decorative: do not put independent focusable controls inside them.

## Async options

### Asynchronous options

Enable manual responses to create local Promises and resolve the oldest or newest load in either order. The demo loader uses a version guard: obsolete responses cannot finish a newer load, clear selections, release a `max=2` slot, or increment user changes. Removing options invalidates in-flight results; a fresh load reflects the retained model. Deactivation or unmount settles waiting jobs and cancels timers. This is demo business logic, not automatic network-race handling by the component; no external service is used.

Loading/removing options or updating the external value never emits reverse updates. Selected values absent from the current options are retained. This demo simulates a request with an 800ms local delay; removing options while loading cancels the pending result so stale options do not reappear. The selected remote value occupies one slot; selecting Device A reaches `max=2` and disables Device B. Deselecting either item frees a slot. External over-limit values are not truncated.

Use Space or Enter on existing options while waiting. Reloading the same values preserves keyboard focus and the latest selection. Keep the loading-status node stable to avoid remounting the group; deselecting an item still frees a slot for another choice.

Example source: src/checkbox/example/demos/en-US/async-options.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { onDeactivated, onUnmounted, ref, shallowRef } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['remote'])
const options = ref([])
const loading = ref(false)
let pendingTimer
const manual = ref(false)
const waiting = shallowRef([])
const applied = ref(0)
const ignored = ref(0)
const changeCount = ref(0)
let version = 0
let sequence = 0

function cancelPending() {
  version++
  if (pendingTimer !== undefined) {
    clearTimeout(pendingTimer)
  }
  pendingTimer = undefined
  loading.value = false
}

function load() {
  cancelPending()
  loading.value = true
  const ticket = version
  const id = ++sequence
  const complete = () => {
    if (ticket !== version) {
      ignored.value++
      return
    }
    applied.value = id
    options.value = [
      { label: 'Remote device', value: 'remote' },
      { label: 'Device A', value: 'a' },
      { label: 'Device B', value: 'b' },
      { label: 'Disabled device', value: 'locked', disabled: true },
    ]
    pendingTimer = undefined
    loading.value = false
  }
  if (manual.value) {
    new Promise((resolve) => {
      waiting.value = [...waiting.value, { id, resolve }]
    }).then(complete)
  } else {
    pendingTimer = setTimeout(complete, 800)
  }
}

function settle(latest) {
  const jobs = [...waiting.value]
  const job = latest ? jobs.pop() : jobs.shift()
  waiting.value = jobs
  job?.resolve()
}

function cleanup() {
  cancelPending()
  const jobs = waiting.value
  waiting.value = []
  jobs.forEach((job) => job.resolve())
}

function remove() {
  cancelPending()
  options.value = []
}

onDeactivated(cleanup)
onUnmounted(cleanup)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space class="checkbox-async-demo" direction="column">
    <p>Values survive loading and removing options:{{ value }}</p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="manual" @change="remove">Manual responses / 手动返回</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="load">Load options</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="remove">Remove options</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" :disabled="waiting.length === 0" @click="settle(false)">Resolve oldest load</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" :disabled="waiting.length === 0" @click="settle(true)">Resolve newest load</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p aria-live="polite">
      {{
        loading
          ? 'Loading. Remove the options before completion to cancel this request.'
          : 'Loading preserves the current selection and keyboard focus.'
      }}
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox-group v-model="value" :options="options" :max="2" @change="changeCount++" />
    <p>User changes：{{ changeCount }}</p>
    <p role="status">Applied: {{ applied }} · Ignored: {{ ignored }} · Pending: {{ waiting.length }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Native input attributes and keyboard cancellation

Native `id`, `form`, `required`, constraints, aria/data attributes and keyboard listeners belong to the actual input. Class/`style` and other shell attributes remain on the label. Generated native IDs are stable and unique, and an external label can target an explicit `id`. HTML `required` participates in native browser `form` validation, separately from Form business rules.

Once / Capture / Passive native listener modifiers stay on the input rather than firing from interactive slot children. Native preventDefault can veto Enter / Space activation and RadioGroup arrow navigation; canceled Space leaves no delayed release action. Checked, disabled, input type and group Tab navigation remain component-managed.

The nullable Checkbox model is preserved. checked in default / checkbox slots is always boolean, with null shown as false; rendering alone never proposes a new model.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

The `options` prop accepts an array or `(query, { signal }) => array/Promise`. The component manages loading, cancellation and stale-result isolation; failures emit load-error. Single/multiple groups initialize with an empty-string query, searchable fields reload when the query changes, and root loading for tree fields remains independent of existing load-more child loading.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

CheckboxGroup checkAll/inverseAll change values only through an active editor. When a deferred editor is closed, deactivated, or unmounted, calls return an independent array copy of the current business value without opening the editor or publishing model changes.

## API

### Parameters, presentation clearing and mount-time boundaries

orientation accepts horizontal / vertical and falls back to horizontal after invalid-value diagnostics. max belongs to CheckboxGroup: valid values are finite nonnegative integers, zero forbids new choices, and omission is unlimited. Existing external values are never truncated. Invalid JavaScript callers retain the existing normalization after diagnostics: negatives become zero, fractions are floored, NaN is unlimited, and Infinity remains unlimited.

icon-size accepts positive lengths. Numbers and numeric strings use px, including positive fractions such as 0.5. Invalid, nonpositive or nonfinite values diagnose and fall back to the theme; the Divider minimum of 1 does not apply. Business styles determine the final resolved value of CSS expressions.

uninject-group-context decides group participation at mount. Changing it later does not reinject; change the key or remount. An isolated control still participates in Form. clearable / empty-value apply only to explicit presentation-layer clearing; native unchecking still proposes false or removes the array value and never uses empty-value. Ordinary event Promises do not participate in waiting; before-commit uses payload / done / context only when saving a deferred edit.

During an explicit options request both group roots announce aria-busy and emit one load-error on failure. No loading prop or extra graphic is added, and loading/failure never proposes a new model.

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

`ChoiceValue = string | number | boolean`；`CheckboxModel = boolean | ChoiceValue[] | null`；`RadioModel = ChoiceValue | null`。

### Checkbox Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------- |
| model-value (v-model) | Controlled value | CheckboxModel | undefined |
| default-value | Initial uncontrolled value | CheckboxModel | false |
| value | Option identifier in array/group mode | string\|number\|boolean | true |
| disabled | Disabled state; inherits from the form/group when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| readonly | Readonly state; inherits from the form/group when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| error | Error state; inherits from the form/group when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| indeterminate | Whether to display an indeterminate state | boolean | false |
| checked-color | Instance checked color; error/disabled states take precedence | string | undefined |
| unchecked-color | Instance unchecked color; error/disabled states take precedence | string | undefined |
| icon-size | Positive length; invalid values diagnose and fall back to the theme | number \| string | undefined |
| ripple | Whether to enable ripple feedback | boolean | true |
| uninject-group-context | Ignore surrounding CheckboxGroup; form state still applies | boolean | false |
| name | Native field name; inherits from Group when omitted | string | undefined |
| aria-label | Accessible name when no visible label exists | string | undefined |
| edit-mode | Editing mode, inherited from FormItem and Form | `'direct' \| 'popup'` | `'direct'` |
| read-pretty | Independent read presentation; explicit false overrides the parent | `boolean` | `false` |
| clearable | Deferred editor clearing; does not change native deselection | `boolean` | `false` |
| empty-value | Explicit presentation clear output; does not control native unchecking | `CheckboxModel \| (() => CheckboxModel)` | `false` |
| empty-values | Empty-value recognition; field takes precedence over FormItem and Form | `readonly unknown[]` | `-` |
| empty-text | Read empty text; an explicit empty string is valid | `string` | `'-'` |
| before-commit | Guard before saving a deferred edit; return a boolean or Promise, or complete via done | `(payload: { value: unknown; previousValue: unknown }, done: (allow?: boolean) => void, context: { signal: AbortSignal; event?: Event }) => void \| boolean \| Promise<void \| boolean>` | `-` |
| open | Controlled editor visibility, separate from native input focus | `boolean` | `-` |
| default-open | Initial visibility of an uncontrolled editor | `boolean` | `false` |
| popup-container | Editor mount container | `string \| HTMLElement \| false` | `-` |

### CheckboxGroup Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| model-value (v-model) | Controlled value | ChoiceValue[] \| null | undefined |
| default-value | Initial uncontrolled value | ChoiceValue[] | [] |
| max | Maximum selection count | number | undefined |
| options | Options; replaces default slot when supplied | Array<ChoiceValue \| CheckboxOption \| Record<string, unknown>> / `(query, { signal }) => Array / Promise` | `undefined` |
| orientation | Horizontal/vertical arrangement of checkbox-group options, default horizontal; not text reading direction | Orientation<br>`'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | 'horizontal' |
| disabled | Disabled state; inherits from the form/group when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| readonly | Readonly state; inherits from the form/group when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| error | Error state; inherits from the form/group when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| field-names | Option field mapping | ChoiceFieldNames | undefined |
| name | Native input name within the group | string | undefined |
| aria-label | Accessible group name | string | undefined |
| edit-mode | Editing mode, inherited from FormItem and Form | `'direct' \| 'popup'` | `'direct'` |
| read-pretty | Independent read presentation; explicit false overrides the parent | `boolean` | `false` |
| clearable | Deferred editor clearing; does not change native deselection | `boolean` | `false` |
| empty-value | Explicit presentation clear output; does not control native unchecking | `ChoiceValue[] \| null \| (() => ChoiceValue[] \| null)` | `[]` |
| empty-values | Empty-value recognition; field takes precedence over FormItem and Form | `readonly unknown[]` | `-` |
| empty-text | Read empty text; an explicit empty string is valid | `string` | `'-'` |
| before-commit | Guard before saving a deferred edit; return a boolean or Promise, or complete via done | `(payload: { value: unknown; previousValue: unknown }, done: (allow?: boolean) => void, context: { signal: AbortSignal; event?: Event }) => void \| boolean \| Promise<void \| boolean>` | `-` |
| open | Controlled editor visibility, separate from native input focus | `boolean` | `-` |
| default-open | Initial visibility of an uncontrolled editor | `boolean` | `false` |
| popup-container | Editor mount container | `string \| HTMLElement \| false` | `-` |

| ------ | --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------ |

| focus | Focus the control | options?: FocusOptions | void |
| blur | Blur the control | - | void |

| Method | Arguments | Returns |
| ---------- | ---- | ------------- |
| checkAll | - | ChoiceValue[] |
| inverseAll | - | ChoiceValue[] |

| ------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- |

| focus | Focus | event: FocusEvent |
| blur | Blur | event: FocusEvent |

| load-error | Explicit option loading failed; does not change the model | error: unknown |

`{ label?: string; value?: string; disabled?: string; readonly?: string; indeterminate?: string }`

## CSS Variables

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-checkbox-action-padding` | `6px` | `padding` |
| `--mp-checkbox-animation-duration` | `var(--mp-sys-motion-duration-standard)` | `transition` |
| `--mp-checkbox-control-border-radius` | `2px` | `border-radius` |
| `--mp-checkbox-control-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-border-default)` | `color` |
| `--mp-checkbox-control-color-checked` | `var(--mp-sys-color-action-primary)` | `color` |
| `--mp-checkbox-control-color-disabled` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-disabled)` | `color` |
| `--mp-checkbox-control-color-error` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-danger)` | `color` |
| `--mp-checkbox-control-size` | `24px` | `height`, `width` |
| `--mp-checkbox-group-gap` | `0` | `gap` |
| `--mp-checkbox-label-font-size` | `var(--mp-font-size-md)` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-checkbox-label-gap` | `0` | `margin-inline-start` |
| `--mp-checkbox-label-text-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-primary)` | `color` |
| `--mp-checkbox-label-text-color-disabled` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-disabled)` | `color` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-checkbox-action-padding: 6px;
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

### Reduced motion

Built-in CSS transitions follow `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Removing transitions does not change final visibility, selected/expanded state or event semantics. Applications control custom animations inside slots.

# Components Library Tools

### Intro

The out-of-the-box `Vue3 component library` rapid prototyping tool provides a series of commands and tools to solve the problem of component library development.

### Features

- 📦 &nbsp;Out-of-the-box component library development environment
- 📦 &nbsp;An out-of-the-box component library compilation tool that supports exporting `esm`, `cjs`, `umd` module codes
- 🛠️ &nbsp;Configuration file-based component library documentation site, support Baidu statistics and theme customization
- 🛠️ &nbsp;Supports both `sfc` and `tsx` styles for writing component libraries
- 📦 &nbsp;Out-of-the-box code inspection tool
- 📦 &nbsp;Out-of-the-box unit testing tools
- 📦 &nbsp;Out-of-the-box code publishing tool, publishes to both `npm` and `github`, and automatically generates changelogs
- 💪 &nbsp;Support for `VSCode` extension development
- 💪 &nbsp;Support `build svg to web fonts`
- 💪 &nbsp;Support for `Typescript`
- 💪 &nbsp;Support `Various themes, including default / maple brands and light / dark modes`
- 🌍 &nbsp;Support `Internationalization`
- 🚀 &nbsp;Based on `pnpm`

### Quickstart

`@maple-design/cli-vue` has built-in `sfc` and `tsx` style component library project templates, which can be generated directly by the `gen` command.
It is convenient for you to directly enter the component library development.

```shell
# playground-ignore
pnpm add @maple-design/cli-vue -g
maple-cli gen
```

### Custom pages

If you want to insert other pages into the component library, you can create a `pages` folder in the project root directory to write a vue component to generate other pages.
The directory structure is as follows:

```text
// playground-ignore
|-- maple-ui
  |-- src
  |-- docs
  |-- pages
    |-- sponsor
      |-- index.vue
    |-- contributor
      |-- locale
        |-- en-US.ts
      |-- index.vue
    |-- changelog
      |-- locale
        |-- zh-CN.ts
        |-- en-US.ts
      |-- index.vue
      
```

The resulting route is as follows:

```text
// playground-ignore
/zh-CN/sponsor
/en-US/contributor
/zh-CN/changelog
/en-US/changelog
```

``` shell
pnpm config set sharp_binary_host "https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/sharp"
pnpm config set sharp_libvips_binary_host "https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/sharp-libvips"
```

# Code

### Intro

Code Block component, used for code highlighted

### Notes

- `Code` does not bundle a syntax highlighter. Provide one that implements `codeToHtml` through `HighlighterProvider`.
- Shiki is a recommended integration, not a required dependency. You do not need to install Shiki if your project already has a compatible highlighter.

### Optional: Use Shiki

If you choose [Shiki](https://shiki.tmrs.site/), install it in your application with `pnpm add shiki`, `npm install shiki`, or `yarn add shiki`. See the Shiki documentation for [available themes](https://shiki.tmrs.site/themes) and other configuration options.

The examples below use Shiki only to demonstrate how highlighting is injected into `HighlighterProvider`; `Code` is not coupled to Shiki.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/code/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { Highlighter } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import { createHighlighterCore } from 'shiki/core'
import { createOnigurumaEngine } from 'shiki/engine/oniguruma'
import wasmUrl from 'shiki/onig.wasm?url'

let highlighter: ReturnType<typeof createHighlighterCore> | undefined

// Keep the demo bundle limited to its actual languages and themes. Load the
// binary as an asset, rather than embedding its base64 representation in JS.
const codeToHtml: Highlighter['codeToHtml'] = async (code, options) => {
  highlighter ??= createHighlighterCore({
    langs: [import('shiki/langs/javascript.mjs'), import('shiki/langs/python.mjs')],
    themes: [
      import('shiki/themes/vitesse-light.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/vitesse-dark.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/github-light.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/github-dark.mjs'),
    ],
    engine: createOnigurumaEngine(() => fetch(wasmUrl)),
  })
  return (await highlighter).codeToHtml(code, options)
}

const props = defineProps<{ dark?: boolean }>()
</script>

<template>
  <mp-highlighter-provider :highlighter="{ codeToHtml }" :theme="props.dark ? 'vitesse-dark' : 'vitesse-light'">
    <mp-space direction="column" size="lg">
      <mp-code code="console.log('Hello Maple UI')" language="javascript" />
      <mp-code code="print('Hello Maple UI')" language="python" />
      <mp-code
        code="console.log('Hello Maple UI')"
        language="javascript"
        :theme="props.dark ? 'github-dark' : 'github-light'"
      />
    </mp-space>
  </mp-highlighter-provider>
</template>
```

## Layout and arrangement

### Word Wrap

Set `word-wrap` to support automatic line wrapping when code overflows.

Example source: src/code/example/demos/word-wrap.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { Highlighter } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import { createHighlighterCore } from 'shiki/core'
import { createOnigurumaEngine } from 'shiki/engine/oniguruma'
import wasmUrl from 'shiki/onig.wasm?url'

let highlighter: ReturnType<typeof createHighlighterCore> | undefined

// Keep the demo bundle limited to its actual languages and themes. Load the
// binary as an asset, rather than embedding its base64 representation in JS.
const codeToHtml: Highlighter['codeToHtml'] = async (code, options) => {
  highlighter ??= createHighlighterCore({
    langs: [import('shiki/langs/javascript.mjs'), import('shiki/langs/python.mjs')],
    themes: [
      import('shiki/themes/vitesse-light.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/vitesse-dark.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/github-light.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/github-dark.mjs'),
    ],
    engine: createOnigurumaEngine(() => fetch(wasmUrl)),
  })
  return (await highlighter).codeToHtml(code, options)
}

const props = defineProps<{ dark?: boolean }>()
</script>

<template>
  <mp-highlighter-provider :highlighter="{ codeToHtml }" :theme="props.dark ? 'vitesse-dark' : 'vitesse-light'">
    <mp-code code="console.log('Hello Maple UI');console.log('Hello Maple UI');" language="javascript" word-wrap />
  </mp-highlighter-provider>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Configuration

Without a highlighter, or if highlighting fails, escaped source remains readable. Only the latest asynchronous result is used. The converter returns HTML that is rendered directly, so its output must be trusted. `word-wrap` controls wrapping on overflow; Code has no component events, slots, or public methods.

## API

### Code Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- | --------- | ------- |
| `code` | Code Snippet | _string_ | `''` |
| `language` | Code Language | _string_ | `-` |
| `theme` | Code Theme | _string_ | `-` |
| `word-wrap` | Whether to support automatic line wrapping when code overflows | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `trim` | Whether to remove the blank characters at the beginning and end of the code | _boolean_ | `true` |

### HighlighterProvider Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------- | ------------ | ------------- | ------ |
| `highlighter` | Code Highlighter | `Highlighter` | `-` |
| `theme` | Code Theme | _string_ | `-` |
| `tag` | Custom tag name | _string_ | `div` |

## Types

### Highlighter

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `codeToHtml` | Highlighter function, component highlighter must implement this function | `(code: string, options: CodeToHtmlOptions) => string \| Promise<string>` | `-` |

### CodeToHtmlOptions

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------- | ---- | -------- | ------ |
| `lang` | Code Language | _string_ | `-` |
| `theme` | Code Theme | _string_ | `-` |

# Col

24-column Flex layout. Row manages gutters and alignment; Col manages spans, offsets, ordering and breakpoints. Use Grid for CSS Grid collapse and suffix items.

> **Choosing a layout**
>
> - Grid + GridItem: Use for form columns and card grids with consistent column widths, spans, responsive column counts, or collapsed rows and suffix items.
> - Row + Col: Use for 24-column Flex layouts that need horizontal/vertical alignment, wrapping control, fixed and flexible widths together, or responsive ordering. Row controls the row; Col controls width, offset and order.
> - Space: Use for simple groups of buttons, tags or text that only need spacing, direction and alignment. Use native Flex for more flexible width allocation.

## Basic examples

### Span and offset

Example source: src/col/example/demos/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const span = ref(8)
const offset = ref(4)
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <div class="controls">
      Span<mp-radio-group v-model="span"
        ><mp-radio v-for="value in [4, 8, 12]" :key="value" :value="value">{{ value }}</mp-radio></mp-radio-group
      >
    </div>
    <div class="controls">
      Offset<mp-radio-group v-model="offset"
        ><mp-radio v-for="value in [0, 4, 8]" :key="value" :value="value">{{ value }}</mp-radio></mp-radio-group
      >
    </div>
    <mp-row :gutter="12"
      ><mp-col :span="span" :offset="offset"
        ><div class="cell">{{ span }} / +{{ offset }}</div></mp-col
      ><mp-col :span="4"><div class="cell soft">4</div></mp-col></mp-row
    >
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.controls {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 12px;
}
.cell {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  padding: 12px;
  min-width: 0;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: var(--mp-color-primary);
  color: var(--mp-color-white);
  text-align: center;
```
