## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->
### Col Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| span | Column span; integer 0–24, with zero hiding the column | `number` | `24` |
| offset | Offset from the logical inline start; integer 0–24, with zero restoring it | `number` | `undefined` |
| order | Visual order; finite integer, including negative values; zero restores it | `number` | `undefined` |
| xs | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| sm | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| md | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| lg | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| xl | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| xxl | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| flex | Ratio, fixed length or CSS flex value | `number / string` | `undefined` |

### Col Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| click | Native MouseEvent, emitted once per click |

### Col Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Layout content |

### Col Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

The order example restores every column to `order: 0` when reverse is turned off. Responsive breakpoints use the browser viewport rather than the demo card width; widening the card alone does not activate a breakpoint. `span: 0` hides a column, and a matching larger breakpoint can restore it.

## Responsiveness and accessibility

Row resolves responsive gutter with JavaScript matchMedia, using xs for SSR and synchronizing the viewport after mounting. Col uses CSS media queries: SSR already emits all configured classes without waiting for measurement. Breakpoints use viewport width: xs is the base; sm ≥576, md ≥768, lg ≥992, xl ≥1200 and xxl ≥1600px. Only configured fields override earlier values. Offset starts at the logical inline edge and mirrors in RTL. Order affects visual positioning while preserving DOM, keyboard and assistive technology reading order.

Span, offset and their breakpoint fields accept integers from 0 through 24. A zero span hides the column; offset 24 shifts it by a full row width. Order accepts finite integers, including negative values and values above 24, subject to browser CSS order computation. Gutter accepts finite nonnegative numbers, six-breakpoint objects or exactly two entries [horizontal, vertical]. Development diagnostics report unknown breakpoints, invalid numbers and enum values. Invalid span falls back to 24; invalid offset/order is ignored; breakpoint objects retain valid fields; invalid gutter components fall back to zero.

## Imports

Grid contains only Grid.Item. Import the independent Row and Col components from the library root or their row/col subpaths; installing Grid does not register them. 

`flex` overrides column width while preserving `offset`, `order` and responsive configuration. `span: 0`, including breakpoint values, still hides the column; a matching nonzero span restores visibility while `flex` controls width. Removing `flex` restores the span width. Visual ordering does not change DOM or keyboard navigation `order`.

Internal custom properties and measurement values are implementation details and are not customization APIs.

# Collapse

A content area which can be collapsed and expanded. Examples match Cedar Design Web, with a more compact mobile layout.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Group and hide complex content. Multiple panels can stay open.

Example source: src/collapse/example/demos/basic.vue

```vue
<template>

    <mp-collapse-item title="Beijing Toutiao Technology Co., Ltd." name="1">
      <div>Beijing Toutiao Technology Co., Ltd.</div>
    </mp-collapse-item>
    <mp-collapse-item title="Beijing Toutiao Technology Co., Ltd." :name="2">
      <div>Beijing Toutiao Technology Co., Ltd.</div>
    </mp-collapse-item>
    <mp-collapse-item title="Beijing Toutiao Technology Co., Ltd." name="3">
      <div>Beijing Toutiao Technology Co., Ltd.</div>
    </mp-collapse-item>
  </mp-collapse>
```

## Interaction and control

### Toggle all

Use `toggleAll` to expand or collapse all panels. It is a no-op in accordion mode.

Example source: src/collapse/example/demos/toggle-all.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :style="{ width: '100%' }">
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: 'inverse' })">Toggle all</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: 'inverse', skipDisabled: true })">Toggle all (skip disabled)</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: true })">Expand all</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: true, skipDisabled: true })">Expand all (skip disabled)</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: false })">Collapse all</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: false, skipDisabled: true })">Collapse all (skip disabled)</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <mp-collapse ref="collapseRef" v-model="activeNames">
      <mp-collapse-item title="Panel 1" name="1">
        <div>Content 1</div>
      </mp-collapse-item>
      <mp-collapse-item title="Panel 2" name="2">
        <div>Content 2</div>
      </mp-collapse-item>
      <mp-collapse-item title="Panel 3" name="3" disabled>
        <div>Content 3</div>
      </mp-collapse-item>
      <mp-collapse-item title="Panel 4" name="4" disabled>
        <div>Content 4</div>
      </mp-collapse-item>
    </mp-collapse>
  </mp-space>
</template>
<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const collapseRef = ref<{
  toggleAll: (options: { expand: boolean | 'inverse'; skipDisabled?: boolean }) => void
}>()
const activeNames = ref<(string | number)[]>(['2', '4'])

const toggleAll = (options: { expand: boolean | 'inverse'; skipDisabled?: boolean }) => {
  collapseRef.value?.toggleAll(options)
}
</script>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Header and expanded content inherit reading direction; changing direction preserves expansion. expand-icon-position left/right remain physical sides. Custom expansion graphics are not mirrored automatically.

## API

The main value uses ordinary `v-model`: `modelValue` is an array of expanded panel names, including in accordion mode. `defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled state only on creation; later changes do not reset it. Initialization does not emit `update:modelValue`. When `modelValue` is provided, the parent controls the state and its value is authoritative.

<!-- same-source-api:start -->

### Collapse Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model-value | Expanded names; v-model | `(string \| number)[]` | `—` |
| default-value | Uncontrolled initial expanded names | `(string \| number)[]` | `[]` |
| accordion | Accordion mode; at most one open panel | `boolean` | `false` |
| show-expand-icon | Whether to show expansion icons; child items decide when omitted | `boolean` | `—` |
| expand-icon-position | Expand-icon position within the header: left or right, default left. Does not control content expansion direction | `'left' \| 'right'` | `'left'` |
| bordered | Whether to show border | `boolean` | `true` |
| divider | Show dividers | `boolean` | `true` |
| offset | Gap between expanded panels | `boolean` | `false` |
| destroy-on-hide | Destroy content when hidden | `boolean` | `false` |

Panel content is mounted eagerly by default. When either the parent or an item enables `destroy-on-hide`, closed content is destroyed after the closing transition; reopening during the transition preserves it. Changing this setting while closed takes effect immediately. An explicit parent `show-expand-icon` overrides the item setting.

### Collapse Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:model-value | Request an expanded-name update | `(string \| number)[]` |
| change | Emitted when expanded panels change | `(string \| number)[]`, `Event` |

### Collapse Slots

| Slot | Description | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Panel list | `—` |

### Collapse Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| toggleAll | Expand or collapse all panels (no-op in accordion) |

<!-- same-source-api:end -->


The parent `expand-icon` slot is forwarded to items that do not provide their own icon. Scope: `expanded`, `disabled`, `position`. It is not rendered on the root node.

### CollapseItem Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name **(required)** | Unique panel identifier corresponding to a value in `modelValue` | `string \| number` | `—` |
| title | Panel title | `string` | `—` |
| heading-level | Heading level from 1 to 6, chosen for the page; omitted by default | `1–6` | `—` |
| region | Whether content is a region landmark | `boolean` | `true` |
| disabled | Whether disabled | `boolean` | `false` |
| show-expand-icon | Whether to show an expansion icon | `boolean` | `true` |
| destroy-on-hide | Destroy content when hidden | `boolean` | `false` |

Choose `heading-level` for the page structure; set `:region="false"` when many panels would create excessive region landmarks. `extra` sits outside the header button and can contain independent actions; avoid interactive controls in title and expand-icon slots. A right-side expand icon sits inside the header button, followed by `extra`.

### CollapseItem Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| title | Panel title | `—` |
| extra | Extra content | `—` |
| expand-icon | Expand icon | expanded: `boolean`<br>disabled: `boolean`<br>position: `'left' \| 'right'` |
| default | Panel content | `—` |

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-collapse-border-color: var(--mp-sys-color-border-default);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

#### Reduced motion

Built-in CSS transitions follow `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Removing transitions does not change final visibility, selected/expanded state or event semantics. Applications control custom animations inside slots.

# Color

### Intro

Semantic color utilities with prefix `mp-` (Cedar uses `c-*`), variables `--mp-*`.  
Full scales: [Palette](#/en-US/palette).

```js
// playground-ignore
import '@maple-design/ui-vue/utilities/style'
```

### Class rules

| Class | Variable |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `mp-primary` / `mp-success` / `mp-warning` / `mp-danger` / `mp-info` | `rgb(var(--mp-{hue}-6))` |
| `mp-*-hover` / `mp-*-pressed` / `mp-*-disabled` | scale 5 / 7 / 3 |
| `mp-bg-primary` etc. | `rgb(var(--mp-{hue}-1))` |
| `mp-text-1` … `mp-text-4` | `var(--mp-color-text-*)` |
| `mp-fill-1` … `mp-fill-4` | `var(--mp-color-fill-*)` |
| `mp-color-border-1` … `mp-color-border-4` | `var(--mp-color-border-*)` |
| `mp-bg-0` / `mp-bg-1` / `mp-bg-2` | background levels |

`mp-info` maps to `--mp-info-*`. See phone preview for demos.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/color/example/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { onThemeChange } from '@maple-design/cli-vue/client'

onThemeChange()
const status = ['primary', 'success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info']
const levels = [1, 2, 3, 4]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="demo mp-px-16 mp-py-16">
    <div class="mp-text-1 mp-mb-8">Status</div>
    <div class="mp-flex mp-flex-wrap mp-items-center" style="gap: 8px">
      <div
        v-for="name in status"
        :key="name"
        class="mp-px-8 mp-py-4 mp-rounded-sm"
        :class="[`mp-${name}`, `mp-bg-${name}`]"
      >
        mp-{{ name }}
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="mp-text-1 mp-mt-24 mp-mb-8">Text / Fill / Border / Bg</div>
    <div class="mp-flex mp-flex-wrap" style="gap: 8px">
      <div v-for="n in levels" :key="`t-${n}`" :class="`mp-text-${n}`">mp-text-{{ n }}</div>
    </div>
    <div class="mp-flex mp-flex-wrap mp-mt-8" style="gap: 8px">
      <div v-for="n in levels" :key="`f-${n}`" class="mp-px-8 mp-py-4 mp-rounded-sm" :class="`mp-fill-${n}`">
        mp-fill-{{ n }}
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="mp-flex mp-flex-wrap mp-mt-8" style="gap: 8px">
      <div
        v-for="n in levels"
        :key="`bd-${n}`"
        class="mp-px-8 mp-py-4 mp-rounded-sm"
        :class="`mp-color-border-${n}`"
        style="border-width: 2px; border-style: solid"
      >
        mp-color-border-{{ n }}
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="mp-flex mp-flex-wrap mp-mt-8" style="gap: 8px">
      <div
        v-for="n in [0, 1, 2]"
        :key="`b-${n}`"
        class="mp-px-8 mp-py-4 mp-rounded-sm mp-border-2"
        :class="`mp-bg-${n}`"
        style="border-width: 1px; border-style: solid"
      >
        mp-bg-{{ n }}
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style lang="less">
@import '../../style/theme/css-variables.less';
@import '../../utilities/style/utilities.less';
</style>
```

## Empty-value recognition and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

# Cross-platform component reuse

The labels mean: Same source (verified copies), Logic copies (verified), Same source (planned copies), Adapt (planned copies after adaptation), Logic copies (planned; keep platform UI), Separate (different abstraction). Each library owns its source; there is no shared runtime core or generated component source. Planned labels do not mean completed alignment. Unmarked entries are unassessed or have no confirmed counterpart. The detailed audit below is maintained in Chinese.

# Cedar / Maple 跨端代码复用调研

审计日期：2026-10-09。基于当前工作区源码（包含正在进行的 API 对齐改动），不是发布版本保证。标记规则更新：2026-09-21；已完成的完整同源与逻辑同源均有独立源码门禁。

已同源 56 组；待同源 0 组；待适配 0 组；逻辑待同源 0 组；逻辑已同源 15 组；独立 1 组。按组件族计数，包含子组件及异名 Drawer / Popup；不等于菜单条目数量。

## 菜单标记

| 标记 | 含义 | 建议顺序 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [已同源] | 已完成对应范围的源码对齐并纳入一致性检查；两端各自维护源码 | P0：保持检查，作为后续样板 |
| [逻辑已同源] | 稳定逻辑已独立复制并纳入一致性检查；端侧展示/交互按职责保留 | P0：保持检查 |
| [待同源] | 主体适合同源复制；尚待实现对齐与双端验证，不是已完成 | P1 |
| [待适配] | 先对齐 API 或适配依赖，再同源复制主体；尚未完成 | P2 |
| [逻辑待同源] | 计划将内部逻辑同源复制为两份，保留端侧展示/交互；尚未完成 | P3 |
| [独立] | 同名但语义层级不同，不要求主体同源 | 暂缓 |

未标记表示本次没有确认跨端对应关系，或是主题/指南/指令等页面；不表示无法复用。所有候选均采用独立复制、双端同步维护；不引用同一份核心，不建立跨库运行时依赖，不通过外部模板生成组件源码。各库内部工具复用不受影响。

## 调研依据和限制

重新运行 api-contract-inventory.mjs，从 TypeScript 根入口追踪得到 Cedar 129 / Maple 119 个运行时 Props 导出，97 个同名导出可比较（包含子组件）。Props 名称相同不能证明默认值、类型、事件、插槽、方法和行为完全一致。额外检查了主体模板/TSX、事件触发、插槽、计时与弹层依赖；详细 Props 键差异见下方附录。单独登记尚未收口的能力与主体差异，不把历史根导出不对称当作当前结论。

copied-components-check.mjs 覆盖完整同源主体；copied-foundations-check.mjs 覆盖逻辑同源控制器。安装入口、主题 token、图标及端侧视图仍由两库独立维护。新增检查不会自动升级分类，须完成双端验证后更新。

初轮完成调研、菜单和文档标记；后续已完成的复制重构按同源标记维护。后续严格遵循包内复制 + 一致性检查方式：先修改并验证一端，再复制自然一致的部分至另一端，仅调整前缀、本地导入与必要端侧实现，后续两边同步修改。不抽取两端共同引用的核心实现，不共享实例或状态。

## 后续维护与实施

1. 以已完成组件的包内独立复制和源码一致性检查为模板；差异按职责拆分到本库文件，不引入共享运行时或 platform 配置层。
2. 原待同源 11 组和 Link / Paper 已完成；后续按待适配、逻辑待同源分类逐项推进，不因本批完成而自动升级其他候选。
3. 每个组件先固定 Props 类型/默认值、事件载荷和顺序、Slots 参数、Expose，以及受控/非受控语义；子组件必须一并验收。
4. 配对测试各自保存在两库并分别运行，覆盖键盘与触控、禁用/只读、SSR、挂载清理和主题。弹层额外覆盖嵌套、焦点恢复及滚动锁。通过后再升级为已同源标记。

## 未配对范围

Cedar 的 Tree / Transfer / Descriptions / Timeline / FilterForm 等，以及 Maple 的 PullRefresh / SwipeCell / IndexBar / NumberKeyboard / Signature 等，本次没有确认可直接同源对齐的对应组件，保留原菜单。Drawer / Popup 是异名候选；Message 不直接等同 NoticeBar 或 Notification。Cedar 日期/时间 picker 在内部子目录，Maple 菜单通过字段文档组织，标记数量因此不同。

## 维护

唯一分类数据：design-ui/audits/component-reuse.json。修改后从工作区运行 node design-ui/bin/component-reuse-sync.mjs，同步两库的文档元数据；--check 检查漂移。复制的是文档元数据，不是组件源码。后续源码变化后应重新运行 Props 审计并复核分级，不能只更新日期。

# Controlled state, defaults and clear values: learn by interaction

Start with Input behavior, then expand v-model and finally examine emptyValue. This guide describes current workspace behavior; the proposed unified contract is discussed separately at the end.

Register components and include styles as described in Quick Start. Each complete Vue example is independent. Input examples explicitly use `edit-mode="direct"` so popup confirmation drafts do not obscure ownership.

## 1. Separate the questions

| Question                                | What determines it?                          | Example                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Who decides the final current value?    | modelValue and the component ownership check | Parent supplies A, rejects B, final value remains A    |
| Is this only an initial value?          | defaultValue                                 | Start with Hangzhou, let the user change it later      |
| What value does a clear action propose? | emptyValue, written empty-value in templates | null, an empty string, or a configured value           |
| Does a value look empty?                | Component type, options and formatting       | Input renders null as blank, but EMPTY as literal text |

Controlled means the parent owns the final value. It does not mean disabled, unfocusable, without input events, or stored on a server. The parent is the Vue component containing `<mp-input ... />`; its ref or form object holds the external state.

emptyValue answers the clear-output question. It does not automatically answer ownership or empty-value recognition. It is not a list of values considered empty.

## 2. Uncontrolled: provide a seed, let the component store later edits

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const seed = ref('Hangzhou')
const instanceKey = ref(0)
const lastRequest = ref<string | null>()
function record(next: string | null) {
  lastRequest.value = next
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input :key="instanceKey" :default-value="seed" edit-mode="direct" @update:model-value="record" />
  <p>Initial seed: {{ seed }}</p>
  <p>Last update request: {{ JSON.stringify(lastRequest) }}</p>
  <button type="button" @click="seed = 'Beijing'">Change default only</button>
  <button type="button" @click="instanceKey++">Remount</button>
</template>
```

| Action                             | Input text   | Parent seed | Explanation                                                            |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mount                              | Hangzhou     | Hangzhou    | The component reads the default                                        |
| Select all and replace with Suzhou | Suzhou       | Hangzhou    | The component stores the edit; recording an event does not modify seed |
| Change default only                | Still Suzhou | Beijing     | Defaults do not overwrite current edits                                |
| Remount                            | Beijing      | Beijing     | The new instance reads the current default                             |

An update listener only observes candidates. Without binding the recorded value back through modelValue, it does not control the component. Initialization does not emit an initial value to populate the parent.

Changing defaultValue is not a reset command. Use controlled binding when the application needs to replace the current value programmatically.

## 3. Controlled and accepting updates

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const text = ref<string | null>('A')
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input v-model="text" edit-mode="direct" />
  <p>Parent value: {{ JSON.stringify(text) }}</p>
  <button type="button" @click="text = 'C'">Parent sets C</button>
</template>
```

Select A and replace it with B. Parent text becomes B and the input follows that parent value. Click the button and the parent replaces it with C.

```text
Parent text=A → input receives A
User enters B → component emits update:modelValue(B)
Parent assigns text=B → prop becomes B → final display is B
```

Writing back means assigning the parent's own ref/form field and passing that value down again. The child does not directly modify the parent variable. v-model generates the write-back binding for you. [Vue documentation](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/v-model.html)

## 4. Controlled and rejecting updates

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const text = ref<string | null>('A')
const requested = ref<string | null>()
const count = ref(0)
function recordOnly(next: string | null) {
  requested.value = next
  count.value++
  // Deliberately do not assign text.value = next.
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input :model-value="text" edit-mode="direct" @update:model-value="recordOnly" />
  <p>Parent value: {{ JSON.stringify(text) }}</p>
  <p>Candidate: {{ JSON.stringify(requested) }}; requests: {{ count }}</p>
</template>
```

Select all of A and try entering B. The candidate becomes B and the counter increases, but parent text stays A. The settled input remains A. Native editing text can appear briefly before the component reconciles; judge the final state after the current update settles.

| Item                | Before | After proposing B |
| ------------------- | ------ | ----------------- |
| Parent text         | A      | A                 |
| Candidate           | None   | B                 |
| Final model/display | A      | A                 |

An update event is not proof of acceptance. The parent can accept, reject or correct a candidate.

For an intentionally non-editable field, use readonly/disabled and their documented focus, copy and event semantics. Ignoring updates here demonstrates ownership; it is not the recommended way to implement readonly UI.

## 5. Accept conditionally

A boolean Switch makes the decision easy to see:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const enabled = ref(false)
const allowUpdate = ref(false)
const requested = ref<string | number | boolean | null>()
function decide(next: string | number | boolean | null) {
  requested.value = next
  if (allowUpdate.value && typeof next === 'boolean') {
    enabled.value = next
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <label><input v-model="allowUpdate" type="checkbox" />Parent accepts updates</label>
  <mp-switch :model-value="enabled" @update:model-value="decide" />
  <p>Parent value: {{ enabled }}；Candidate: {{ JSON.stringify(requested) }}</p>
</template>
```

With the native checkbox unchecked, clicking Switch proposes true but leaves the parent and Switch false. Enable the checkbox, click again, and the parent accepts true.

This uses Switch's default boolean values. Adapt the parent type and decision if checkedValue/uncheckedValue are customized. When acceptance requires asynchronous work, show pending explicitly so a request is not mistaken for a completed change.

## 6. What does v-model generate?

```html
<mp-input v-model="text" />
```

The corresponding template binding is:

```html
<mp-input :model-value="text" @update:model-value="text = $event" />
```

Script functions assign `text.value = next`; templates unwrap refs automatically.

| Binding                             | Passes an external value? | Writes updates back?                                          | Meaning for strict controlled components |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| default-value only                  | No                        | No                                                            | Component stores subsequent values       |
| Update listener only                | No                        | Depends on listener, but not controlling without binding back | Observation                              |
| model-value=A only                  | Yes                       | No                                                            | Final value remains A                    |
| model-value plus recording listener | Yes                       | No                                                            | Observe candidates, keep A               |
| model-value plus assignment handler | Yes                       | Yes                                                           | Parent may filter updates                |
| v-model=text                        | Yes                       | Automatically                                                 | Usually accepts every update             |

For components checking modelValue !== undefined, a v-model ref initialized to undefined still starts uncontrolled. Local proxy exceptions also exist; see section 15.

Adding an update listener to v-model and returning false does not cancel v-model's generated assignment. Use an explicit value binding and handler when rejection matters. Returning false from change is not a guard either. Do not execute the same save twice in both update and change handlers.

## 7. Does emptyValue conflict with controlled state?

The features are compatible. The specific problem is undefined carrying two meanings in a particular binding.

For models using this ownership rule, including Input, InputNumber, Switch, Slider and Select:

```ts
// Conceptual rule, not code users need to add.
const isControlled = modelValue !== undefined
```

An empty string, 0, false and a supported null are defined values. Validity remains component-specific: a defined 0 is not automatically a valid page number.

| Clear candidate | Parent decision                    | Returned modelValue | Result                                             |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| null            | Accept                             | null                | Controlled if null is supported                    |
| Empty string    | Accept                             | Empty string        | Controlled                                         |
| undefined       | Accept unchanged                   | undefined           | Becomes uncontrolled                               |
| undefined       | Normalize to null                  | null                | Remains controlled                                 |
| Any candidate   | Ignore, retain A                   | A                   | Retains the original controlled state              |
| undefined       | Component was already uncontrolled | Unbound             | Internal empty state; no parent control to release |

Do not infer ownership loss from emptyValue alone. The mode changes when the parent actually passes undefined back, not merely when the factory runs or an event is observed.

## 8. The empty-value forms are different

Current resolveEmptyValue behavior uses each component's fallback when no override is provided:

| Configuration                    | Meaning                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Omitted                          | Component's current default clear output                                |
| `:empty-value="undefined"`       | Same fallback; does not force undefined output                          |
| `:empty-value="() => undefined"` | Explicit undefined output, where the component type permits the factory |
| `:empty-value="null"`            | Explicit null output                                                    |
| `empty-value="EMPTY"`            | Literal EMPTY string, not necessarily a blank display                   |
| `:empty-value="0"`               | Numeric zero, if valid for this component                               |
| `:empty-value="() => []"`        | New empty array, subject to model and business constraints              |

The factory distinguishes absence from an explicit undefined result. Input's clear type is string/null or a matching factory; do not bypass its type to force an unsupported undefined factory. The next undefined example uses InputNumber, which supports it.

Vue binding matters: `empty-value="null"` is a string, while `:empty-value="null"` is null. An unbound `empty-value="0"` is not a numeric binding.

Verified current default paths:

| Component/path                               | Default candidate without an override                   |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Input clear button                           | Empty string                                            |
| InputNumber clear button                     | undefined                                               |
| Select single without an empty-string option | Usually empty string                                    |
| Select single with a value='' option         | undefined, distinguishing that option from no selection |
| Select multiple                              | Usually []; protected disabled selections may remain    |

This is not an inventory of all component empty-value contracts. Dates, times and panels have additional paths. emptyValue does not bypass disabled/readonly, pending transactions or protected selections.

## 9. Input clears to null and stays controlled

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const text = ref<string | null>('A')
const updates = ref<string[]>([])
function accept(next: string | null) {
  updates.value.push(JSON.stringify(next))
  text.value = next
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input :model-value="text" :empty-value="null" edit-mode="direct" clearable @update:model-value="accept" />
  <p>Parent value: {{ JSON.stringify(text) }}</p>
  <p>Update log: {{ updates.join(' → ') }}</p>
</template>
```

| Action                               | Candidate    | Parent text  | Display |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------ | ------------ | ------- |
| Mount                                | None         | A            | A       |
| Click clear                          | null         | null         | Blank   |
| Type B                               | B            | B            | B       |
| Select all and delete with Backspace | Empty string | Empty string | Blank   |

null and an empty string look blank but are different model values. Current emptyValue controls the clear action; it does not transform manual deletion into null. If your business requires every empty text value to be null, assign `text.value = next === '' ? null : next` in the parent.

Likewise, an Input configured with literal EMPTY emits and displays EMPTY on clear. A clear button does not guarantee a blank final model.

## 10. Why can undefined clear change ownership?

This example observes current behavior. It is not the recommended configuration for a persistently controlled form.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const quantity = ref<number | null | undefined>(12)
const clearToUndefined = () => undefined
const describe = (value: unknown) => (value === undefined ? 'undefined' : JSON.stringify(value))
const lastRequest = ref('No update yet')
function accept(next: number | null | undefined) {
  lastRequest.value = describe(next)
  quantity.value = next
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input-number
    :model-value="quantity"
    :empty-value="clearToUndefined"
    edit-mode="direct"
    clearable
    @update:model-value="accept"
  />
  <p>Parent value: {{ describe(quantity) }}；Candidate: {{ lastRequest }}</p>
  <p>Controlled by the current check: {{ quantity !== undefined }}</p>
</template>
```

| Step                                                     | Parent quantity | quantity !== undefined | Final owner                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Initially 12                                             | 12              | true                   | Parent                                           |
| Component proposes undefined, before handling            | Still 12        | true                   | Still parent                                     |
| Parent accepts unchanged                                 | undefined       | false                  | Component                                        |
| Later interaction while parent supplies no defined value | undefined       | false                  | Component may store subsequent values internally |

The trigger is the actual modelValue becoming undefined, not the blank display. A later defined parent value makes it controlled again. Current handoff retention varies between components; do not rely on mode changes for reset.

A ref's declared number/null type does not convert a runtime undefined event into null automatically.

## 11. Recommended: normalize at the parent boundary

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const quantity = ref<number | null>(12)
const lastRequest = ref('No update yet')
function acceptNormalized(next: number | null | undefined) {
  lastRequest.value = next === undefined ? 'undefined' : JSON.stringify(next)
  quantity.value = next ?? null
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input-number
    :model-value="quantity"
    :empty-value="null"
    edit-mode="direct"
    clearable
    @update:model-value="acceptNormalized"
  />
  <p>组件Candidate: {{ lastRequest }}</p>
  <p>Final parent value: {{ JSON.stringify(quantity) }}</p>
  <p>Controlled by the current check: {{ quantity !== undefined }}</p>
</template>
```

This handles the clear button and other update paths producing undefined: null → null, undefined → null, 0 → 0, other numbers unchanged. The parent's quantity remains defined, preserving final controlled ownership.

Why use a handler as well as empty-value=null? InputNumber's clear-button path calls resolveEmptyValue, while manual deletion followed by commit can directly produce undefined. modelEvent='input' may propose the empty value earlier. emptyValue is not an input parser or a normalizer for every submission path.

Avoid `next || null`, which also discards valid zero. Use `next ?? null` for null/undefined only. Do not apply this nullable-number example to a model such as pagination that does not accept null.

A writable computed setter can perform the same normalization behind v-model; a readonly computed cannot accept assignments. Separate local updates from persistence. Usually update the form synchronously and save on explicit submission; if acceptance must wait for approval, keep the old value and show pending deliberately.

## 12. A valid empty-string option differs from no selection

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
const options = [
  { label: 'All', value: '' },
  { label: 'Enabled only', value: 'enabled' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <mp-select v-model="selected" :options="options" :empty-value="null" edit-mode="direct" clearable />
  <p>Parent value: {{ JSON.stringify(selected) }}</p>
</template>
```

| Action              | Parent selected | Meaning                        |
| ------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Initially           | null            | No selection                   |
| Choose All          | Empty string    | A valid selected option        |
| Choose Enabled only | enabled         | Another valid option           |
| Clear               | null            | No selection, still controlled |

Do not use selected === '' to mean both All and no selection. Element Plus illustrates a similar case but exposes separate empty-values and value-on-clear APIs. Our emptyValue does not automatically provide its empty-values functionality.

For multiple selection, initialize and clear according to the array model. A nullable single-selection example does not imply that every multi-selection should use null. Protected disabled selections can survive clear; emptyValue does not override that rule.

## 13. Value and popup visibility are separate models

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
const panelOpen = ref(false)
const allowClose = ref(true)
const options = [
  { label: 'Hangzhou', value: 'hz' },
  { label: 'Beijing', value: 'bj' },
]
function acceptOpen(next: boolean) {
  if (next || allowClose.value) panelOpen.value = next
}
</script>

<template>
  <label><input v-model="allowClose" type="checkbox" />Accept close requests</label>
  <mp-select
    v-model="selected"
    :open="panelOpen"
    :options="options"
    :empty-value="null"
    edit-mode="direct"
    clearable
    @update:open="acceptOpen"
  />
  <p>Value: {{ JSON.stringify(selected) }}; open: {{ panelOpen }}</p>
  <button type="button" @click="panelOpen = false">Parent closes directly</button>
</template>
```

The value binding accepts updates directly; the visibility handler can reject close requests. Disable Accept close requests: value changes can still be accepted while close requests are ignored. Parent closes directly changes panelOpen itself.

There is no single global controlled flag for the whole component. Each model has its own owner. v-model:open is shorthand for open plus its update assignment.

This example uses Select's direct editing mode. Confirmation presentations additionally own a draft: selecting edits the draft, confirmation submits it and cancellation discards it. A visible draft changing does not prove the committed model is uncontrolled.

## 14. Initialize, reset and serialize form data

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'

const form = reactive<{ name: string | null; quantity: number | null }>({
  name: null,
  quantity: null,
})
const payloadText = ref('Not submitted yet')
function updateQuantity(next: number | null | undefined) {
  form.quantity = next ?? null
}
function reset() {
  form.name = null
  form.quantity = null
}
function submit() {
  const payload = {
    name: form.name === null ? undefined : form.name,
    quantity: form.quantity === null ? undefined : form.quantity,
  }
  payloadText.value = JSON.stringify(payload)
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-input v-model="form.name" :empty-value="null" edit-mode="direct" clearable />
  <mp-input-number
    :model-value="form.quantity"
    :empty-value="null"
    edit-mode="direct"
    clearable
    @update:model-value="updateQuantity"
  />
  <button type="button" @click="reset">Reset parent data</button>
  <button type="button" @click="submit">Build payload</button>
  <p>Payload: {{ payloadText }}</p>
</template>
```

This uses an ordinary reactive object without depending on Form layout/validation APIs. The parent initializes and resets its fields. defaultValue does not populate an empty parent form; initialize form.name directly when a name is required initially.

Serialization maps UI null to undefined object properties, which JSON omits, without changing the UI model itself. If the API expects explicit JSON null, retain null in the payload instead.

UI empty values and transport formats need not match. A backend's omitted-field convention does not require modelValue to be undefined. Empty strings are still sent unchanged in this example; omit them explicitly at the serialization boundary if your business requires it.

## 15. Current exceptions

These describe current behavior, not an implemented target contract:

| Scope                                | Difference                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Maple ActionSheet.open               | Default useVModel local proxy can change internal state                                    |
| Maple NumberKeyboard.open/modelValue | Both use the default proxy                                                                 |
| Maple FloatingPanel.modelValue       | Proxy anchor plus separate gesture display height                                          |
| Maple Popup with beforeClose         | Internal visible can intercept external open=false and emit update:open(true) on rejection |
| Both Collapse implementations        | Nullish fallback; null falls back internally, use [] to collapse all                       |

For the first three, ignoring update does not guarantee the display remains unchanged. Passing the same external value again may not trigger the proxy watcher. Both libraries have equivalent useVModel helpers, but Input/Switch/Slider manage their own ownership.

InputNumber may retain intermediate text, Input has IME composition, and Popup can retain transition DOM. Distinguish final models from editing/gesture state and animation retention.

## 16. Documentation patterns worth borrowing

These are references for explanation style, not interchangeable APIs, empty values or handoff rules. All examples above were written for our components.

| Reference                                                                                                                            | Useful teaching pattern                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Reka controlled state](https://www.reka-ui.com/docs/guides/controlled-state)                                                        | Place explicit write-back, v-model and defaultValue side by side              |
| [React Input](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/input#controlling-an-input-with-a-state-variable)                     | Explain ownership through visible reversion when updates are ignored          |
| [Radix async Dialog submission](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dialog#close-after-asynchronous-form-submission) | Show why a parent closes only after saving                                    |
| [Element Plus Select empty values](https://element-plus.org/en-US/component/select.html#empty-values)                                | Separate empty recognition and clear output using a valid empty-string option |
| [Naive UI controlled state](https://www.naiveui.com/zh-CN/docs/controlled-uncontrolled)                                              | State how undefined affects ownership explicitly                              |

React's native controlled text input should not receive null/undefined. Our Input supports null and renders it blank. Borrow explanations, not framework-specific empty-value constraints. A value-only binding can also be intentional; it is an error only relative to an expectation of accepting edits.

## 17. Proposed design and existing emptyValue

The unified design is not implemented. The recommendation is parent-owned final state, initialize-only defaults, defined domain values for standard clear output, and separate drafts/gestures/animation.

Retain configurable emptyValue output rather than treating every () => undefined as invalid. It remains useful with explicit parent normalization, published APIs and intentional business behavior. Passing the result back unchanged as undefined must still mean uncontrolled under the chosen predicate.

Audit all empty paths separately: clear buttons, keyboard deletion, panel clearing and Form reset. Fixing the button alone leaves gaps. Changing published default empty values, ownership handoff or proxy behavior requires a versioned migration; changing documentation does not implement that behavior.

## 18. Troubleshooting order

1. Identify the exact state: modelValue, open or a draft.
2. Inspect the actual external value, not only the ref's static type or blank display.
3. Record update candidates and inspect whether/how the parent assigns them.
4. Distinguish clear button, manual deletion, panel confirmation and Form reset.
5. Check whether emptyValue is omitted, null, a string or an undefined-returning factory.
6. Check the proxy/guard exceptions in section 15.

Source references: both libraries' packages/_-ui/src/input/use-input-value.ts, input-number/use-number-value.ts, select/use-select-controller.ts and empty-value helpers; packages/_-use/src/useVModel.ts; Maple's listed proxy components and Popup. Expected-value tables explain audited paths; they are not a claim that every component and browser interaction has been verified.

## Numeric and animation boundaries

### Scientific notation and decimal floor

Precision is an integer from -292 to 292. Fractional and nonfinite precision falls back to 0; out-of-range integers are clamped. Unsupported inputs produce a development prop warning. String precision keeps the existing parseFloat conversion. Negative precision rounds at tens/hundreds and larger decimal places. The result is a number rounded toward negative infinity, without trailing-zero padding, and may use scientific notation. Changing precision only reformats the current value. IEEE-754 representability still applies; animation values are not decimal accounting values.

Example source: src/count-to/example/demos/decimal-floor.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>微小数值 / Small value: -1.234e-7</p>
    <mp-count-to
      class="scientific-small"
      :from="-1.234e-7"
      :to="-1.234e-7"
      :precision="precision"
      :auto-start="false"
    />
    <mp-button @click="precision = precision === 9 ? 8 : 9">切换精度 / Toggle precision</mp-button>
    <p role="status">Precision: {{ precision }}. 仅改变展示精度，不重播。Changes formatting without replay.</p>
    <p>大数按十进制位取整 / Large value, precision -23:</p>
    <mp-count-to class="scientific-large" :from="-1.234e24" :to="-1.234e24" :precision="-23" :auto-start="false" />
    <p>向负无穷取整 / Floor toward negative infinity:</p>
    <mp-count-to class="negative-floor" :from="-12.351" :to="-12.351" :precision="2" :auto-start="false" />
  </mp-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const precision = ref(9)
</script>
```

### Zero duration and replay

Example source: src/count-to/example/demos/zero-duration.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-count-to ref="counter" :from="0" :to="100" :duration="duration" @end="ends++" />
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="duration = duration === 0 ? 600 : 0">切换时长 / Toggle duration</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="counter?.reset()">重新播放 / Replay</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p role="status">Duration: {{ duration }}ms; end: {{ ends }}. 0 时长在下一帧完成，不占用持续动画帧。</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { CountToInstance } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const counter = ref<CountToInstance>()
const duration = ref(0)
const ends = ref(0)
</script>
```

### Change easing and replay

Changing timing-function affects the next reset, including resets caused by from, to or duration changes. It does not restart the current animation. Pause/start resumes the existing curve; reset creates a fresh playback using the latest function. Clearing the function restores linear easing. A curve may reach the target early, but end still reports completion of the configured duration.

Example source: src/count-to/example/demos/easing-replay.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-count-to ref="counter" :to="100" :duration="1200" :timing-function="curve" />
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="cubic = !cubic">切换曲线 / Change curve</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="replay">重新播放 / Replay</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p role="status">Next: {{ cubic ? 'ease-out cubic' : 'linear' }}; current: {{ applied }}.</p>
    <p>切换曲线在下次播放生效；点击重新播放查看效果。Changing the curve applies on replay.</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import type { CountToInstance } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const counter = ref<CountToInstance>()
const cubic = ref(false)
const applied = ref('linear')
const linear = (value: number) => value
const easeOutCubic = (value: number) => 1 - Math.pow(1 - value, 3)
const curve = computed(() => (cubic.value ? easeOutCubic : linear))
function replay() {
  applied.value = cubic.value ? 'ease-out cubic' : 'linear'
  counter.value?.reset()
}
</script>
```

## Animation duration boundaries

Duration is a finite nonnegative number of milliseconds. Zero reaches the target on the next frame. Negative, NaN and infinite values produce development prop diagnostics and safely behave as zero without continuing to request animation frames. Pausing or unmounting before that frame cancels completion. String durations retain parseFloat conversion. reset reads auto-start again. end remains a notification; its listener Promise is not awaited.

## API

String `from`, `to`, `duration`, and `precision` values use parseFloat, so `10px` parses as 10. Invalid or non-finite endpoints produce a warning and use 0. If the difference between finite endpoints overflows, the animation completes on the next frame. `precision` floors the numeric result toward negative infinity without padding zeros and accepts integers in the range [-292, 292]. `auto-start` is read on mount or reset; calling start after completion does not replay until reset.

### CountTo Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------ | ------- |
| `from` | Start value | _number \| string_ | `0` |
| `to` | Target value | _number \| string_ | `0` |
| `duration` | Animation duration (ms) | _number \| string_ | `2000` |
| `precision` | Precision | _number \| string_ | `0` |
| `auto-start` | Whether to start animation automatically | _boolean_ | `true` |
| `timing-function` | Animation curve | _(v: number) => number_ | `-` |

### CountTo Events

| Event | Description | Callback arguments |
| ---------- | -------------- | -------- |
| `end` | Triggered when animation ends | `-` |

### CountTo Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --------- | ---------- | ------------------------ |
| `default` | Custom content | `value: number` |

### CountTo Methods

| Method | Description | Arguments | Returns |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---- | ------ |
| `start` | Start the animation | `-` | `-` |
| `pause` | Pause the animation | `-` | `-` |
| `reset` | Reset the animation. If `auto-start` is `true`, the animation will restart automatically | `-` | `-` |

## Usage notes



Animation pauses on unmount and KeepAlive deactivation and resumes on reactivation. Each instance keeps independent values and animation state.

# Countdown

### Countdown business clock and deactivation

Countdown RAF refreshes business time, not visual interpolation; CSS duration/reduced motion must not alter the clock. Pause and KeepAlive deactivation freeze remaining duration; activation resumes that value without charging inactive time. Inactive time updates/reset may update data and emit change but schedule no RAF; auto-start is deferred to activation, and explicit pause cancels pending resume. Direct inactive start is ignored; disposed start/reset emit and schedule nothing.

Pause and deactivation synchronize the displayed and slot values with the frozen remaining time without emitting another `change`. If the deadline has passed before the next frame, pausing displays zero and resuming emits `end` once.

Pausing or resetting cancels pending countdown updates. A newer start or reset takes precedence over an earlier update. end fires once per round; reset permits a new completion.

### Intro

For real-time display of countdown values, with millisecond precision.

`time` is remaining duration in milliseconds. To align with a deadline, pass `deadline - Date.now()`.

## API

`time` is a duration rather than an absolute deadline; the remaining duration freezes while paused or deactivated by KeepAlive. The default slot receives the five fields days, hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds directly. `change` fires on reset and animation frames and may be frequent. `auto-start` is read on mount or reset; changing it alone does not start or pause. Repeated format tokens are all replaced. Omitted larger units accumulate into smaller units, so `SSS` alone can exceed three digits.

### Countdown Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----- | -------------- | -------- | ---------- |
| `time` | Total time(ms) | _string \| number_ | `0` |
| `format` | Time format | _string_ | `HH:mm:ss` |
| `auto-start` | Whether to auto start count down | _boolean_ | `true` |

### format specification

| Format | Description |
| -- | --- |
| `DD` | Day |
| `HH` | Hour |
| `mm` | Minute |
| `ss` | Seconds |
| `S` | Millisecond, 1-digit |
| `SS` | Milliseconds: 2 digits |
| `SSS` | Millisecond, 3-digit |

### Countdown Events

| Event | Description | Callback arguments |
| ----- | -------------- | -------- |
| `end` | Emitted after countdown ended | `-` |
| `change` | Emitted after countdown changed | `timeData: TimeData` |

### Countdown Slots

| Name | Description | Prop |
| ----- | -------------- | -------- |
| `default` | Custom content | `timeData: TimeData` |

### TimeData format

| Name | Description | Type |
| ---- | ------- | -------- |
| `days` | Remain days | `number` |
| `hours` | Remain hours | `number` |
| `minutes` | Remain minutes | `number` |
| `seconds` | Remain seconds | `number` |
| `milliseconds` | Remain milliseconds | `number` |

### Countdown Methods

Access Countdown through ref to call instance methods.

| Method | Description | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | Start countdown | `-` | `-` |
| `pause` | Pause countdown | `-` | `-` |
| `reset` | Reset the countdown; `auto-start`=`true` restarts it automatically | `-` | `-` |

## Usage notes



SSR renders the initial formatted time. Changing format while paused updates the display. The finish event fires once per round; reset starts another round. Unmounting cleans up animation frames.

# DateRange

Endpoint locks are provided reactively by the local mobile presentation adapter to calendars and wheels. Inherited and current locks are merged and remain intact when switching views or unlocking the other endpoint. The shared draft/confirmation owner has no mobile injection dependency; external model updates and confirm/cancel behavior are unchanged.

Floating panel height follows the visual viewport. A full calendar is visible when space permits; short windows scroll content while keeping actions visible. Override `--mp-date-picker-popover-max-height` to cap the panel (default `100dvh - 32px`). Switching back to default/Maple removes brand overrides.

The embedded example calls `confirm` from the `actions` slot and binds its `disabled` state to the submit button. Selecting a draft does not update the committed value until confirmation. Tightening bounds does not clear the existing model, but an invalid draft cannot be submitted; choose valid endpoints to submit again.
Pure panels do not accept open/default-open, popup-container, placement, trigger-props, placeholder, variant or clearable. disable-confirm controls confirmation; actions receives { confirm, disabled }. Panels support independent app.use installation. Root and date/date-range subpaths export components, Props, Instance, Type, Options and Emits; no standalone date-picker/date-range-picker npm subpath exists.

Installing DateRange also registers DateRangePicker, which is available through the static member `DateRange.Picker`.

Fields configure this through `dateRangePickerProps`.

`abbreviation` (boolean, default `true`) controls abbreviated month labels in the calendar month grid. Set it to `false` for full month names from the active Locale. It does not affect weekday labels, headers, wheel columns, or value formats. Range calendars use the top-level option; nested calendar options cannot override it.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Keep both start/end summaries at the top; click either to switch the edited endpoint. The lower summary shows the current endpoint. Each opening selects the start endpoint (or the end when only the start is locked) and returns the calendar to the start date when available, clamped to date bounds; explicitly controlled picker-value remains owned by the caller. Confirm changes the edited endpoint and cancel preserves committed values.

Summary blocks have no visible start/end captions. The active endpoint is highlighted. Summary buttons and the footer view button support Tab, Enter and Space, with `aria-pressed` indicating selection. Switching views does not commit; cancel restores committed values.

Example source: src/date-range/example/demos/en-US/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<script setup>

const range = ref([])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="lg">
    <mp-date-range v-model="range" placeholder="Select a date range" clearable />
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Time and range rules

### Bounds and endpoint rules

### Intro

Date range selection **panel**. Embed alone when you only need the panel.

The top summary displays start and end values in separate background blocks without captions or a chevron. Clicking a summary selects and highlights the endpoint. Existing endpoints navigate to their date; empty endpoints preserve the current calendar viewport.

- Default `calendarPicker` (`calendar` also applies): a single-selection calendar highlights only the active endpoint, without range bands. A half-hour quick time Picker appears on the right when `show-time` is enabled.
- `presentation="picker"`: date columns for the selected endpoint, using 1/2/3 columns for year/month/date.
- The footer shows the current endpoint label and date. With time enabled, its right side shows the time and a clock button. The button opens the detailed time Picker and changes to a calendar icon for returning to the date view.
- Detailed time uses 2 columns without seconds or 3 with seconds, with matching unit labels. Endpoint switching preserves the view and the other endpoint. Viewing or switching does not round or commit a time.
- Date-only ranges hide the quick time Picker and view button.

Form field: [`DateRange`](llms/en-US/date-range.md). Single date panel: [`DatePicker`](en-US/date-picker).

## Value model and text input

### String models: date, month and month/day ranges

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `format` | Display format or formatter | String models: date, month and month/day ranges, Text entry and panel selection, Date Time |
| `value-format` | Model format, Date or timestamp | String models: date, month and month/day ranges, Date Time |
| `panel-type` | Panel mode: `calendar` `picker` | String models: date, month and month/day ranges |
| `date-fields` | readonly DatePickerField[] | String models: date, month and month/day ranges |
| `disabled` | Disable all or individual endpoints | Text entry and panel selection |
| `input-editable` | Allow text entry; function format/multiple stays readonly | Text entry and panel selection |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


`format` controls display; `value-format` controls the model and emitted value. The examples produce `"2026-09-10"`, `"2026-09"` and `["09-10", "10-10"]` directly. `MM-DD` has no year and parsing uses the current year; it cannot express cross-year ordering or a leap day in a specific year. For those cases retain `YYYY-MM-DD` and map the submitted payload in application code. The default calendar remains page mode and the default timezone remains browser-local.

Example source: src/date-range/example/demos/en-US/string-values.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const date = ref('2026-09-10')
const month = ref('2026-09')
```

## Content and presentation

### Cross-month, DST and endpoint locks

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `value-format` | Model format, Date or timestamp | Cross-month, DST and endpoint locks, Calendar Mode |
| `show-time` | Enable time selection | Cross-month, DST and endpoint locks, Calendar Mode |
| `placeholder` | Placeholder | Type, With FormItem |
| `clearable` | Whether the value can be cleared | Type, With FormItem |
| `disabled` | Disable all or individual endpoints | Cross-month, DST and endpoint locks |
| `input-editable` | Allow text entry; function format/multiple stays readonly | Cross-month, DST and endpoint locks |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/date-range/example/demos/en-US/zoned-range.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import type { CalendarInteractiveMode } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const zone = ref('America/New_York')
const mode = ref<CalendarInteractiveMode>('page')
const lock = ref('none')
const locked = computed(() => [
  lock.value === 'start' || lock.value === 'both',
  lock.value === 'end' || lock.value === 'both',
])
const range = ref<number[]>([])
const days = ref(['2026-10-01', '2026-10-03'])
const presets = [
  ['Cross-month range', 'America/New_York', '2026-10-31T14:30:00Z', '2026-11-02T15:00:00Z'],
  ['Spring gap', 'America/New_York', '2026-03-08T06:30:00Z', '2026-03-08T07:30:00Z'],
  ['Second 01:30', 'America/New_York', '2026-11-01T06:30:00Z', '2026-11-01T07:30:00Z'],
  ['Half-hour DST', 'Australia/Lord_Howe', '2026-10-03T15:00:00Z', '2026-10-03T16:00:00Z'],
]
function preset(index: number) {
  zone.value = presets[index][1]
  range.value = presets[index].slice(2).map(Date.parse)
}
preset(0)
const description = computed(() =>
  range.value
    .map((value) => {
      const date = new Date(value)
      return `${date.toISOString()} · ${new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
        timeZone: zone.value,
        dateStyle: 'short',
        timeStyle: 'long',
      }).format(date)}`
    })
    .join(' → '),
)
</script>

<template>

        item[0]
      }}</mp-button></mp-space
    >
    <p>
      Keep the start/end summaries above the current endpoint summary. Each opening selects the start and returns to its
      date, or edits the end if the start is locked. Locked endpoints cannot change; confirm saves and cancel preserves
      committed values.
    </p>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="days = ['2026-08-01', '2026-08-03']">Six-week month</mp-button>
```

### Calendar Mode

Fields also support Picker wheels. Use `panel-type="calendar | picker"` to switch content; the example also supports date-time ranges. Field `edit-mode` selects the container. Empty calendar summaries display “Select start / Select end”; both valid endpoints are required to confirm.

Example source: src/date-range/example/demos/en-US/calendar-mode.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const mode = ref('calendar')
const showTime = ref(false)
const hideYear = ref(false)
const dateFields = computed(() => (hideYear.value ? ['month', 'day'] : ['year', 'month', 'day']))
const dateRange = ref([])
const dateTimeRange = ref([])
const range = computed({
  get: () => (showTime.value ? dateTimeRange.value : dateRange.value),
  set: (value) => {
    if (showTime.value) {
      dateTimeRange.value = value
    } else {
      dateRange.value = value
    }
  },
})
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" align="stretch" size="lg">
    <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="Selection mode">
      <mp-radio-group
        v-model="mode"
        aria-label="Selection mode"
        :options="[
          { label: 'Calendar selection', value: 'calendar' },
          { label: 'Column selection', value: 'picker' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </mp-form-item>
    <mp-space align="center">
      <span>Include time</span>
      <mp-switch v-model="showTime" aria-label="Include time" />
    </mp-space>
    <mp-space v-if="mode === 'picker'" align="center">
      <span>Hide year column</span>
      <mp-switch v-model="hideYear" aria-label="Hide year column" />
    </mp-space>
    <p>
      Switch between calendar and wheels; enable time to compare date-time ranges. Selections are kept when switching
      modes.
    </p>
    <mp-date-range
      v-model="range"
      :date-fields="dateFields"
      :time-fields="['hour', 'minute']"
      :format="showTime ? 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' : 'YYYY-MM-DD'"
      :value-format="showTime ? 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' : 'YYYY-MM-DD'"
      :panel-type="mode"
      :show-time="showTime"
      :disable-confirm="false"
    />
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Picker wheels stage missing endpoints when opened and show the candidate dates in the summaries, so confirmation does not require scrolling first. An empty range starts at the same valid date/time; a missing endpoint prefers the existing endpoint. Bounds, disabled rules and endpoint locks remain enforced. Without a valid candidate, confirmation stays disabled. Initialization emits no select/change/model events: Confirm saves the draft and Cancel discards it. Returning to the calendar keeps the draft.

Field `edit-mode` selects the `direct` / `popup` container; `panel-type` selects `calendar` / `picker` content. Standalone `DateRangePicker` uses `presentation` for its content mode.

### Endpoint locks

Locking both endpoints does not block parent model updates, but dates and confirmation stay disabled. Unlocking the start afterward restores editing without submitting. Choosing 16 and confirming retains the new end 22 rather than restoring the old end 15.

“External range 18~~22” updates the parent model directly: the pending draft synchronizes and the locked endpoint uses the new model as its baseline. This update adds no selection or confirmation events. Choosing 24 and confirming then commits 18~~24, without restoring the old start.

Locking an endpoint after editing its draft does not authorize that draft to replace the committed endpoint. Confirmation stays disabled while that locked draft differs from the model. Unlocking preserves the draft and restores confirmation, but does not itself submit; explicitly confirm to commit.

An inverted candidate that would move a locked endpoint must be rejected before it changes a nested calendar draft. The committed range and displayed draft remain unchanged; a subsequent valid choice can still be confirmed. Range sorting must never silently relocate a locked endpoint.

This demo explicitly sets disable-confirm=false. With one locked endpoint, a single date choice edits only the unlocked endpoint instead of starting a new two-click range. With both locked, date candidates expose disabled semantics and confirmation is unavailable; unlocking restores editing without submitting.

Use disabled=[startLocked, endLocked] to retain a committed endpoint while editing the other draft. Confirmation writes the model; changing locks alone does not submit. Locking both endpoints blocks selection. This standalone panel does not demonstrate popup cancellation.

Example source: src/date-range/example/demos/en-US/endpoint-lock.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['2026-09-10', '2026-09-15'])
const lockStart = ref(true)
const lockEnd = ref(false)
const confirms = ref(0)
const selections = ref(0)
</script>

<template>
  <section class="date-range-lock-demo">
    <p>
      Local dates: lock one endpoint, edit the other and confirm. Locking both endpoints blocks selection. Lock changes
      do not submit drafts.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="lockStart">Lock start</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="lockEnd">Lock end</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-button html-type="button" @click="value = ['2026-09-18', '2026-09-22']">External range 18~22</mp-button>
    <mp-date-range-picker
      v-model="value"
      presentation="calendar"
      :disable-confirm="false"
      :disabled="[lockStart, lockEnd]"
      @select="selections++"
      @confirm="confirms++"
    />
    <p role="status">Selections：{{ selections }}；Confirmations：{{ confirms }}</p>
    <output>{{ value }}</output>
  </section>
</template>
```

## Interaction and field configuration

### Interaction state comparison

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `panel-type` | Panel mode: `calendar` `picker` | Rejected controlled close, Field viewport and shortcut events, Field and embedded panel |
| `presentation` | Panel mode: `calendar` `picker` `calendarPicker` | Field and embedded panel, Typed passthrough configuration, Copying and editing |
| `open` | Controlled popup visibility | Rejected controlled close, Typed passthrough configuration |
| `input-editable` | Allow text entry; function format/multiple stays readonly | Field viewport and shortcut events, Copying and editing |
| `date-range-picker-props` | Props for `mp-date-range-picker` | Field viewport and shortcut events, Field and embedded panel |
| `value-format` | Model format, Date or timestamp | Interaction state comparison |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Toggle disabled, read-only and error states, then interact with the same instance. Recovery controls remain outside the target; error appearance alone does not validate data.

#### Interaction states

Use this example for booking and query date ranges. Adjust read-only, error feedback and compare the component with the same data. The controls remain available to restore editing; error appearance alone does not run validation.

</details>
