Icon inherits host size/color; use size="20" explicitly for the former fixed mobile appearance. Paper uses surface-default / border-default, with 4px radius, 1px border and system slow (240ms) background transition; content color is inherited. Ripple inherits currentColor and retains its expansion curve, not a text-color role.

Skeleton placeholders use neutral fill2 (state-hover), not an actual hover state. Shimmer uses transparent / surface-default / transparent at layer opacity 0.3. Existing geometry is preserved: content padding 16px; card 160px high, radius 4px, bottom gap 16px; avatar 34px, round, gap 16px; title width 50%, radius 10px; rows 12px high, radius 10px, top gap 10px; shape sizes 36/48/60px and radius 4px. Fullscreen remains a placeholder, not a scrim.

Space physical row/column gaps remain xs 4/4, sm 8/6, md 12/8, lg 16/12, xl 24/16px and reference system spacing. Flex direction does not swap axes. Numeric/custom pair sizes bypass preset tokens. Space has no color responsibilities.

Run node bin/foundation-theme-check.mjs: 448 compiled CSS, override, state-priority and spacing checks across both platforms/brands/modes. Browser motion, full reduced-motion/forced-color coverage and arbitrary custom colors remain outside validation.

## Foundation motion policy

Six new component tokens: hover-transition-duration uses system fast (120ms); icon-spin-duration is 1s; ripple-expand-duration / fade-duration are 200ms / 140ms; skeleton-animation-duration is 1s and transition-duration uses system slow (240ms). Existing paper-transition-duration now uses system slow. Both system duration defaults are value-governed.

Use valid nonnegative CSS time values. Spin/shimmer cycle time is distinct from surface transitions. Icon transition remains a millisecond name-change delay. Ripple expand-duration=200ms controls transform, fade-duration=140ms controls opacity appearing/fading, and cubic-bezier only controls expansion easing. Both platforms share these defaults. Runtime reads resolved transition duration/delay from the actual wave's ownerDocument, including s/ms, repeated lists and all; it does not parse unresolved var() strings.

Ripple's two 250ms policies are minimum display from creation and minimum removal grace after fade starts, not visual durations or total lifetime tokens. Internal creation/activation scheduling remains 30ms/20ms. Fade waits for the later of creation+250ms and actual activation+computed transform time; removal waits max(250ms, computed opacity time). Longer 600ms/800ms overrides are no longer truncated. Explicit 0ms, missing CSS or reduce hiding retain cleanup floors. Expansion timing is sampled at creation/activation and fade timing at fade start; arbitrary later CSS changes or custom animation are not promised.

Release work is scheduled once per wave. Disable/unmount cancels owned timers/direct wave children, without deleting nested directives. Document listeners use the mounted ownerDocument; cross-document adoption rebinding is not covered. Only host Enter/Space and matching keyup or blur participate. The directive does not grant button semantics, accessible names or business click behavior to an ordinary div. Native IAB six-case timing evidence and permanent unit/compiler tests remain separate from touch-device or real OS reduced-motion acceptance.

Reduced motion removes surface transitions, stops built-in Icon spin/shrink, suppresses Skeleton shimmer and decorative Ripple while preserving host content/events and state feedback. Icon subscribes after mount, renders the latest name immediately on preference changes, cancels pending name timers and removes its listener on unmount. SSR never reads window. Explicit rotate orientation is preserved. Limited important declarations enforce preference over inline Icon transition/Ripple opacity and the documented modal, Notification and Message built-in transitions/starting movement; they do not override theme colors or static positioning. Custom animation classes/external SVG animations remain caller responsibilities.

Run check:motion-themes: 96 theme/preference cases, 88 duration overrides and 176 modal active-class consumers, with reduced starting transforms/base transitions checked. Icon runtime tests remain separate. The source inventory records 192 files / 389 CSS motion declaration candidates / 179 runtime-call candidates (including setTimeout scheduling), not selector reachability or acceptance. Compiled CSS and simulated state add zero real OS/browser passes.

The live drift baseline is design-ui/audits/motion-source-inventory.json. Historical evidence snapshots remain unchanged. Line-based hints include non-motion timers; counts are neither defects nor completed acceptance.

BackTop duration (200ms) and easing (quartOut) are JS requestAnimationFrame scroll parameters, not CSS motion tokens. Existing component variables own geometry, color, focus and stacking. Preference comes from the scroll target ownerDocument window; enabling reduce during scrolling jumps to top on the next frame while preserving horizontal scroll, not synchronously on an OS event. Repeated activation, target replacement, deactivation and disposal invalidate even dequeued callbacks. Visibility coalescing is not visual animation. Mocked RAF/iframe-document and SSR tests add no real browser/OS passes.

Drawer's built-in fade/four-side slides and Popup's fade/center scale/four-side pops stop transitions and starting movement under reduce from their own component styles. Scoped !important is a preference override, not a color override. Popup now owns --mp-popup-transition-duration (250ms) and --mp-popup-transition-timing-function (ease), matching Drawer responsibilities without inventing a Cedar Popup counterpart or borrowing Dialog tokens. Set both on the actual shared ancestor/Teleport host to cover outer fade, content and backdrop; style reaches only content and overlay-style only the backdrop. Use valid nonnegative CSS time values; reduce overrides normal motion.

Completion follows actual Transition callbacks, not a fixed 250ms timer. unmountOnClose preserves content and locks during leaving; rapid reopening cancels closing and preserves state. Completion events fire once per valid phase, and callbacks after disposal are ignored. Initial-open mounted notification behavior is unchanged; complete appear timing is not promised. Custom animation or mismatched inner/outer timing is caller-owned. Native IAB default/600ms/0ms, five placements, reopen and disposal checks have separate evidence; explicit 0ms is not an OS reduced-motion test.

Modal contrast covers 16 platform/theme combinations, 72 default and 80 explicit foreground/background pairs; minimum displayed ratio 5.102:1. Composite a translucent surface onto a known opaque backing, then the foreground onto that surface. Compare unrounded text ratios with 4.5; reject poor custom pairs, unknown backing and invalid colors. These direct component overrides do not make root system aliases recompute under arbitrary local overrides. Custom slots, imagery/gradients, status icons and unstyled colors remain caller-owned. See [WCAG text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html) and [interaction animation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html); the latter is AAA, and this batch is not WCAG certification.

Color overrides status. Custom default colors set inline background/border; custom outline colors set border and fallback text on transparent background. Text-color overrides text. ## Field keyboard focus and error state

FieldDecorator no longer draws an extra outer outline. Outline uses the border-state border, filled uses its background and standard uses its underline for --focus/:focus-within feedback. Clear/password/step buttons retain their own keyboard indicators. Readonly remains focusable; error/disabled color priority is preserved. This is not acceptance of native accessibility or focus distinguishability in error states.

Actual Input, Textarea and InputNumber controls use caret-color: currentColor, not field-focus-color/field-error-color. Those tokens and field-border-width retain live label/border/button-outline consumers and must not be deleted because caret/outer-offset paths disappeared. Instance focus-color affects existing supported label/variant routes, not the caret. No production token/default/API changes were made.

Run node bin/field-focus-check.mjs and node --test bin/field-focus-caret.test.mjs for compiled Less, static style imports, retained consumers and three generated sections. Mounted real controls connect the DOM paths. Less/JSDOM is not native keyboard, focus contrast, painting or browser acceptance.

## Declaration ownership and executable consumers (2026-10-12)

Public component defaults belong in the owning `style/token.less`; implementation styles consume them, while internal state variables may remain close to their implementation. This batch relocates 375 public declarations from 34 implementation files. Both Less compilers verified unchanged effective defaults and non-root rules for the relocation.

The inventory compiles `style/index.less` and Less directly imported by `style/index.ts`, including shared selection presentation styles. Runtime consumers require reviewed executable evidence: Watermark reads a variable into its canvas renderer; FloatingPanel, Time clock and TabBar bind variables through inline styles. Comments and theme assignments are not consumers.


Reduced motion must cover JavaScript as well as CSS. Picker commits without transitionend and settles pending selection when the preference changes to reduce. Its columns are listboxes with active options; ArrowUp/Down and Home/End skip disabled items. This does not redefine the additional selected-values checkmark decoration. Time commits a pending draft without blurring before opening, preserving return focus.

Run `check:token-placement`, `check:field-focus`, and `check:theme-contract`. The generated component reference lists exact names, values, conditions and consumer evidence. Compilation and unit tests do not substitute for browser, device or screen-reader acceptance.

A modal focus root must identify its actual tabbable dialog panel, not the outer overlay container. Maple Popup now marks that panel internally. Test opening, nested ownership, Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping and return focus through the real component. The internal data attribute is not a public CSS/API extension point.

## Variable scopes, aliases and Teleport

Same-document portal moves can blur native focus even when the root ref and ownerDocument stay unchanged. After relocation, refocus only the active top modal, preserve its original close-return target and do not steal from higher layers. Read actual activeElement during acceptance; target/color checks, unit tests and pre-fix screenshots are not post-fix native proof. Save screenshots using their actual encoding and record encoded pixel dimensions separately from CSS viewport dimensions, not as native zoom evidence.

The 2026-10-13 post-fix native IAB follow-up passes ten focus-containment checks across both platforms at default/dark, long content and a 320×640 CSS viewport, plus Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping, Enter close and original-opener restoration. Separate evidence lives in design-ui/audits/evidence/portal-focus-2026-10-13/after.json; preserve all eight historical failures. This is not native 200% zoom or Safari/Firefox proof. After runtime resets, resolve the current browser type and ID instead of assuming an old numeric handle still identifies the same browser.

The bounded recheck at 14:12 Shanghai adds zero accepted cases: Chrome supported operations still time out, Safari/Firefox have no supported sessions, and standard Firefox application paths are absent. Each 48-case suite awaits its own restored supported entry; do not extrapolate IAB evidence. Latest blockers: design-ui/audits/evidence/browser-environment-2026-10-13/recheck-1412.json.

Before/after evidence uses a separate screenshot manifest with encoded dimensions and SHA-256 validation. Connection checks, fixture preparation and static rules add no browser passes. Next executable plans are real same-origin iframe and nested-modal keyboard checks in IAB, recording target-document styles, activeElement chains and locks. These plans are not yet executed and do not replace installed browsers, hardware, real OS reduced-motion or screen readers. Detailed scenarios: design-ui/refactors/token-validation/browser/README.md.

Update: real same-origin iframe and nested-modal acceptance are both complete, 8/8 each. Each target Document loads its own component CSS and theme; Teleport neither copies parent variables nor installs parent stylesheets in the frame. Custom absolute-positioned hosts establish positioned, bounded scrolling containers. Capture the original opener along accessible same-origin ancestor focus chains and restore it on close without stealing new outside focus. Do not bypass cross-origin boundaries or claim their coverage. Both focus implementations were repaired without public API/token changes. Final iframe evidence: design-ui/audits/evidence/iframe-2026-10-13/results.json.

Nested acceptance covers both platforms × four themes, child-first and parent-first closure, plus reopening the parent alone. Only the top layer handles Tab/Escape. Child closure returns to its still-visible parent trigger; final closure returns to the original page opener. Closing a lower parent must not steal the live child's focus. Capture ancestor opener chains when opening, and skip hidden, disabled, inert or disconnected candidates on restoration. Both modal-focus copies now fix this case, without new APIs/CSS variables. Scroll locks last until the final user exits; scrollbar compensation is not added twice. This batch uses default retained mounting, same-library nesting and body targets. Background suppression means native keyboard containment and overlay hit-testing, not screen-reader isolation, cross-library coordination, parent-first unmountOnClose removal or cross-origin acceptance. Eighteen native screenshots and per-step evidence: design-ui/audits/evidence/nested-2026-10-13/results.json. Next is reduced-motion rules/contrast preparation; real OS preferences remain separate.

Native zoom and cross-browser acceptance must separately record browser/version, the browser's own visible zoom percentage, actual DOM owner and screenshots. DPR, viewport resizing and CSS zoom/transform are not sufficient proof of native 200% page zoom. Safari/Firefox acceptance requires the corresponding installed browser: connection timeouts, missing installations and missing control surfaces are environment blockers, not component failures or inherited Chromium passes.

Switching a custom host through inline mode back to body must actually leave the old host and restore body/html inheritance, both while open and after reopening. Merely being a descendant of body is insufficient: the old host may also live inside body. Inline modal scroll locks belong to the actual panel document's body, not the remembered Teleport destination.

Constrain floating dimensions to the actual containing block. `100vw` can include the document scrollbar; Cedar Drawer bounds explicit widths with `max-width: 100%`. This is a structural constraint, not a new design token. Long content may scroll inside a panel; arbitrary business slots still own word breaking, typography and paired foreground/background choices.

Custom-property references resolve before inheritance. A child's system override does not automatically recompute component aliases inherited from the document root. [CSS Variables specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-variables-1/#cycles)

| Scenario | Supported customization |
| --- | --- |
| Global theme | Use this library's global ThemeProvider method at the document root |
| Local component | Override its actual public component variables; changing only palette/system roles is not a complete scoped-theme rebuild |
| Local semantic mapping | Redeclare the required component aliases on the same local host |
| Body Teleport | Library declarative portals inherit their owning ThemeProvider through Vue context; third-party portals and services created outside a provider need an explicit host boundary |
| Custom popup-container | Put variables on the existing destination host or actual panel |
| popup-container=false | Retains caller DOM inheritance, with its ancestor clipping, transforms and stacking constraints |
| Iframe HTMLElement | Accepted from its own realm; load CSS and provide variables in the destination document. Selector strings query the caller document only |

For a Maple Popup, override `--mp-popup-content-background-color` and `--mp-popup-content-text-color` together on the host. Cedar Drawer uses `--c-drawer-bg`, `--c-drawer-header-text-color` and `--c-drawer-content-text-color`. For local system-driven customization, declare the component alias on that host too, for example `--mp-popup-content-background-color: var(--mp-sys-color-surface-raised)`. Changing surface-raised alone does not rebind an already inherited root alias.

Panels and overlays are siblings: panel variables cannot reach the overlay through inheritance. Use their common host or the existing separate panel/overlay style props. We do not copy reference computed styles, rewrite all root defaults or create platform-only component counterparts. This clarifies existing behavior; it adds no tokens or automatic full-theme rebinding. Custom background/foreground combinations require their own contrast checks.

`check:portal-scope` verifies real Teleport destinations, state preservation while moving hosts, old-host lock release, foreign-document validation/event ownership and cleanup. It is not a browser rendering test. A local CSS audit must not reevaluate inherited raw root aliases against descendant overrides. Narrow screens, 200% browser zoom, long content and cross-document focus still require browser acceptance.

When an open modal changes destination documents, its event listeners, focus trap, layer registry and scroll locks must follow the actual destination. DOM adoption changes ownerDocument without necessarily changing the Vue element ref: internal rebinding must track the reactive destination too. Moving back and unmounting must clean up old listeners. This adds no public CSS variables; native iframe focus and CSS inheritance still require browser acceptance.

Explicit ThemeProvider `theme="light/dark"` boundaries re-declare palette, system and loaded component aliases through CSS, support nested modes, and carry user overrides to library popup roots. They do not mutate the document theme or scan computed styles. A provider without theme retains its original variable-only override semantics.

# Dialog

With `draggable` enabled, title inputs, textareas, buttons, links with href and editable content retain native pointer behavior and do not start a drag. The ordinary title area remains draggable. In non-centered mode, numeric `top=0` is supported just like the string `0px`.

### Description

Use `<mp-dialog>` for component usage and explicit `Dialog.*` methods for functional usage. Both forms share one configuration model. Callable `Dialog(...)` is not supported.


The sections below follow the same order as the controls in the mobile preview.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Component dialogs show the top-right close button by default.

Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'
import { Dialog, Message } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const basicOpen = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-button status="warning" block @click="basicOpen = true">组件调用</mp-button>
  <mp-dialog
    v-model:open="basicOpen"
    title="兰亭序"
    message="兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水"
    @confirm="Message.success('confirm')"
    @cancel="Message.error('cancel')"
    @closed="Message.info('closed')"
  />
</template>

<style lang="less" scoped>
.mp-button {
  margin-bottom: 11px;
}

.dialog-demo__footer {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 0 12px 12px;
}

:deep(.dialog-demo__body--custom) {
  font-weight: 500;
}

.dialog-demo__body-content {
  padding: 16px 20px;
}
</style>
```

## Invocation and content

### Function Calls

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | Title | confirm box、type icon、form dialog |
| `type` | Semantic icon | confirm box、type icon |
| `message` | Message content; the default slot is also supported | confirm box、type icon |
| `before-close` | Return a boolean/Promise or call done; the first completion wins | form dialog |

Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/function-call.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { Dialog, Message } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const actions = {
  confirm: () => Message.success('confirm'),
  cancel: () => Message.error('cancel'),
  close: () => Message.info('close'),
}
function createBasic() {
  Dialog.open('兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水')
}
async function createAction() {
  const action = await Dialog.open('兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水')
  action && actions[action]?.()
}
function createAndUpdate() {
  const instance = Dialog.open({
    title: '打开对话框',
    message: '兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水',
  })
  setTimeout(() => instance.update({ title: '修改标题' }), 600)
}
function hideButtons() {
  Dialog.open({
    message: '兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水',
    confirmButton: false,
    cancelButton: false,
  })
}
function createOpen() {
  Dialog.open({
    title: '兰亭序',
    message: '兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水',
    onConfirm: () => Message.success('confirm'),
  })
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-button status="primary" block @click="createBasic">基本使用</mp-button>
  <mp-button status="primary" block @click="createOpen">打开对话框</mp-button>
  <mp-button status="primary" block @click="createAndUpdate">动态更新</mp-button>
  <mp-button status="primary" block @click="createAction">处理用户行为</mp-button>
  <mp-button status="primary" block @click="hideButtons">隐藏按钮</mp-button>
</template>

<style lang="less" scoped>
.mp-button {
  margin-bottom: 11px;
}

.dialog-demo__footer {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 0 12px 12px;
}

:deep(.dialog-demo__body--custom) {
  font-weight: 500;
}

.dialog-demo__body-content {
  padding: 16px 20px;
}
</style>
```

### Dialog Form

Use a component dialog for complex forms and validate from `before-close`.

Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/form-dialog.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'
import { Dialog, Message } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const formOpen = ref(false)
const formRef = ref(null)
const formData = reactive({ name: '', email: '' })
async function formBeforeClose({ action }, done) {
  if (action !== 'confirm') {
    done()
    return
  }

  const errors = await formRef.value?.validate()
  if (!errors) {
    done()
    Message.success('表单提交成功')
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-button status="warning" block @click="formOpen = true">对话框表单</mp-button>
  <mp-dialog v-model:open="formOpen" title="对话框表单" :before-close="formBeforeClose">
    <mp-form ref="formRef" :model="formData">
      <mp-form-item field="name" label="姓名" :rules="[(value) => !!value || '该字段为必填项']">
        <mp-input v-model="formData.name" placeholder="请输入姓名" />
      </mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item field="email" label="邮箱" :rules="[(value) => !!value || '该字段为必填项']">
        <mp-input v-model="formData.email" type="email" placeholder="请输入邮箱" />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
  </mp-dialog>
</template>

<style lang="less" scoped>
.mp-button {
  margin-bottom: 11px;
}

.dialog-demo__footer {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 0 12px 12px;
}

:deep(.dialog-demo__body--custom) {
  font-weight: 500;
}

.dialog-demo__body-content {
  padding: 16px 20px;
}
</style>
```

### Programmatic dialog target

Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/service-container.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { getCurrentInstance, h, onBeforeUnmount, ref, shallowRef } from 'vue'
import { Dialog } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import ServiceContainerContent from './service-container-content.vue'

const first = ref<HTMLElement>()
const second = ref<HTMLElement>()
const active = shallowRef<ReturnType<typeof Dialog.open>>()
const context = getCurrentInstance()?.appContext
const result = ref('尚未打开 / Not opened')
function openSample() {
  if (!first.value) {
    return
  }
  active.value?.close()
  const owned: ReturnType<typeof Dialog.open> = Dialog.open(
    {
      title: '服务挂载区域 / Service target',
      popupContainer: first.value,
      content: () =>
        h(ServiceContainerContent, {
          onMove(to: 'A' | 'B') {
            const target = to === 'A' ? first.value : second.value
            if (target) {
              owned.update({ popupContainer: target })
            }
          },
        }),
    },
    context,
  )
  active.value = owned
  result.value = '已打开 / Opened'
  void owned.then((action) => {
    if (active.value === owned) {
      active.value = undefined
      result.value = String(action)
    }
  })
}
onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  active.value?.close()
  active.value = undefined
})
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <mp-button @click="openSample">打开区域 A / Open in A</mp-button>
    <div ref="first" data-service-target="A" style="min-height: 64px; border: 1px dashed currentColor; padding: 12px">
      挂载区域 A / Target A
    </div>
    <div ref="second" data-service-target="B" style="min-height: 64px; border: 1px dashed currentColor; padding: 12px">
      挂载区域 B / Target B
    </div>
    <p role="status">{{ result }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Interaction and customization

### Dragging sessions

Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/draggable.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const open = ref(false)
const draggable = ref(true)
const fullscreen = ref(false)
function keyboard(event: KeyboardEvent) {
  if (event.key.toLowerCase() === 'd') {
    event.preventDefault()
    draggable.value = !draggable.value
  } else if (event.key.toLowerCase() === 'f') {
    event.preventDefault()
    fullscreen.value = !fullscreen.value
  }
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-button @click="open = true">打开拖动示例 / Open drag example</mp-button>
  <mp-dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    :draggable="draggable"
    :fullscreen="fullscreen"
    title="拖动标题 / Drag title"
    @keydown="keyboard"
    @confirm="open = false"
    @cancel="open = false"
  >
    <p>
      拖动标题时按 D 开关拖动，按 F 开关全屏。关闭后可以重新打开。Drag the title, press D to disable dragging or F for
      fullscreen, and reopen after closing.
    </p>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="draggable = !draggable">{{
        draggable ? '停用拖动 / Disable drag' : '启用拖动 / Enable drag'
      }}</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="fullscreen = !fullscreen">{{
        fullscreen ? '退出全屏 / Exit fullscreen' : '进入全屏 / Fullscreen'
      }}</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p role="status">{{ draggable ? '允许拖动 / Drag enabled' : '拖动已停止 / Drag stopped' }}</p>
  </mp-dialog>
</template>
```

## Async actions and closing

### Async Close

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `before-close` | Return a boolean/Promise or call done; the first completion wins | Async close, before hooks and callback compatibility |
| `title` | Title | async close |
| `message` | Message content; the default slot is also supported | async close |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


`beforeClose` supports boolean/Promise results and the existing done callback. Functional calls default to `simple: true` and `closable: false`.



Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/async-close.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'
import { Dialog, Message } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const loadingOpen = ref(false)
function buttonLoadingClose({ action }, done) {
  if (action !== 'confirm') {
    done()
    return
  }

  setTimeout(() => {
    done()
    Message.success('confirm')
  }, 1000)
}
function createAsyncClose() {
  Dialog.open({
    message: '兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水',
    beforeClose: buttonLoadingClose,
  })
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-button status="primary" block @click="createAsyncClose">异步关闭</mp-button>
  <mp-button status="warning" block @click="loadingOpen = true">按钮 Loading</mp-button>
  <mp-dialog
    v-model:open="loadingOpen"
    title="兰亭序"
    message="兰亭临帖 行书如行云流水"
    :before-close="buttonLoadingClose"
  />
</template>

  padding: 16px 20px;
```

### Before hooks and callback compatibility

`beforeClose({ action }, done, context)` is the only hook entry. No new closeGuard/confirmGuard/cancelGuard prop is introduced.


A before hook that only logs synchronously must explicitly return true; synchronous undefined means callback completion is still pending. Old async callbacks that returned `Promise<void>` without calling done now complete on Promise resolution.


Example source: src/dialog/example/demos/en-US/guard-protocol.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { DialogBeforeClose } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const open = ref(false)
const mode = ref('promise')
const allowed = ref(false)
const status = ref('')
const check: DialogBeforeClose = (payload, done, { signal }) => {
  status.value = `Waiting: ${payload.action}`
  if (mode.value === 'done') {
    setTimeout(() => {
      status.value = allowed.value ? 'Allowed' : 'Rejected'
      done(!signal.aborted && allowed.value)
    }, 500)
    return
  }
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) =>
    setTimeout(() => {
      status.value = allowed.value ? 'Allowed' : 'Rejected'
      resolve(!signal.aborted && allowed.value)
    }, 500),
  )
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" align="stretch">
    <mp-switch v-model="allowed" />
    <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="mode">
      <mp-radio-group
        v-model="mode"
        aria-label="mode"
        :options="[
          { value: 'promise', label: 'Promise' },
          { value: 'done', label: 'done callback' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </mp-form-item>
    <mp-button @click="open = true">Open</mp-button>
    <mp-dialog v-model:open="open" :before-close="check" @guard-error="status = 'Error'">
      <template #default
        ><mp-button v-if="false" @click="open = true">Confirm action</mp-button
        ><span v-else>Close with beforeClose</span></template
      >
    </mp-dialog>
    <p role="status">{{ status }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```


Promise and done share a single completion state: false/done(false) rejects; true/done() allows; a resolved Promise&lt;void&gt; allows. The first completion wins. Errors emit guard-error; cancellation/unmount invalidates late completion. Synchronous void retains the callback protocol and waits for done on these close/confirm guards.


Cancellable hooks use `(payload, done, context)`: closure payloads contain `{ action }`, change/commit payloads contain `{ value, previousValue }`, and Popup uses `{ reason }`. Context provides `signal` and an optional original `event`. Return a boolean/Promise, or call done()/done(false). Synchronous void waits for done; Promise&lt;void&gt; allows the operation. First completion wins. Pending state controls loading/disabled automatically. Cancellation invalidates stale results. Button refs are not exposed.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Content, titles and action spacing use logical start/end. External popovers inherit their source direction. Closing, confirmation, cancellation and uncommitted state are unchanged by direction switches.

## Usage notes

### Async operation feedback
Awaited before-* hooks show loading feedback and aria-busy. Rejection or failure restores interaction; repeated input does not start the same operation again. Ordinary event return Promises do not participate in loading.

Programmatic notification callbacks do not control task completion. Service selection/closing results settle independently of callback errors, and closing completion always releases the owned host. Exceptions still propagate through the caller or Vue error channel; returned Promises do not control loading or closing.

### Dragging and cancellation
Title dragging is controlled only by the initiating primary pointer. Disabling `draggable`, closing, entering fullscreen, losing pointer capture or owner-window focus, deactivation and unmount all end the gesture and release listeners and capture. Reenabling requires a new gesture; the previous pointer cannot resume it. Disabling preserves the current offset; fullscreen and the existing post-close reset restore defaults. Listeners belong to the title element's document.

### Programmatic dialog mount targets
Function calls honor `popupContainer` from explicit configuration or `setDefaultOptions`, using the component's selector/HTMLElement resolution and missing/invalid-selector fallback to body. The default targets body; `false` renders inline in the service's own body host. `handle.update({ popupContainer })` moves the same dialog and preserves content state and app context. Closing removes teleported content and its service host, independently of notification callback results. A custom container controls DOM attachment; layout still follows Dialog positioning and its containing block.

## API

### Dialog Props

Dividers follow Card and are disabled by default. Enable them separately with `top-divider` and `bottom-divider`; each appears only when its corresponding header or footer exists. Dialog also supports these options in simple mode and service calls, using `topDivider` and `bottomDivider` in service configuration.

### Dialog Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | --------------- |
| `update:open` | Open state changed | `boolean` |
| `open` / `opened` | Opening starts / opening animation completes | `-` |
| `close` / `closed` | Closing starts / closing animation completes | `-` |
| `confirm` | Confirmation closing succeeds | `Event` |
| `cancel` | Cancellation closing succeeds | `Event` |
| `click-overlay` | `MouseEvent` | `MouseEvent` |
| `key-escape` | ESC pressed | `KeyboardEvent` |

The `close` button, overlay, ESC and `close()` all use action `close` without an additional `cancel` event.

Built-in buttons, overlay, Escape, footer methods and instance confirm()/cancel() request beforeClose. Instance close(), returned handle close(), Dialog.close() and parent open=false are direct commands that bypass guards; a controlled parent still decides whether to accept update:open(false). Direct closing retires pending guards so late results cannot close a reopened instance. close does not mean leave completion; observe closed/onClosed. Maple Popup close()/requestClose() instead return `Promise<boolean>` for guarded requests.

### Dialog Slots / Methods

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- |
| `default` | Content | `-` |
| `title` | Title | `-` |
| `footer` | Show footer | `confirm`, `cancel`, `close` |

Instances expose `confirm()`, `cancel()` and `close()`.

### Dialog Methods

All open methods accept `DialogConfig | string` and return `Promise<DialogAction | void> & DialogReturn`.
Function-based Dialog calls default to simple layout (`simple: true`) with the top-right close button hidden (`closable: false`). Explicit options or global defaults can override both.

| Method | Default behavior |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `Dialog.open(config)` | Ordinary dialog |
| `Dialog.confirm(config)` | `type: 'warning'`, simple layout |
| `Dialog.alert(config)` | No cancel button; overlay/ESC closing disabled |
| `Dialog.info/success/warning/error(config)` | Corresponding status, no cancel button, simple layout |
| `Dialog.close()` | Close the latest functional dialog |
| `Dialog.setDefaultOptions(config)` | Set default programmatic options |
| `Dialog.resetDefaultOptions()` | Reset default programmatic options |

`DialogConfig` matches camelCase component props and additionally supports renderable `content`/`title`/`message`/`footer` plus `onOpen`/`onOpened`/`onClose`/`onClosed`/`onConfirm`/`onCancel`/`onClickOverlay`/`onKeyEscape`.

`DialogReturn.close()` closes this dialog; `DialogReturn.update(config)` updates mutable configuration. After installation, `this.$dialog` exposes the same API.

```ts
type DialogAction = 'confirm' | 'cancel' | 'close'
type DialogType = 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'
```

## CSS Variables

Normal and simple modes grow with their content up to `90dvh`, falling back to `90vh` when unsupported. Beyond this height, only the body scrolls; the title and actions remain visible. Override the limit with `--mp-dialog-max-height` or `dialogStyle.maxHeight`; fullscreen mode uses the full viewport height. A custom footer also stays inside the non-scrolling actions container.

Variables use `--mp-`, e.g. `--mp-dialog-width`, `--mp-dialog-background`, `--mp-dialog-border-radius`, `--mp-dialog-simple-width`, `--mp-dialog-fullscreen-width` and `--mp-dialog-close-button-color`.

Color semantics match Cedar: `--mp-dialog-background` uses `surface-raised`; `--mp-dialog-overlay-background` controls scrim; titles/body use primary content and close controls secondary content. `--mp-dialog-status-{info|success|warning|danger}-color` uses readable content-info/success/warning/danger, not status fill. Business themes should override component variables; shared themes override system variables. Mobile borderless geometry/layout remain independent.

The backdrop consumes `sys-color-scrim` through the Dialog component variable. Dialog uses its own backdrop variables. Set a per-instance backdrop variable via `overlay-style`; a variable on the panel (`dialog-style`) does not inherit to its sibling backdrop. Explicit `overlay-style.backgroundColor` wins. Teleported content needs variables on its actual DOM ancestors. Dark themes inherit the same semantic colors; geometry remains platform-specific. Status icons use readable content colors.

Variables are grouped by purpose: background/overlay-background for panel/scrim; border-* for panel/divider borders; title-* for title typography; content-* for body typography; actions-* for actions; close-button-* for the close button; status-* for semantic icons; simple-*/fullscreen-* for mode dimensions; animation-* for enter/leave motion. width/margin-top control ordinary panel layout. Internal drag/position variables are not public customization points.

# Divider

Separate content sections in lists and layouts.

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`. Horizontal text start/end follows reading order; vertical start/end remains top/bottom. Inset controls along-line indentation and spacing controls perpendicular margins. Paired horizontal inset and vertical spacing uses logical start/end. Vertical borders use inline start; hairline, border type and aria-orientation retain their meaning. Direction changes preserve content nodes.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Separate adjacent content sections.

Example source: src/divider/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div>
    <p>内容上方 / Before</p>
    <mp-divider />
    <p>内容下方 / After</p>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Layout and arrangement

### Vertical Divider

| `description` | Description text; the default slot takes priority | Vertical Divider |

### Line size, style and color

Compare thickness or insets, line style and color. Text and custom content remain separate.

<details>
<summary>Configuration details and limits</summary>

#### Spacing & Inset

Compare five presets, numbers, CSS lengths and asymmetric pairs. The vertical example shows how spacing follows orientation.

#### Color, Thickness & Opacity

Customize the line using `color`, `thickness` and `opacity`. Zero opacity preserves layout; `hairline` takes priority over `thickness`.

#### Line Style

Compare solid, dashed, dotted and double lines using `type`. Use a `thickness` of at least 3px for a visible double line.

</details>

## Content and layout

### Content height and minimum thickness

Explicit thickness accepts finite numbers greater than or equal to 1. hairline still takes priority, using half the theme width. Values below 1 (including zero and negative values), and non-finite values, are ignored and use the theme width; development builds warn.

Multiline descriptions and custom content occupy their full height, including spacing=0. Subsequent content stays below the divider.

Example source: src/divider/example/demos/content-flow.vue

```vue
<template>
  <section class="divider-flow-demo">
    <h4>1px：最小显式线宽 / Minimum explicit width</h4>
    <div class="flow-sample">
      <mp-divider
        data-min-line
        :thickness="1"
        :spacing="0"
        description="内容仍正常占位 / Content stays in normal flow"
      />
      <p>后续正文 / Following content</p>
    </div>
    <h4>4px：多行文字 / Multiline content</h4>
    <div class="flow-sample">
      <mp-divider
        data-multiline
        :thickness="4"
        :spacing="0"
        description="分区标题支持换行，并为后续内容保留完整空间 / A wrapping section title reserves its full height"
      />
      <p>后续正文 / Following content</p>
    </div>
    <h4>默认插槽 / Custom content</h4>
    <div class="flow-sample">
      <mp-divider data-custom-content :spacing="0"
        ><span class="flow-content">第一行 / First line<br />第二行 / Second line</span></mp-divider
      >
      <p>后续正文 / Following content</p>
    </div>
    <p>thickness ≥ 1；hairline 优先，使用主题线宽的一半。hairline takes priority and halves the theme width.</p>
  </section>
</template>
<style scoped>
.flow-sample {
  max-width: 280px;
}
.flow-sample p {
  margin: 0;
}
.flow-content {
  padding: 12px 0;
}
</style>
```

## Usage notes

### Configuration

Presets read the active platform theme. Text spacing is 16px on desktop and 8px on mobile.

## API

### Divider Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | Horizontal/vertical orientation of the divider itself, default horizontal; does not control text alignment | `horizontal` \| `vertical` | `horizontal` |
| `type` | Line style | `solid` \| `dashed` \| `dotted` \| `double` | `solid` |
| `text-align` | Text position along the line; start/end follow logical direction | `start` \| `center` \| `end` | `center` |
| `description` | Description text; the default slot takes priority | `string` | — |
| `inset` | Inset along the line: left/right horizontally, top/bottom vertically | `DividerSize` | — |
| `spacing` | Outer spacing across the line: top/bottom horizontally, left/right vertically | `DividerSize` | `md` |
| `thickness` | Finite line width of at least 1px; omission uses the 1px theme default; hairline takes precedence | `number` | — |
| `hairline` | Scale the theme line width by half; 0.5px with the default theme | `boolean` | `false` |
| `color` | Line color; defaults to the theme border color | `string` | — |
| `opacity` | Opacity of the entire divider, including text, from 0 to 1; zero preserves layout | `number` | — |

### Spacing values

`DividerSize = number | string | [number | string] | [number | string, number | string]`

`inset` controls the ends of the line; `spacing` controls the outer gap between the line and adjacent content. Both accept presets `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, a number in px, a CSS length, or an array. A scalar or single-item array applies to both ends; `[start, end]` sets each end separately. Array entries are lengths, not preset names.

| Direction | inset array order | spacing array order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| horizontal | Inline start/end inset; right/left in RTL | Top/bottom margin |
| vertical | Top/bottom inset | Inline start/end margin; right/left in RTL |

`inset` has no inset by default; `spacing` defaults to the platform’s `md` spacing. Presets use platform theme tokens, so pixel values may differ.


Development checks cover orientation, text-align, type, spacing shape, thickness and opacity. Invalid enums use defaults; invalid inset produces no indentation, invalid spacing falls back to md, and invalid opacity does not override styles. opacity must be finite and within 0–1. Arrays accept one or two lengths and no preset names. Finite negative margins and CSS var/calc expressions remain supported; browsers parse their CSS syntax.

### Divider Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Custom divider content; overrides description |

# Drag

### Intro

Make the element draggable freely.

## Basic examples

### Basic Use

Example source: src/drag/example/demos/basic-use.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div class="drag-demo-surface">
    <mp-drag
      ref="drag"
      style="left: 16px; top: 16px"
      :boundary="{ top: 12, right: 12, bottom: 12, left: 12 }"
      :popup-container="false"
```

## API

### Drag Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `axis` | Allowed drag axis, default xy: x is horizontal only, y vertical only, xy both. Not an expansion side | _DragAxis_<br>`'x' \| 'y' \| 'xy'` | `xy` |
| `attraction` | Attraction direction, optional value is `x` `y` `xy` | _DragAttraction_<br>`'x' \| 'y' \| 'xy'` | `-` |
| `disabled` | Disables dragging only; ordinary click still notifies. Disabling during a drag cancels the gesture and retains the current position. | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `boundary` | Four physical boundaries; replacement or in-place updates automatically clamp an already-dragged position. | _{ top?: number \| string, bottom?: number \| string, left?: number \| string, right?: number \| string }_ | `{ top: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0, right: 0 }` |
| `z-index` | Drag element z-index | _string \| number_ | `90` |
| `popup-container` | The location where the dragged element is mounted | _PopupContainer_ | `body` |

With `popup-container`=`false`, draggable elements stay local rather than teleporting to `body` and are positioned/constrained against the nearest positioned ancestor. Give it `position: relative` for local dragging in cards/panels.

### Input and boundary rules

Touch dragging only. Physical x/y axes do not swap in RTL. Mouse input only produces ordinary clicks. Supply button/link semantics in business content; the root is not automatically a button.

Boundaries support finite numbers, numeric strings and px, rem, vw, vh, vmin and vmax. Negative values expand the allowed range. Percentages, em, calc, var and nonfinite values are unsupported, warn in development and use 0. Invalid axis falls back to xy; invalid attraction disables snapping. Boundary changes cancel the gesture and clamp the current position. Cancellation and disabling do not snap; normal touchend does.

### Drag Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| `click` | Ordinary click notification; suppressed during dragging and for one frame after ending. Promises are not awaited. | `event: Event` |

### Drag Methods

| Method | Description | Arguments | Returns |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---- | ------ |
| `resize` | Manually reread the visual position and clamp after host layout changes. Boundary prop changes need no manual call. | `-` | `-` |
| `reset` | Clear the gesture and translation, restoring the initial position defined by external styles. | `-` | `-` |

### Drag Slots

| Name | Description | Prop |
| --------- | -------------- | ---- |
| `default` | Drag element's content | `-` |


Wait for snapping animation to finish before calling resize, to avoid capturing an intermediate visual position. Both methods return void. Window resizing resolves relative units again and clamps; call resize for other host layout changes.

```ts
import { Drag } from '@maple-design/ui-vue/drag'
import type { DragProps, DragInstance, DragAxis, DragAttraction, DragBoundary, PopupContainer } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
```

## Usage notes

### Rows and content boundaries

expand-trigger supports only click. Invalid values produce Vue prop validation warnings in development and do not enable button semantics, click or keyboard expansion. line-clamp accepts finite numbers or numeric strings of at least one row and floors decimals. Values below one, nonfinite values and invalid strings warn and fall back to ordinary single-line mode, clearing old multiline styles. Prefer plain text or inline content without independent interactions. The default Tooltip still does not detect actual overflow and remains focusable with Tab when enabled. Custom tooltip content and controlled expansion remain unchanged.

## API

### Ellipsis Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expand` | Controlled expansion | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `default-expand` | Initial uncontrolled expansion | `boolean` | `false` |
| `expand-trigger` | Enable click / Enter / Space toggling | `'click'` | `—` |
| `line-clamp` | Positive line count; omitted or invalid means single line | `number \| string` | `—` |
| `tooltip` | Tooltip configuration; false disables it | `boolean \| TooltipProps` | `true` |

Providing `expand` makes the component request updates from its parent rather than changing controlled state. When omitted, internal state is used, initialized once by `default-expand`. Tooltip follows its own width and trigger defaults; display does not depend on measured overflow. Touch callers can include `click` in `tooltip.trigger` explicitly. External class/style/width apply directly to the text node.

### Ellipsis Events / Slots

- `update:expand(expand: boolean)`: the new state requested by user interaction; external updates do not emit it.
- `default`: body text.
- `tooltip-content`: tooltip content. Without it, tooltip.content takes precedence, then body text; content is not concatenated twice.
- Keyboard: expandable text supports Enter / Space; tooltip-enabled text is focusable with Tab. No public instance methods.

## Types

```ts
import type { EllipsisProps, EllipsisInstance, EllipsisExpandTrigger } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
```

### Imports and event types

The subentry default component and the named components from the subentry and root are the same component. Props includes actual listener parameters. Events remain notifications and do not await returned Promises. Use only the documented instance methods.

```ts
import Ellipsis, { Ellipsis as NamedEllipsis } from '@maple-design/ui-vue/ellipsis'
import { Ellipsis as RootEllipsis } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import type { EllipsisProps, EllipsisInstance } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import type { EllipsisProps as SubEllipsisProps } from '@maple-design/ui-vue/ellipsis'
const options: EllipsisProps = { 'onUpdate:expand': (expanded: boolean) => String(expanded) }
```

<details>
<summary>Configuration details and limits</summary>

#### Custom Image and Copy

Customize the illustration with the `image` slot or default slot copy. Use `image-url` for an image source.

#### Extra Action

Reload updates a local attempt counter and description only; it does not call a service. Provide your own request and result state for real reload behavior.

Add actions with the `extra` slot.

</details>

Example source: src/empty/example/demos/content-comparison.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { proxyRefs as demoProxyRefs, ref } from 'vue'

const scene1 = demoProxyRefs(
  (() => {
    const attempts = ref(0)
    return { attempts }
  })(),
)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="demo-comparison">
    <section class="demo-comparison-case demo-comparison-case--1" data-comparison-scene="extra-slot">
      <h4><span lang="zh-CN">操作按钮</span><span lang="en-US">Extra Action</span></h4>
      <mp-empty :description="scene1.attempts ? 'No data. Local refresh completed.' : 'No data, please reload'">
        <template #extra>
          <mp-button status="primary" @click="scene1.attempts++">Reload</mp-button>
          <p aria-live="polite">Local refresh attempts: {{ scene1.attempts }}</p>
        </template>
      </mp-empty>
    </section>

    <section class="demo-comparison-case demo-comparison-case--2" data-comparison-scene="custom-image">
      <h4><span lang="zh-CN">自定义图片和文案</span><span lang="en-US">Custom Image and Copy</span></h4>
      <mp-space direction="column" :size="24">
        <mp-empty>
          <template #image>
            <m-icon-alert-circle />
          </template>
          No data, please reload!!
        </mp-empty>
        <mp-empty image-url="/cat.jpg" alt="空状态图片" description="自定义图片和文案" />
      </mp-space>
    </section>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped lang="less">
.demo-comparison {
  display: grid;
  gap: 24px;
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 100%;
}
.demo-comparison-case {
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 100%;
```

| `--mp-empty-size-xs` | `80px` | `font-size`, `height`, `width` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-empty-description-color: var(--mp-sys-color-content-tertiary);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

<!-- Source: docs/emptyValues.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/emptyValues -->

# Empty recognition, clear output and reading placeholders

## Choose the setting for your task

| Task                                                       | Setting                                    | Example                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| Emit null, -1 or another supported value when clearing     | empty-value / emptyValue                   | Clear icon and manual deletion        |
| Treat API marker -1 as unselected and missing for required | empty-values / emptyValues                 | Empty markers and required validation |
| Keep an empty string as a valid All option                 | Exclude the empty string from empty-values | Valid empty-string option             |
| Show '-' or No data for empty reading content              | empty-text / emptyText                     | Reading placeholders and inheritance  |

Each prop has one job. emptyValue defines clear output, emptyValues defines empty identity, and emptyText defines reading text. They do not derive one another. Rendering or configuration changes do not write the model or change controlled ownership.

## Learn by scenario

### Clear icon and manual deletion

Clear with the icon to produce null. Restore the initial value and delete all text with Backspace to produce `''`. The model output quotes strings so the two outcomes are visible.

Example source: src/input/example/demos/en-US/empty-value.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive } from 'vue'

const model = reactive({ text: 'Hello' as string | null })
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>The clear icon produces null; Backspace to empty produces an empty string.</p>
    <mp-form :model="model" layout="vertical">
      <mp-form-item field="text" label="Keyword">
        <mp-input v-model="model.text" edit-mode="direct" clearable :empty-value="null" />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-button @click="model.text = 'Hello'">Restore initial value</mp-button>
    <p>
      Current model: <output>{{ JSON.stringify(model.text) }}</output>
    </p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Manual deletion is an input event and does not invoke emptyValue. Form reset restores recorded initial values. See [Input value model and interaction](#/en-US/input).

### Valid empty-string option

All has value `''` and remains selected. emptyValues excludes it with `[null, undefined]`, while emptyValue independently clears to null. Clear, then choose All again and compare model outputs.

Example source: src/select/example/demos/en-US/empty-value.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'

const model = reactive({ status: '' as string | null })
const multiple = ref(['active'])
const optional = ref<string | undefined>('active')
const options = [
  { value: '', label: 'All' },
  { value: 'active', label: 'Active' },
]
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>All uses an empty string as a valid option value. Clearing produces null.</p>
    <mp-form :model="model" layout="vertical">
      <mp-form-item field="status" label="Status">
        <mp-select
          v-model="model.status"
          :options="options"
          edit-mode="direct"
          clearable
          :empty-values="[null, undefined]"
          :empty-value="null"
        />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-button @click="model.status = ''">Choose All</mp-button>
    <p>
      Current model: <output>{{ JSON.stringify(model.status) }}</output>
    </p>
    <mp-form layout="vertical">
      <mp-form-item label="Multiple: clear to []">
        <mp-select
          v-model="multiple"
          :options="options"
          edit-mode="direct"
          multiple
          clearable
          :empty-value="() => []"
        />
        <output>{{ JSON.stringify(multiple) }}</output>
      </mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item label="Single: clear to undefined">
        <mp-select v-model="optional" :options="options" edit-mode="direct" clearable :empty-value="() => undefined" />
        <output>{{ String(optional) }}</output>
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Select preserves empty-string options by default. Explicit settings align field and required semantics. Deleting the search query does not delete selection. See [Select value model and linked fields](#/en-US/select).

### Empty markers and valid zero

Include -1 in emptyValues when an API uses it for missing data; also set emptyValue=-1 if clearing should emit it. The initial input is blank while the model stays -1. Set it to 0 to see a valid zero, then clear back to -1.

Example source: src/input-number/example/demos/en-US/empty-value.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'

const model = reactive({ quantity: -1 as number | null | undefined })
const restored = ref<number | null | undefined>(12)
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>-1 means missing and renders blank; 0 remains a valid number. Clearing produces -1.</p>
    <mp-form :model="model" layout="vertical">
      <mp-form-item field="quantity" label="Quantity">
        <mp-input-number
          v-model="model.quantity"
          edit-mode="direct"
          clearable
          :empty-values="[null, undefined, -1]"
          :empty-value="-1"
        />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="model.quantity = 0">Set to 0</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="model.quantity = -1">Set to -1</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p>
      Current model: <output>{{ String(model.quantity) }}</output>
    </p>
    <p>This field clears to 0 without treating 0 as missing.</p>
    <mp-form layout="vertical">
      <mp-form-item label="Clear restores valid zero">
        <mp-input-number v-model="restored" edit-mode="direct" clearable :empty-value="0" />
        <output>{{ String(restored) }}</output>
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

0 and false are valid by default; do not classify both with `!value`. InputNumber manual empty commits retain numeric parsing rules and may emit undefined. See [InputNumber numeric input and formatting](#/en-US/input-number).

### Empty markers and required validation

Form provides `[null, undefined, -1]` to its fields, while Select defines clear output -1. Validate the initial value, select a department and validate again, then clear and validate the missing value.

Example source: src/form/example/demos/en-US/empty-values-validation.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'

const model = reactive({ department: -1 as number | null | undefined })
const form = ref()
const result = ref('Not validated')
const options = [
  { value: 1, label: 'Engineering' },
  { value: 2, label: 'Product' },
]
async function validate() {
  const errors = await form.value.validate()
  result.value = errors ? 'Required error' : 'Valid'
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>Validate the initial -1, then select a department and validate again. Clearing restores -1.</p>
    <mp-form ref="form" :model="model" layout="vertical" :empty-values="[null, undefined, -1]">
      <mp-form-item field="department" label="Department" required>
        <mp-select v-model="model.department" :options="options" edit-mode="direct" clearable :empty-value="-1" />
      </mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <mp-button @click="validate">Validate</mp-button>
    <p role="status">{{ result }}</p>
    <p>
      Current model: <output>{{ String(model.department) }}</output>
    </p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

emptyValue=-1 alone does not identify -1 as empty; emptyValues alone does not change clear output. Required runs on validation calls or configured triggers, not merely because an input looks blank. See [Form validation and submission](#/en-US/form).

### Reading placeholders and inheritance

Initially, Name inherits Form's default `'-'`, Code uses the FormItem override, Nickname uses the field override, and Quantity remains 0. Change Form's text to No data: only inheriting empty fields change. Toggle reading/editing and observe the unchanged model.

Example source: src/form/example/demos/en-US/empty-text.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'

const reading = ref(true)
const emptyText = ref('-')
const model = reactive({
  name: null as string | null,
  code: null as string | null,
  nickname: null as string | null,
  quantity: 0 as number | null | undefined,
})
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>
      Initially, reading mode shows “-” for Name, overrides for Code and Nickname, and the valid number 0 for Quantity.
    </p>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="reading = !reading">Toggle reading/editing</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="emptyText = 'No data'">Use “No data”</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="emptyText = '-'">Use default “-”</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <mp-form :model="model" layout="vertical" :read-pretty="reading" :empty-text="emptyText">
      <mp-form-item field="name" label="Name: inherits Form"><mp-input v-model="model.name" /></mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item field="code" label="Code: FormItem override" empty-text="Unassigned"
        ><mp-input v-model="model.code"
      /></mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item field="nickname" label="Nickname: field override" empty-text="Unassigned"
        ><mp-input v-model="model.nickname" empty-text="Anonymous"
      /></mp-form-item>
      <mp-form-item field="quantity" label="Quantity"><mp-input-number v-model="model.quantity" /></mp-form-item>
    </mp-form>
    <p>
      Current model: <output>{{ JSON.stringify(model) }}</output>
    </p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Precedence is **Field > FormItem > Form > '-'**. Explicit emptyText=`''` renders blank; custom read slots win. This text is separate from an input placeholder and never becomes validation or submitted data. See [Form field presentation and interaction](#/en-US/form).

## Rules and boundaries

### emptyValues: recognize the current model

Field settings override FormItem, which overrides Form. Lists replace rather than merge. Unconfigured text fields recognize null, undefined and the empty string; Select and numeric fields retain their nullish defaults.

Scalars use includes; 0 and false remain valid by default. Objects use reference identity. Empty arrays always mean an empty collection; nonempty `[null]` does not. An explicit empty list removes additional scalar markers without turning an empty collection into a selection.

Fixed state controls and Upload consume the policy for reading and required without rewriting checked state, bounds or transport. Invalid dates and unfinished numeric drafts retain domain rules.

### emptyValue: define clear output

Omission preserves component defaults. Check each component's supported types: Input declares string/null and corresponding factories. Where undefined output is supported, such as InputNumber and date/time fields, use `:empty-value="() => undefined"`; a directly bound undefined leaves the fallback in place.

Factories run during actual clear actions, not initialization, reading or validation. Arrays follow existing independent-result rules. Output is not automatically classified as empty: clearing to 0 can restore valid data.

Some shared editing panels fall back to defaultValue. Their clear action updates a draft; confirmation commits and cancellation discards it. Clear icons, manual deletion, removing the last item and reset retain component-specific behavior.

### Required and custom rules

With explicit emptyValues, built-in required follows the primary field policy. Unconfigured validation retains each library's behavior; Cedar b-validate and Maple function/Zod validation need not agree on every boundary value.

Custom validators, Zod, min/max and enum receive raw values. A UI marker -1 does not make `number().positive()` accept it; business schemas define optional handling. Recognition also does not imply business validity.

false is valid by default, so required does not mean must agree. Classify false explicitly or require true in a custom agreement rule. Prefer one primary field per FormItem and separate independently validated values.

### Controlled ownership

Business emptiness differs from ownership. Adding -1 or removing undefined from emptyValues does not change existing controlled predicates. Do not replace every internal undefined check with isEmpty: ownership, failed parsing, invalid dates and business markers have distinct meanings.

## Relationship to Element Plus

The separation follows [Element Plus configuration](https://element-plus.org/en-US/component/config-provider.html#empty-values-configurations) and [useEmptyValues](https://github.com/element-plus/element-plus/blob/dev/packages/hooks/use-empty-values/index.ts). Our emptyValue serves the role of valueOnClear; no synonym is added.

We use Form/FormItem inheritance and action-time factories, preserving component defaults and collection rules. Array deep equality, clear-output warnings and ConfigProvider integration are not copied.

# VSCode Extension

### Intro

For a better development experience, we built a `VSCode plugin`.

### Features

- 🛠️ &nbsp;Support syntax hints and quick completion for all components.
- 🛠️ &nbsp;Support document address preview and quick jump for all components.
- 🛠️ &nbsp;Support frame selection of code snippets to quickly open `Playground`.
- 🛠️ &nbsp;Support full icon preview for icon components.
- 🌍 &nbsp;Support switching between Chinese and English.

Moving the mouse to the component name will display the document address of the component, which can be clicked to jump, and it also directly displays the properties, events and slots of the component in the form of a table.

<img src="https://maplejs.org/vscode/2.png" style="width: 100%; display: mp-block; border-radius: 4px; margin-top: 16px">

<img src="https://maplejs.org/vscode/4.png" style="width: 100%; display: mp-block; border-radius: 4px; margin-top: 16px">

# Fab

### Intro

The floating action button component, press to display a group of action buttons.

The live preview starts expanded. Actions show a Message and collapse the menu. Changing direction moves the button to a compatible edge. Use click on touch devices; hover is intended for a mouse.

The local preview uses `fixed=false` and `popup-container=false`. The drag example keeps the default `fixed=true` to enable dragging and uses `popup-container=false` to keep the button inside the preview container. Drag boundaries use the container dimensions. Dragging uses touch gestures.

The preview and button remain visible when toggling dragging. Switching it off stops dragging. The preview scrolls with the page.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/fab/example/demos/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { Message } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const demoText = {
  basic: '基础用法',
  preview: '实时预览',
  previewHint: '点击悬浮按钮展开或收起，点击动作按钮查看提示。下方参数实时生效。',
  dragHint: '拖拽模式：按钮位于屏幕角落，可用触摸拖动；关闭拖拽回到预览区。',
  hiddenState: '按钮已隐藏',
  expandedState: '动作已展开',
  collapsedState: '动作已收起',
  profile: '查看用户',
  complete: '标记完成',
  notify: '发送提醒',
  type: '主题色按钮',
  trigger: '触发方式',
  direction: '动作菜单弹出方向',
  position: '触发器位置',
  default: '默认',
  primary: '主要',
  info: '信息',
  success: '成功',
  warning: '警告',
  danger: '危险',
  drag: '拖拽',
  disabled: '禁用',
  elevation: '海拔效果',
  triggerToggle: '触发器显示/隐藏',
  actionsToggle: '动作菜单展开/收起',
  customTrigger: '自定义触发器',
  toggle: '切换',
}

const open = ref(false)

function runAction(action) {
  Message.info(demoText[action] ?? String(action))
  open.value = false
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="fab-demo-stage">
    <p>点击悬浮按钮展开或收起，点击动作按钮查看提示。下方参数实时生效。</p>
    <mp-fab v-model:open="open" :fixed="false" :popup-container="false" status="primary">

        <template #icon><m-icon-user-circle-fill /></template>
      </mp-button>
      <mp-button
        status="success"
        variant="tonal"
        :elevation="false"
        aria-label="标记完成"
        @click="runAction('complete')"
      >
        <template #icon><m-icon-checkbox-marked-circle-fill /></template>
      </mp-button>
      <mp-button status="warning" variant="tonal" :elevation="false" aria-label="发送提醒" @click="runAction('notify')">
        <template #icon><m-icon-bell-fill /></template>
      </mp-button>
    </mp-fab>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.fab-demo-stage {
  position: relative;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  min-height: 250px;
  padding: 16px;
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 1px dashed var(--mp-color-border-2);
  border-radius: 8px;
}
.fab-demo-stage p {
  max-width: calc(100% - 72px);
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--mp-color-text-3);
  font-size: 13px;
  line-height: 1.5;
}
</style>
```

```vue
      ></mp-button>
    </mp-fab>
  </div>
</template>
```

### visible versus v-if

Use `<mp-fab v-if="showFab" />` when destroying the instance is acceptable; visible is optional. v-if=false destroys FAB, its drag state and action children; remounting reads defaultOpen again. `:visible="showFab"` retains the instance and internal state while hiding its trigger and actions. FAB uses Drag/Teleport, so visible controls the actual content internally; avoid relying on v-show on the Teleport component. The action menu itself still uses open.

The default icon button has a localized name; pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to customize it. When actions exist, the trigger also exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Bind the `triggerProps` slot value to a custom focusable button; the application owns its disabled state.

Hover mode supports Enter/Space on the trigger. It stays open while focus remains on the trigger or actions after the pointer leaves, and closes when both pointer and focus leave. Escape requests close and returns focus to the trigger when focus was in the actions. Action clicks do not close automatically; control `v-model:open` in the application when desired.

`open` and `close` are interaction requests which a controlled parent may reject. External model changes and disabling do not necessarily emit matching request events. `opened`/`closed` receive the action element after the animation. Position and placement use physical sides without automatic flipping; `FabDrag` is a boolean or an object with `axis`, `attraction`, and `boundary`.

## Usage notes

### Configuration

When importing on demand, also import `@maple-design/ui-vue/fab/style`, or use the full stylesheet `@maple-design/ui-vue/style`.

## API

`open`/`update:open` control the action menu through `v-model:open`. Without binding, `defaultOpen` initializes internally maintained state. `visible` controls the whole component without changing saved menu-`open` state. The `trigger` slot receives `{ open, triggerProps }`; bind `triggerProps` to its actual focusable button.

### Fab Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------- |
| `v-model:open` | Whether to activate the action menu | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `default-open` | Initial uncontrolled action-menu state, read only at creation | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `visible` | Whether to show the whole widget | _boolean_ | `true` |
| `drag` | Drag component props, for deep customization (support `axis` `attraction` `boundary`） | _FabDrag_ | `false` |
| `status` | Semantic status, optional values are `default` `primary` `secondary` `tertiary` `info` `success` `warning` `danger` | _string_ | `primary` |
| `position` | Corner of the button itself within the screen or positioning container, default bottom-right. Corner values use vertical-first spelling | _string_ | `bottom-right` |
| `placement` | Action-menu placement relative to the button, default top; no automatic flipping. Does not change the button position | _string_ | `top` |
| `trigger` | Trigger: `click`/`hover` | _string_ | `click` |
| `disabled` | Whether disabled | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `color` | trigger color | _string_ | `-` |
| `closed-icon` | Inactive trigger icon | _string_ | `plus` |
| `open-icon` | trigger icon when open | _string_ | `close` |
| `closed-icon-size` | Inactive trigger icon size | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `open-icon-size` | Trigger icon size when open | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `fixed` | Whether to use fixed positioning, set to `false` to enable absolute positioning (absolute positioning prohibited from dragging) | _boolean_ | `true` |
| `z-index` | Same as css z-index, used for custom trigger level | _string \| number_ | `90` |
| `top` | Same as css top, for custom trigger position | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `bottom` | Same as css bottom, for custom trigger position | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `left` | Same as css left, for custom trigger position | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `right` | Same as css right, for custom trigger position | _string \| number_ | `-` |
| `safe-area` | Whether to respect the vertical and horizontal safe areas at the corner selected by position | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `popup-container` | element to which the component mounts | _TeleportProps['to'] \| false_ | `body` |
| `elevation` | Elevation level, options `true` `false` and level of `0-24` | _number \| boolean_ | `true` |

### Fab Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | Triggered when the trigger is clicked, not triggered when `disabled` state is `true` | `open: boolean, event: Event` |
| `open` | Fires when the action menu is activated and opened | `-` |
| `opened` | The action region finished opening | `element: Element` |
| `close` | Triggered when the action menu is deactivated and closed | `-` |
| `closed` | The action region finished closing | `element: Element` |

### Fab Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | Action menu | `-` |
| `trigger` | Trigger | `{ open: boolean, triggerProps: FabTriggerProps }` |

## CSS Variables

The following CSS variables support customization with [ThemeProvider](#/en-US/theme-provider).

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-fab-action-border-radius` | `50%` | `border-radius` |
| `--mp-fab-action-margin` | `6px` | `margin` |
| `--mp-fab-action-size` | `40px` | `height`, `min-width`, `width` |
| `--mp-fab-actions-padding` | `10px 0` | `padding` |
| `--mp-fab-bottom` | `16px` | `bottom` |
| `--mp-fab-left` | `16px` | `left` |
| `--mp-fab-right` | `16px` | `right` |
| `--mp-fab-top` | `70px` | `top` |
| `--mp-fab-transition-standard-easing` | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` | `transition` |
| `--mp-fab-trigger-active-icon-size` | `22px` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-fab-trigger-border-radius` | `50%` | `border-radius` |
| `--mp-fab-trigger-inactive-icon-size` | `26px` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-fab-trigger-size` | `56px` | `height`, `min-width`, `width` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-fab-action-border-radius: 50%;
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->
