## Reading direction

Linear progress grows from inline start, and active/indeterminate animation follows reading direction. Percentages, numeric values and ring angles do not reverse. Reduced-motion preferences still apply.

## Usage notes

### Configuration

Determinate circular success/danger states show completion/failure icons, including xs. The text slot overrides these; ARIA numeric values remain.

### Layout updates

Circular `stroke-width` is resolved in the component CSS context, including `1em`, `calc()`, `var()` and percentages; a percentage is relative to the circle diameter. Font, variable and size changes update the geometry, and stroke width is capped at 99% of the diameter.

## API

### Progress Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode | Line or circle | `line \| circle` | `line` |
| percent | Decimal 0–100; numeric strings supported; invalid values become zero, out-of-range values clamp | `number \| string` | `0` |
| size | xs/sm/md/lg/xl or CSS length; line thickness / circle diameter | `ProgressSize`<br>`'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| number \| string` | `md` |
| stroke-width | Overrides thickness, numbers in px | `number \| string` | Follows size |
| steps | Line segments, floored and clamped to 0–1000; ignored when indeterminate | `number` | `0` |
| status | default/primary/secondary/tertiary/info/success/warning/danger; default becomes success at 100 unless indeterminate | `ProgressStatus`<br>`'default' \| 'success' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `default` |
| color | Solid or gradient stops; overrides status | `string \| Record<string, string>` | — |
| track-color | Background track color | `string` | — |
| buffer-color | Remaining line track decoration, not a second progress value | `ProgressColor` | — |
| track | Show track and buffer decoration | `boolean` | `true` |
| show-text | Show text; xs circle hides text | `boolean` | `true` |
| text-class | Text container class | `string` | — |
| rotate | Clockwise angle from twelve o'clock | `number` | `0` |
| animation | Determinate continuous line shimmer | `boolean` | `false` |
| indeterminate | Unknown progress; omits aria-valuenow | `boolean` | `false` |

### Size semantics

| size | xs | sm | md | lg | xl |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear thickness / default circular stroke in px | 2 | 3 | 4 | 6 | 8 |
| Circular diameter in px | 16 | 48 | 64 | 80 | 96 |

`size=12` / `size="12"` means 12px; `size="2rem"`, `"50%"` and `"calc(100% - 2px)"` retain CSS lengths. Custom linear size controls thickness; custom circular size controls diameter. stroke-width always takes precedence for thickness. Invalid/nonpositive lengths fall back to md. Percentage circular diameters require a definite parent width. All five presets are implemented; xs circular progress hides text. Cedar inherits omitted size from ConfigProvider; Maple defaults to md.

### Progress Slots

| Slot | Prop | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| text | `{ percent: number }` | Takes precedence over default |
| default | `{ percent: number }` | Custom display text |

Indeterminate progress shows an ellipsis by default; use the text slot for business text. The component does not mutate values or emit updates. Provide `aria-label` for the business task. All built-in animations respect reduced-motion settings.

## Types

Exports `ProgressProps`, `ProgressInstance`, `ProgressSize`, `ProgressMode`, `ProgressStatus`, `ProgressColor` and runtime `progressProps`.

# PullRefresh

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/pull-refresh/example/demos/en-US/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { onBeforeUnmount, onDeactivated, ref } from 'vue'

const data1 = Array(30).fill('List item')
const data2 = Array(30).fill('New list item')
const isRefresh = ref(false)
const data = ref(data1)
let refreshTimer

function cancelRefresh() {
  clearTimeout(refreshTimer)
  refreshTimer = undefined
  isRefresh.value = false
}
onBeforeUnmount(cancelRefresh)
onDeactivated(cancelRefresh)

function refresh() {
  clearTimeout(refreshTimer)
  refreshTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    refreshTimer = undefined
    data.value = data.value[0] === 'List item' ? data2 : data1
    isRefresh.value = false
  }, 2000)
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="pull-refresh-demo__scroller">
    <mp-pull-refresh v-model="isRefresh" :success-duration="2000" @refresh="refresh">
      <mp-cell v-for="(item, index) in data" :key="index" border> {{ item }} {{ index + 1 }} </mp-cell>
    </mp-pull-refresh>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.pull-refresh-demo__scroller {
  height: 360px;
  overflow: auto;
  overscroll-behavior: contain;
}
</style>
```

`animation-duration` and `success-duration` accept finite nonnegative milliseconds or numeric strings; zero is valid, and invalid values use the respective default. Without `success-bg-color`, the indicator uses the theme background; without `success-color`, it uses the success color token rather than the normal inline color.

A selector target must exist when bound; invalid or missing targets throw. Changing `target` rebinds and settles the indicator to the current model. No imperative refresh method is part of the public contract.

Provide a keyboard-accessible button that invokes the same refresh operation, with `disabled` and `aria-busy` derived from business state. A separate `role="status"` region can announce completion or failure. `refresh` is a notification: accept `update:modelValue` true and set it to false when the operation completes; returned promises do not control state.

## API

### Value and default value

Use ordinary `v-model`. `modelValue` is refresh-loading state; the parent still sets false after async completion. `defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled state once without later resets. Explicit binding wins, without initialization `update:modelValue`.

### PullRefresh Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | Loading status | `boolean` | `-` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled refresh state, read once | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | Disable pull-to-refresh | `boolean` | `false` |
| `target` | Scroll container. Defaults to the nearest scrollable ancestor | `string \| HTMLElement` | `-` |
| `animation-duration` | Rebound animation duration (ms) | `number \| string` | `300` |
| `success-duration` | Success state duration (ms) | `number \| string` | `2000` |
| `bg-color` | Indicator background | `string` | `-` |
| `color` | Indicator color | `string` | `-` |
| `success-bg-color` | Success indicator background | `string` | `-` |
| `success-color` | Success indicator color | `string` | `-` |

### PullRefresh Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh` | Fired when refresh starts | `-` |
| `update:model-value` | Fired when loading status changes | `(value: boolean)` |

### PullRefresh Slots

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | List content |

## CSS Variables

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-pull-refresh-background` | `#fff` | `background-color` |
| `--mp-pull-refresh-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-brand)` | `color` |
| `--mp-pull-refresh-icon-size` | `25px` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-pull-refresh-size` | `40px` | `height`, `width` |
| `--mp-pull-refresh-success-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-success)` | `color` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-pull-refresh-background: #fff;
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

# Quick start

Start with an existing Vue 3 + Vite project and render a button with explicit imports. See [Import on demand](#/importOnDemand?language=en-US) for automatic imports and other integration options.

## 1. Install

```shell
# npm
npm i @maple-design/ui-vue @maple-design/icons-vue

# pnpm
pnpm add @maple-design/ui-vue @maple-design/icons-vue
```

## 2. Render a component

Import the button and its styles in `App.vue`:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Button } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import '@maple-design/ui-vue/button/style'
</script>

<template>
  <Button status="primary">Confirm</Button>
</template>
```

The component style entry includes the required foundation styles. Run your project’s development command to see the button.

## Next steps

- [Import on demand](#/importOnDemand?language=en-US): configure automatic imports, manual imports or full registration.
- [Defaults and global configuration](#/defaultsCustomization?language=en-US): configure component defaults, overlay z-index and ripple behavior.

### Optional global reset

Component styles do not reset page elements or set the `body` font. To opt in to normalize.css, import it in your application entry:

```ts
import '@maple-design/ui-vue/reset.css'
```

Configure fonts, page backgrounds, and global box sizing in your application.

# Radio

### Intro

Basic demos follow the site language without changing business values or selection. Group demos cover accepted/rejected updates, readonly state and asynchronous option labels; removing options does not clear the model. Use `direction="column"` on the outer Space and `orientation="vertical"` on the choice group itself.

Single selection among multiple options.

## Reading direction

Radio groups inherit source dir. Horizontal keys follow visible direction in RTL and skip disabled options; vertical keys and Home/End keep logical order. Radio and button variants retain one Tab entry. Changing direction does not change the selected value.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

### Group state and readonly

A defined `model-value` is controlled: rejected updates do not change the selection. `default-value` initializes uncontrolled state only. Only Group emits `update:model-value → change(value, event?)` and notifies FormItem once; children do not duplicate these notifications.
Native checked values, ARIA state and selection styles stay synchronized with the model. A rejected group selection restores both the previous and clicked inputs; label, Enter and Space activation each propose one update.
Group inherits `disabled`, `readonly` and `error` from the form when omitted. An explicit `false` overrides the form; children cannot bypass a locked group.

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/group-state.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const accepted = ref('a')
const proposed = ref('')
const readonly = ref(false)
const options = [
  { label: 'Device A', value: 'a' },
  { label: 'Device B', value: 'b' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <div>
      <p>Uncontrolled: default-value initializes only</p>
      <mp-radio-group :default-value="'a'" :options="options" />
    </div>
    <div>
      <p>Controlled: parent accepts updates {{ accepted }}</p>
      <mp-radio-group v-model="accepted" :options="options" :readonly="readonly" />
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="readonly = !readonly">{{ readonly ? 'Unlock' : 'Read only' }}</mp-button>
    </div>
    <div>
      <p>Parent rejects updates; proposals only {{ proposed }}</p>
      <mp-radio-group :model-value="''" :options="options" @update:model-value="proposed = $event" />
    </div>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Button sizes

Both libraries support `variant="button"`. RadioGroup supports `xs / sm / md / lg / xl`; size changes button height, not circular icons. Unset size inherits the form/global setting and finally defaults to md. The group variant takes precedence over its children.

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/button-sizes.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">

  { label: 'Week', value: 'week' },
  { label: 'Month', value: 'month' },
]
</script>
<template>
  <section class="radio-demo">
    <div v-for="size in sizes" :key="size">
      <p>{{ size }}</p>
      <mp-radio-group variant="button" :size="size" default-value="week" :options="options" :aria-label="size" />
    </div>
    <p>Vertical and readonly</p>
    <mp-radio-group
      variant="button"
      orientation="vertical"
      readonly
      default-value="day"
      :options="options"
      aria-label="Readonly period"
    />
  </section>
</template>
```

## Options and value model

### Standalone values and methods

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `value` | Option identity | Standalone values and methods, Set State Value |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value | Standalone values and methods |
| `readonly` | Readonly; inherits Form when omitted | Standalone values and methods |
| `disabled` | Disabled; inherits Form when omitted | Standalone values and methods |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Radio accepts string, number, boolean or null; null means unselected. Selecting an already selected radio does not deselect it; the parent can clear it with null.
Use `default-value` only to initialize uncontrolled state. Rejected controlled proposals preserve the current selection. The event order is `update:model-value → change(value, event?)`; imperative calls have no native event.
Methods are `select()`, `focus(options?)` and `blur()`. Disabled controls cannot select or focus; readonly controls can focus but cannot change value. Enter on keydown and Space on keyup activate only the local control. Repeated Enter is ignored; blur/deactivation cancels pending Space activation.

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/control-value.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const control = ref()
const value = ref(null)
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>null means unselected; repeated selection does not deselect. Current value:{{ value }}</p>
    <mp-radio ref="control" v-model="value" :value="false">Select the false option</mp-radio>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="control?.select()">Select</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="control?.focus()">Focus</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="value = null">Reset</mp-button>
    </mp-space>

    <p>
      Read-only controls can receive focus; disabled controls cannot be edited. Enter/Space activates only this control.
    </p>
    <mp-radio :default-value="true" readonly>Read only</mp-radio>
    <mp-radio :default-value="true" disabled>Disabled</mp-radio>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Option data and labels

Both libraries accept primitive options or objects. `field-names` maps `label/value/disabled/readonly/indeterminate`; read-only options remain focusable but cannot change the value. Checkbox indeterminate is presentation only.
The `label` slot receives `{ data, checked }` and takes precedence over a label render function `(data, checked) => VNodeChild`. Data is normalized and retains business fields; source objects are not mutated. Missing labels fall back to the value's text.
Providing `options` replaces the default slot, including `[]`; omit it to use the default slot. Values must be strings, finite numbers or booleans; missing/invalid values and duplicate values of the same type are skipped (first occurrence wins). `false`, `0`, `''` and `'0'` remain distinct. Option changes never rewrite the model.
RadioGroup defaults to `null` (no selection). Set `model-value` to `null` to clear; `''` is a valid option, not an empty-state marker.

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/option-data.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { h, ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref<string | number | boolean | null>(null)
const fields = { value: 'id', label: 'name', disabled: 'unavailable', readonly: 'locked' }
const options = ref([
  { id: false, name: 'Boolean false' },
  { id: 0, name: 'Number zero' },
  { id: '', name: 'Empty string' },
  { id: 'locked', name: 'Read-only option', locked: true },
  { id: 'disabled', name: 'Disabled option', unavailable: true },
])
const renderOptions = [
  {
    value: 'render',
    label: (_data: unknown, checked: boolean) => h('strong', checked ? 'Selected' : 'Rendered label'),
  },
]
</script>

<template>
  <section class="option-demo">
    <p>Field mapping and label slots. Read-only options can receive focus; disabled options cannot be edited.</p>
    <mp-radio-group v-model="value" :options="options" :field-names="fields" orientation="vertical">
      <template #label="{ data, checked }">{{ data.label }} {{ checked ? '✓' : '' }}</template>
    </mp-radio-group>
    <p>Current value: {{ JSON.stringify(value) }}</p>
    <mp-button @click="value = null">Clear</mp-button>
    <p>
      Labels also support render functions. Omitting options uses the default slot; passing [] renders an empty group.
    </p>
    <mp-radio-group :options="renderOptions" />
  </section>
</template>

<style scoped>
.option-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 12px;
}
.option-demo p {
  margin: 0;
}
</style>
```

### Keyboard navigation

Tab enters the selected item, or the first enabled item. Arrow keys cycle; Home / End move to the first / last enabled item. Readonly items receive focus without changing the value. Navigation is local to the group and does not intercept embedded buttons.

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/keyboard-navigation.vue

```vue

  { label: 'Email', value: 'email' },
  { label: 'Readonly', value: 'locked', readonly: true },
  { label: 'Disabled', value: 'disabled', disabled: true },
  { label: 'SMS', value: 'sms' },
]
</script>
<template>
  <section class="radio-demo">
    <p>
      Tab enters the group. Arrow keys cycle; Home / End focus the first / last item. Readonly items receive focus
      without changing the value.
    </p>
    <mp-radio-group v-model="value" :options="options" aria-label="Notification channel" />
    <p>Current value：{{ value }}</p>
    <mp-button @click="value = null">Clear</mp-button>
  </section>
</template>
```

## Control and content customization

### Native control and custom icons

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ----------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `checked-color` | Checked color | Native control and custom icons, Modify Icon And Color |
| `value` | Option identity | Native control and custom icons |
| `icon-size` | Icon size | Native control and custom icons |
| `readonly` | Readonly; inherits Form when omitted | Native control and custom icons |
| `unchecked-color` | Unchecked color | Modify Icon And Color |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Both libraries render a native radio input. Use name on the group for native form submission; aria-label/input-attrs address the input. Managed type, checked, disabled and tabindex take precedence over input-attrs. Icon slots replace only the icon; #radio replaces the complete visible content, so provide an accessible name.

```vue
        <template #unchecked-icon><span aria-hidden="true">○</span></template>
        Email
      </mp-radio>
      <mp-radio value="sms">SMS</mp-radio>
```

### Modify Icon And Color

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/set-style.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive, toRefs } from 'vue'

const values = reactive({
  value: false,
  value2: false,
  value3: false,
  value4: false,
  value5: false,
  value6: 0,
  value9: 0,
  optionValue: 0,

<template>
  <mp-radio v-model="value3" unchecked-color="var(--mp-color-warning)" checked-color="var(--mp-color-danger)">
    <template #unchecked-icon>
      <m-icon-heart-half-full size="24px" />
    </template>
    <template #checked-icon>
      <m-icon-heart-fill size="24px" />
    </template>
    <template #default> Current value: {{ value3 }} </template>
  </mp-radio>
</template>

<style lang="less" scoped>

  margin-top: 10px;
}

.button {
  margin-right: 10px;
}

.space {
  height: 40px;
}
</style>
```

## Async options

### Asynchronous options

Enable Manual responses to start real local promises instead of the default timer. Load twice and resolve newest/oldest in either order: only the current request version may replace options or end loading. Removing options invalidates the outstanding version but preserves the selected business value; old tasks remain available to resolve manually. Applied/Ignored/Pending expose this behavior. Loading and responses do not count as user changes. Versioning and pending cleanup belong to this Demo's business loader, not an automatic Radio network-race guarantee; no external service is called.

Loading/removing options or updating the external value never emits reverse updates. Selected values absent from the current options are retained. Selecting the current value again does not emit change. false, zero and empty string retain their identity.

This demo simulates loading with an 800ms local delay. Set Device A or clear the selection while waiting: arriving options reflect the latest model without increasing the user-change count. Removing options while loading cancels the pending task so stale options do not reappear.

Arrow keys can still select existing options while loading. Reloading the same option values preserves focus. Keep the loading-status node stable to avoid remounting the group when the message changes; activating the current value again does not emit another change.

Example source: src/radio/example/demos/en-US/async-options.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { onDeactivated, onUnmounted, ref, shallowRef } from 'vue'

const value = ref('remote')
const options = ref([])
const loading = ref(false)
const changeCount = ref(0)
let pendingTimer
const manual = ref(false)
const waiting = shallowRef([])
const applied = ref(0)
const ignored = ref(0)
let version = 0
let sequence = 0

function cancelPending() {
  version++
  if (pendingTimer !== undefined) {
    clearTimeout(pendingTimer)
  }
  pendingTimer = undefined
  loading.value = false
}

function load() {
  cancelPending()
  loading.value = true
  const ticket = version
  const id = ++sequence
  const complete = () => {
    if (ticket !== version) {
      ignored.value++
      return
    }
    applied.value = id
    options.value = [
      { label: 'Remote device', value: 'remote' },
      { label: 'Device A', value: 'a' },
      { label: 'Disabled device', value: 'locked', disabled: true },
    ]
    pendingTimer = undefined
    loading.value = false
  }
  if (manual.value) {
    new Promise((resolve) => {
      waiting.value = [...waiting.value, { id, resolve }]
    }).then(complete)
  } else {
    pendingTimer = setTimeout(complete, 800)
  }
}

function settle(latest) {
  const jobs = [...waiting.value]
  const job = latest ? jobs.pop() : jobs.shift()
  waiting.value = jobs
  job?.resolve()
}

function cleanup() {
  cancelPending()
  const jobs = waiting.value
  waiting.value = []
  jobs.forEach((job) => job.resolve())
}

function remove() {
  cancelPending()
  options.value = []
}

onDeactivated(cleanup)
onUnmounted(cleanup)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space class="radio-async-demo" direction="column">
    <p>Values survive loading and removing options:{{ value }}</p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="manual" @change="remove">Manual responses / 手动返回</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="load">Load options</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="remove">Remove options</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="value = 'a'">Set Device A</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" @click="value = null">Clear selection</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" :disabled="waiting.length === 0" @click="settle(false)">Resolve oldest load</mp-button>
      <mp-button size="sm" :disabled="waiting.length === 0" @click="settle(true)">Resolve newest load</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p aria-live="polite">
      {{
        loading
          ? 'Loading. Remove the options before completion to cancel this request.'
          : 'Loading preserves the current selection and keyboard focus.'
      }}
    </p>
    <mp-radio-group v-model="value" :options="options" @change="changeCount++" />
    <p>User changes：{{ changeCount }}</p>
    <p role="status">Applied: {{ applied }} · Ignored: {{ ignored }} · Pending: {{ waiting.length }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Native input attributes and keyboard cancellation

Native `id`, `form`, `required`, constraints, aria/data attributes and keyboard listeners belong to the actual input. Class/`style` and other shell attributes remain on the label. Generated native IDs are stable and unique, and an external label can target an explicit `id`. HTML `required` participates in native browser `form` validation, separately from Form business rules.

Once / Capture / Passive native listener modifiers stay on the input rather than firing from interactive slot children. Native preventDefault can veto Enter / Space activation and RadioGroup arrow navigation; canceled Space leaves no delayed release action. Checked, disabled, input type and group Tab navigation remain component-managed.

input-attrs preserves native attribute aliases. An alias overrides a matching top-level native attribute, but cannot override component-managed state. Radio's checked state is managed through native `checked`; supplied `aria-checked` does not override it. The component still manages tabindex, retaining one Tab entry per RadioGroup.

## Usage notes

### Native attributes and appearance

| Component | Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------ | ------------------- | --------- |
| Radio / RadioGroup | name | Native field name; child overrides group | string | undefined |
| Radio | aria-label | Native control accessible name | string | undefined |
| Radio | input-attrs | Native input attributes | InputHTMLAttributes | undefined |

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

The `options` prop accepts an array or `(query, { signal }) => array/Promise`. The component manages loading, cancellation and stale-result isolation; failures emit load-error. Single/multiple groups initialize with an empty-string query, searchable fields reload when the query changes, and root loading for tree fields remains independent of existing load-more child loading.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

## API

### Parameters, presentation clearing and mount-time boundaries

orientation accepts horizontal / vertical and falls back to horizontal after invalid-value diagnostics. max belongs to CheckboxGroup: valid values are finite nonnegative integers, zero forbids new choices, and omission is unlimited. Existing external values are never truncated. Invalid JavaScript callers retain the existing normalization after diagnostics: negatives become zero, fractions are floored, NaN is unlimited, and Infinity remains unlimited.

icon-size accepts positive lengths. Numbers and numeric strings use px, including positive fractions such as 0.5. Invalid, nonpositive or nonfinite values diagnose and fall back to the theme; the Divider minimum of 1 does not apply. Business styles determine the final resolved value of CSS expressions.

uninject-group-context decides group participation at mount. Changing it later does not reinject; change the key or remount. An isolated control still participates in Form. clearable / empty-value apply only to explicit presentation-layer clearing; native unchecking still proposes false or removes the array value and never uses empty-value. Ordinary event Promises do not participate in waiting; before-commit uses payload / done / context only when saving a deferred edit.

During an explicit options request both group roots announce aria-busy and emit one load-error on failure. No loading prop or extra graphic is added, and loading/failure never proposes a new model.

Ordinary circular Radio icons do not scale with Group.size. The five sizes apply to button presentation; circular dimensions use icon-size or the theme. The radio slot replaces the complete visible circular content while retaining the native input. Button presentation uses the default label and ignores the radio slot.

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

`ChoiceValue = string | number | boolean`；`CheckboxModel = boolean | ChoiceValue[] | null`；`RadioModel = ChoiceValue | null`。

# Rate

### Intro

Used to rate things.

| `empty-icon` | Unchecked icon | Customize Rating Icon Style |
| `color` | Active color or increasing per-icon threshold color map | Customize Rating Icon Style |
| `empty-color` | Inactive color | Customize Rating Icon Style |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Set the selected and unselected icons through the `icon` and `empty-icon` properties.

### Listen Event

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue'

const scores = reactive({
  score: 3,
  score1: 3,
  score3: 3,
  score4: 3,
  score6: 3.5,
  score7: 3,
  score8: 3,
  score10: 3,
  score12: 3.5,
})
function handleChange(score) {
  Message({
    content: `click ${score}`,
    position: 'top',
  })
}
</script>
```

```vue
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

`before-commit({ value, previousValue }, done, { signal })` can reject an overlay save. FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps the editor open on failure. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. Use `#read="{ value, text }"` to customize display. See the full field comparison in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

Inside FormItem, when `label-attrs.for` matches Rate's `id`, the rating control uses the form label as its accessible name; explicit `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` takes precedence. Clicking the default native label focuses an enabled rating control; preventing the label click default cancels that focus.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Rate Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------- |
| model-value | Controlled value, including zero; external updates emit no events | number | undefined |
| default-value | Initial uncontrolled value; subsequent changes do not reset it | number | 0 |
| count | 0 < count <= 1000; floors to at least one; invalid or oversized counts fall back to five | number \| string | 5 |
| allow-half | Enable half-point steps | boolean | false |
| clearable | Click the current score again to clear; keyboard boundaries do not clear | boolean | false |
| grading | Fixed five-face rating; overrides slots and icon props | boolean | false |
| disabled | Disable interaction; inherits Form when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| readonly | Focusable but not editable; inherits Form when omitted | boolean | undefined |
| aria-label | Accessible business label | string | undefined |
| size | Icon dimension: number/numeric string in px, otherwise CSS length | number \| string | Style default |
| gap | Icon spacing: number/numeric string in px, otherwise CSS length | number \| string | Style default |
| color | Active color or increasing per-icon threshold color map | string \| Record<string, string> | undefined |
| empty-color | Inactive color | string | undefined |
| disabled-color | Disabled color, overriding active/inactive colors | string | undefined |
| icon | Checked icon | string \| Component | Filled star |
| half-icon | Half icon | string \| Component | Half star |
| empty-icon | Unchecked icon | string \| Component | Empty star |
| ripple | Click ripple | boolean | true |

size/gap do not accept xs/sm/md/lg/xl presets. Omitted or invalid values retain style defaults. Size must be positive; gap accepts zero and negative gaps fall back to the style default. CSS var/calc/min/max/clamp lengths are supported. Scores normalize to 0–count in steps of 1 or 0.5. Non-finite scores display zero without changing the external value.

### Rate Events

| Event | Arguments | Description |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| update:model-value | value: number \| null | User produces a new value |
| change | value: number \| null | Confirmed new value; no duplicate for equal values |
| hover-change | value: number \| null | Hover preview; resets to zero on leave/blur/disabled/readonly |

### Rate Slots

| Slot | Prop | Description |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| character | { index, value, active } | index starts at zero, value at one; active means fully selected; replaces the rating symbol |
| read | { value, text } | Custom reading content retaining nullable models |

Precedence: grading > character > icon/half-icon/empty-icon > default icon. String icons require global registration; component values do not.

### Rate Methods

focus() focuses the rating; blur() removes focus. Readonly remains focusable, while disabled leaves the Tab sequence. Arrow keys adjust, Home clears and End selects the maximum. Keyboard events from interactive children and Alt/Ctrl/Meta combinations are not intercepted. Touch and mouse share half-selection/clearing rules.

## Types

Exports RateProps, RateColor, RateIcon, RateInstance, RateExpose, RateEmits, RateCharacterSlotProps, RateSlots and RateReadScope.

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

Handled scoring keys clear pointer preview and emit hover-change(0) once if a preview was active. If a controlled parent refuses an update, the display follows the external value. Later pointer motion can preview again; unhandled keys preserve the preview.

character.active means fully selected: at 1.5, the second symbol has active=false and its wrapper carries the half-selection class. read receives { value, text }, retaining null/undefined with shared formatted text. Custom read takes precedence over empty-text without changing an empty model to zero. Neither slot executes business tasks.

before-commit uses ({ value, previousValue }, done, { signal }). Return a boolean or Promise, or call done. A synchronous undefined return waits for done; aborted signals prevent stale results from committing. Ordinary change only notifies and does not await return values.

## CSS Variables

Cedar defaults to gold stars and compact spacing. Maple defaults to the theme primary color and larger touch spacing. CSS variables with the same suffix serve the same purpose on both platforms, while defaults may differ.

`transition-duration` controls hover/color transitions, `scale-duration` controls selection animation, and `transition-timing-function` controls easing. Reduced motion disables these animations. `size` and `gap` props override the corresponding tokens for a single instance.

# Result

### Intro

It is used to show the results to users.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Next status cycles six local result states and updates the title and graphic; Reset status returns to info. These buttons neither send requests nor navigate. Result displays the supplied status without inferring it from title text.

Example source: src/result/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const statuses = ['info', 'success', 'warning', 'danger', 'question', 'empty'] as const
const index = ref(0)
const status = computed(() => statuses[index.value])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-result data-demo-result :status="status" :title="'Result: ' + status" subtitle="Local state preview">
    <template #extra>
      <mp-space wrap>
        <mp-button status="primary" @click="index = (index + 1) % statuses.length">Next status</mp-button>
        <mp-button @click="index = 0">Reset status</mp-button>
      </mp-space>
      <p aria-live="polite">Current status: {{ status }}</p>
    </template>
  </mp-result>
</template>
```

# Ripple Directive

### Intro

When the element is clicked, a water wave spreading effect is generated.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Supports touch, primary mouse clicks and host Enter / Space. Mouse ripples expand from the press location and end on release or window blur. Nonprimary buttons and compatibility mouse events after touch are ignored. Keyboard ripples expand from the center; use native buttons for interactive hosts.

Example source: src/ripple/example/demos/basic-usage.vue

```vue
<script setup></script>

<template>
  <div v-ripple class="ripple-example__block mp-elevation--2">点击</div>
</template>

<style lang="less" scoped>
@import '../../../style/elevation.less';

.ripple-example__block {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  align-items: center;
  height: 100px;
  user-select: none;
  cursor: pointer;
  -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
  background-color: var(--mp-color-fill-3);
  transition: background-color 0.25s;
}
</style>
```

### Custom Color

### Styles

MapleResolver directive resolution automatically imports `@maple-design/ui-vue/ripple/style`. When registering Ripple without the resolver, explicitly import that style in the application entry. Runtime code does not import CSS, so the package can be imported on the server. Unmounting or disabling cancels pending animations; keyboard state belongs to each instance.

## Usage notes

### Motion

Repeated release does not duplicate work. Disabling/unmounting cleans owned timers/direct child ripples without removing nested instances. Document listeners bind to the mount-time ownerDocument; rebinding after cross-document movement is out of scope. Enter/Space activate on this host and end only on matching keyup/blur. Plain divs must provide their own interactive semantics, keyboard behavior and accessible names; v-ripple supplies none.

## API

### Ripple Options

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `currentColor` | _string_ | `currentColor` |
| `disabled` | Whether to disable ripple decoration | _boolean_ | `false` |

## CSS Variables

The following CSS variables support customization with [ThemeProvider](#/en-US/theme-provider).

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-ripple-color` | `currentColor` | `background-color` |
| `--mp-ripple-cubic-bezier` | `cubic-bezier(0.68, 0.01, 0.62, 0.6)` | `transition` |
| `--mp-ripple-expand-duration` | `200ms` | `transition` |
| `--mp-ripple-fade-duration` | `140ms` | `transition` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-ripple-color: currentColor;
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

### Motion

expand-duration controls transform expansion; cubic-bezier controls its easing. fade-duration controls linear opacity appearance/disappearance. Put variables on the actual directive host so generated ripples inherit them. color overrides ripple-color. Both platforms default to 200ms/140ms.

250ms is the minimum display/post-fade cleanup wait, not visual duration or the complete lifecycle. Runtime reads computed ripple duration/delay. Fade starts no earlier than the later of creation+250ms or activation+expansion duration; deletion waits max(250ms, fade duration). 600ms/800ms overrides are not truncated. 0ms/unstyled cases retain cleanup floors. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce hides decorative ripples without changing host events. Expansion is sampled at creation/activation; fade at fade start. Arbitrary midphase CSS changes/custom animations are not guaranteed.

The binding type `RippleDirectiveValue` is exported from the package root and Ripple entry, with optional `color` and `disabled` fields. Color changes affect subsequently created waves. `disabled` controls decoration only; it does not disable the host. Global `Context.enableRipple` prevents new waves while existing waves finish normally. During animation the directive temporarily sets clipping and, when needed, positioning and stacking styles. When the final wave ends, or on disable or unmount, it restores styles it still owns and preserves values changed by application code. Coordinates account for axis-aligned scaling; rotation and skew are not guaranteed.

<!-- Source: src/row/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/row -->

# Row

24-column Flex layout. Row manages gutters and alignment; Col manages spans, offsets, ordering and breakpoints. Use Grid for CSS Grid collapse and suffix items.

> **Choosing a layout**
>
> - Grid + GridItem: Use for form columns and card grids with consistent column widths, spans, responsive column counts, or collapsed rows and suffix items.
> - Row + Col: Use for 24-column Flex layouts that need horizontal/vertical alignment, wrapping control, fixed and flexible widths together, or responsive ordering. Row controls the row; Col controls width, offset and order.
> - Space: Use for simple groups of buttons, tags or text that only need spacing, direction and alignment. Use native Flex for more flexible width allocation.


Horizontal and vertical gutters both default to 16px (`gutter=[16, 16]`). An explicit number or responsive object sets only the horizontal gutter. Use a tuple for both axes, or `gutter=0` to remove spacing.

## Basic examples

### 24-column layout

Example source: src/row/example/demos/basic.vue

```vue
    >
    <mp-row
      ><mp-col v-for="i in 3" :key="i" :span="8"><div class="cell">8</div></mp-col></mp-row
    >
  </div>
</template>
```

Wrapping examples compare wrapped and ordinary `div` modes. Ordinary mode removes Row layout and child Col spacing. Gap examples distinguish horizontal/vertical spacing. Row uses Flex, not CSS Grid.

## Responsiveness and accessibility

Row resolves responsive gutter with JavaScript matchMedia, using xs for SSR and synchronizing the viewport after mounting. Col uses CSS media queries: SSR already emits all configured classes without waiting for measurement. Breakpoints use viewport width: xs is the base; sm ≥576, md ≥768, lg ≥992, xl ≥1200 and xxl ≥1600px. Only configured fields override earlier values. Offset starts at the logical inline edge and mirrors in RTL. Order affects visual positioning while preserving DOM, keyboard and assistive technology reading order.

Span, offset and their breakpoint fields accept integers from 0 through 24. A zero span hides the column; offset 24 shifts it by a full row width. Order accepts finite integers, including negative values and values above 24, subject to browser CSS order computation. Gutter accepts finite nonnegative numbers, six-breakpoint objects or exactly two entries [horizontal, vertical]. Development diagnostics report unknown breakpoints, invalid numbers and enum values. Invalid span falls back to 24; invalid offset/order is ignored; breakpoint objects retain valid fields; invalid gutter components fall back to zero.

## Imports

Grid contains only Grid.Item. Import the independent Row and Col components from the library root or their row/col subpaths; installing Grid does not register them.

# SafeArea

Keep edge-aligned content clear of display cutouts, rounded corners and the home indicator. Browsers normally provide the insets; an App WebView can supply its own values.

## When to use

| Layout | Approach |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Content away from viewport edges | Usually no extra configuration |
| Bottom actions or fullscreen edge content | Wrap the affected region and choose `edges` |
| Popup or TabBar already handles safe areas | Use its own switch; avoid adding the same outer padding |
| Native host already avoids an edge | Explicitly override that edge with `0` |

## Basic examples

### Bottom padding and nesting

Stripes show safe-area padding. Change the inset, set it to zero, or disable nested protection to compare duplicate spacing, even on desktop.

Example source: src/safe-area/example/demos/en-US/basic.vue

```vue
      <label
        >Bottom inset (CSS px)<mp-input-number v-model="bottom" :min="0" :max="80" aria-label="Bottom inset"
      /></label>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="consume">Prevent duplicate nested padding</mp-checkbox>
    </div>
    <p>Stripes show safe-area padding. Set the inset to zero or disable nested protection to compare.</p>
    <mp-safe-area class="safe-area-basic__outer" :edges="['bottom']" :insets="{ bottom }" :consume="consume">

    </mp-safe-area>

  </section>
```

```vue
  // Local transport exercises the actual uploader lifecycle; no file is transmitted.

  let percent = 0
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    percent = Math.min(100, percent + (uploadScenario.value === 'slow' ? 5 : 25))
    onProgress({ percent })
    if (percent < 100) {
      return
    }
    clearInterval(timer)

      failedUploads.add(file.uid)
      onError(new Error('本地模拟失败，请重试'))

      onSuccess({ local: true })

const viewportPreset = ref('portrait')
const viewportHeightMode = ref('small')
const duoViewport = computed(() => duoViewports[viewportPreset.value])
const insets = reactive({ top: 24, right: 0, bottom: 34, left: 0 })
const previewRoot = ref(null)
const previewScroll = ref(null)
const nativeSize = ref(false)
const availableWidth = ref(390)
const viewportWidth = computed(() => duoViewport.value?.width ?? (orientation.value === 'landscape' ? 844 : 390))
const viewportHeight = computed(() =>
  duoViewport.value
    ? viewportHeightMode.value === 'large'
      ? duoViewport.value.largeHeight
      : duoViewport.value.smallHeight
    : orientation.value === 'landscape'
      ? 390
      : 720,
)
const previewScale = computed(() => (nativeSize.value ? 1 : Math.min(1, availableWidth.value / viewportWidth.value)))
const canvasStyle = computed(() => ({
  width: `${viewportWidth.value * previewScale.value}px`,
  height: `${viewportHeight.value * previewScale.value}px`,
}))
const measurements = ref(null)
const effectiveInsets = computed(() =>
  Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(insets).map(([side, value]) => [side, Math.max(0, Math.min(120, Number(value) || 0))]),
  ),
)
const previewStyle = computed(() => ({
  width: `${viewportWidth.value}px`,
  transform: `scale(${previewScale.value})`,
  height: `${viewportHeight.value}px`,
  ...Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(effectiveInsets.value).map(([side, value]) => [`--mp-safe-area-${side}`, `${value}px`]),
  ),
  '--mp-field-presentation-viewport-max-height': `${viewportHeight.value - effectiveInsets.value.top}px`,
}))
function preset(value) {
  if (value === 'duo-right' || value === 'duo-left') {
    if (!duoViewport.value) {
      viewportPreset.value = 'duo-outer-portrait'
    }
    const selected = duoViewports[viewportPreset.value]
    orientation.value = selected.width > selected.smallHeight ? 'landscape' : 'portrait'
    Object.assign(insets, selected.insets, value === 'duo-right' ? { left: 12, right: 72 } : { left: 72, right: 12 })
    return
  }
  if (duoViewports[value]) {
    viewportPreset.value = value
    const selected = duoViewports[value]
    orientation.value = selected.width > selected.smallHeight ? 'landscape' : 'portrait'
    Object.assign(insets, selected.insets)
    return
  }
  if (value === 'zero') {
    Object.assign(insets, { top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0 })
    return
  }
  viewportPreset.value = value
  orientation.value = value === 'landscape' ? 'landscape' : 'portrait'
  Object.assign(
    insets,
    value === 'landscape' ? { top: 0, right: 44, bottom: 21, left: 44 } : { top: 24, right: 0, bottom: 34, left: 0 },
  )
}
function measure() {
  const root = previewRoot.value
  if (previewScroll.value) {
    availableWidth.value = Math.max(1, previewScroll.value.clientWidth - 4)
  }
  if (!root) {
    return
  }
  const style = (selector) => getComputedStyle(root.querySelector(selector))
  const shell = style('.brand-form-shell')
  const footer = style('.brand-form-footer')
  const nested = style('.brand-form-footer-nested')
  const panel = [...root.querySelectorAll('.mp-field-presentation__panel')].find(
    (el) => el.getBoundingClientRect().height > 0,
  )
  measurements.value = {
    top: parseFloat(shell.paddingTop),
    right: parseFloat(shell.paddingRight),
    left: parseFloat(shell.paddingLeft),
    footer: parseFloat(footer.paddingBottom),
    nested: parseFloat(nested.paddingBottom),
    panelBase: panel ? parseFloat(getComputedStyle(panel).getPropertyValue('--mp-field-presentation-padding')) : 8,
    panel: panel
      ? ['paddingLeft', 'paddingRight', 'paddingBottom'].map((key) => parseFloat(getComputedStyle(panel)[key]))
      : null,
  }
}
const noDuplicate = computed(
  () =>
    measurements.value &&
    measurements.value.footer === effectiveInsets.value.bottom &&
    measurements.value.nested === 0 &&
    measurements.value.top === effectiveInsets.value.top &&
    measurements.value.left === effectiveInsets.value.left &&
    measurements.value.right === effectiveInsets.value.right &&
    (!measurements.value.panel ||
      measurements.value.panel.every(
        (value, i) => value === measurements.value.panelBase + effectiveInsets.value[['left', 'right', 'bottom'][i]],
      )),
)
let resizeObserver
let mutationObserver
onMounted(() => {
  resizeObserver = new ResizeObserver(measure)
  resizeObserver.observe(previewRoot.value)
  resizeObserver.observe(previewScroll.value)
  mutationObserver = new MutationObserver(measure)
  mutationObserver.observe(previewRoot.value, { attributes: true, childList: true, subtree: true })
  measure()
})
watch([effectiveInsets, orientation, viewportWidth, viewportHeight], async () => {
  await nextTick()
  measure()
})
onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  resizeObserver?.disconnect()
  mutationObserver?.disconnect()
  uploadTimers.forEach(clearInterval)
})
defineExpose({
  model,
  form,
  insets,
  orientation,
  measurements,
  preset,
  viewportPreset,
  viewportHeightMode,
  viewportWidth,
  viewportHeight,
  calendarMode,
  calendarZone,
  rangeLock,
  dateScenario,
  guardedOpen,
  guardedPopup,
  guardMode,
})
</script>
```

### Component integration

Choose an edge-aligned component, adjust bottom, left and right insets independently and open it. Expand the measurements when you need exact values. Simulation stays local to this example.

Example source: src/safe-area/example/demos/en-US/affected-components.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import { SafeArea } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const bottom = ref(34)
const left = ref(12)
const right = ref(72)
function preset(side: 'left' | 'right' | 'zero') {
  left.value = side === 'left' ? 72 : side === 'right' ? 12 : 0
  right.value = side === 'right' ? 72 : side === 'left' ? 12 : 0
  bottom.value = side === 'zero' ? 0 : 34
}
const active = ref('popup')
const open = ref(false)
const host = ref<HTMLElement>()
const person = ref('a')
const consumers = [
  'popup',
  'picker',
  'action-sheet',
  'number-keyboard',
  'tab-bar',
  'floating-panel',
  'fab',
  'field-editor',
]
const insets = computed(() => ({ top: 0, bottom: bottom.value, left: left.value, right: right.value }))
watch(
  [host, insets],
  ([target, value], previous) => {
    const old = previous?.[0]
    if (old && old !== target) {
      SafeArea.setInsets(null, old)
    }
    if (target) {
      SafeArea.setInsets(value, target)
    }
  },
  { flush: 'post' },
)
onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  if (host.value) {
    SafeArea.setInsets(null, host.value)
  }
})
const measurements = ref<{ component: string; padding: string; margin: string; bottom: string }[]>([])
function measure() {
  measurements.value = Array.from(
    host.value?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(
      '.mp-popup__content, .mp-picker, .mp-tab-bar, .mp-floating-panel, .mp-fab',
    ) ?? [],
  ).map((element) => {
    const style = getComputedStyle(element)
    return { component: active.value, padding: style.padding, margin: style.margin, bottom: style.bottom }
  })
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" align="stretch">
    <div>Bottom px <mp-input-number v-model="bottom" :min="0" :max="80" /></div>
    <div>Left px <mp-input-number v-model="left" :min="0" :max="120" /></div>
    <div>Right px <mp-input-number v-model="right" :min="0" :max="120" /></div>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="preset('right')">Duo · Right</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="preset('left')">Duo · Left</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="preset('zero')">Zero</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p>Duo asymmetric simulation; values are not device constants.</p>
    <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="active">
      <mp-select
        v-model="active"
        aria-label="active"
        :options="consumers.map((value) => ({ value, label: value }))"
        @change="open = false"
      />
    </mp-form-item>
    <mp-collapse class="safe-area-measurements"
      ><mp-collapse-item title="Inspect spacing" name="details">
        <mp-button @click="measure">Measure current values</mp-button>
        <div v-if="measurements.length" class="safe-area-measurements__scroll">
          <table>
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>Component</th>
                <th>Padding</th>
                <th>Margin</th>
                <th>Bottom</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              <tr v-for="(row, index) in measurements" :key="index">
                <td>{{ row.component }}</td>
                <td>{{ row.padding }}</td>
                <td>{{ row.margin }}</td>
                <td>{{ row.bottom }}</td>
              </tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
        <p v-else>Open a component, then measure.</p>
      </mp-collapse-item></mp-collapse
    >
    <div ref="host" class="safe-area-consumers" aria-label="Component safe-area preview">
      <mp-safe-area :edges="[]">
        <p>Local host：{{ insets }}</p>
        <mp-button v-if="['popup', 'picker', 'action-sheet', 'number-keyboard'].includes(active)" @click="open = true"
          >Open</mp-button
        >
        <mp-popup
          v-if="active === 'popup'"
          v-model:open="open"
          placement="bottom"
          :popup-container="host"
          safe-area-inset-bottom
          safe-area-inset-left
          safe-area-inset-right
        >
          <div class="safe-area-content">Popup consumes bottom, left and right.</div>
        </mp-popup>
        <mp-picker
          v-if="active === 'picker'"
          v-model:open="open"
          dynamic
          :popup-container="host"
          :columns="[[{ text: 'Alice' }, { text: 'Bob' }]]"
          safe-area
        />
        <mp-action-sheet
          v-if="active === 'action-sheet'"
          v-model:open="open"
          :popup-container="host"
          :actions="[{ name: 'Alice' }, { name: 'Bob' }]"
          safe-area
        />
        <mp-number-keyboard
          v-if="active === 'number-keyboard'"
          v-model:open="open"
          :popup-container="host"
          safe-area
          title="Keyboard"
        />
        <mp-tab-bar v-if="active === 'tab-bar'" safe-area>
          <mp-tab-bar-item label="Home" /><mp-tab-bar-item label="Profile" />
        </mp-tab-bar>
        <mp-floating-panel v-if="active === 'floating-panel'" :anchors="[140, 240]" :popup-container="host" safe-area
          ><p>Bottom, left and right padding</p></mp-floating-panel
        >
        <mp-fab v-if="active === 'fab'" :popup-container="host" safe-area />
        <mp-select
          v-if="active === 'field-editor'"
          v-model="person"
          edit-mode="popup"
          :popup-container="host"
          :options="[
            { value: 'a', label: 'Alice' },
            { value: 'b', label: 'Bob' },
          ]"
        />
      </mp-safe-area>
    </div>
  </mp-space>
</template>
<style scoped>

  max-width: 100%;
```

### Asymmetric safe areas on Duo

Duo outer and inner displays in both orientations, plus left and right Split View windows, update the viewport and simulated insets together. Expanded / collapsed toolbar controls select small / large viewport heights. Left / right avoidance swaps asymmetric insets on the current viewport; zero only clears the insets.

WebKit Safari 27.1 CSS viewport sizes (width × small/large height): outer portrait 382 × 580/618, outer landscape 594 × 368/406, inner portrait 669 × 867/902, inner landscape 951 × 585/620, each split window 385 × 571/609. These are not physical display dimensions. Insets are independent stress-test values, not measured insets for those viewports; do not compensate again for a side rail Safari already excludes. Read each edge independently. The host must update the remaining insets relative to the WebView content viewport after folding, unfolding, rotation, Split View or safe-area changes; pass `0` for edges already handled by the host.

Safari and native apps may expose different usable viewports. Keep browser `env()` defaults unless the host supplies accurate remaining insets. Do not copy native side-rail widths into a webpage. A fold inside the screen requires separate segmented layout and cannot be represented by four edge insets.

References: [WebKit web adaptation](https://webkit.org/blog/18486/webkit-features-for-safari-27-1/) and [Apple safe-area guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111461/).

## Application usage

### 1. Enable browser support

Configure the viewport in application HTML:

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover" />
```

Wrap regions needing safe-area spacing. Browser `env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)` is read by default; do not hardcode a phone's dimensions:

```vue
<mp-safe-area :edges="['bottom']">
  <mp-button status="primary" block>Submit</mp-button>
</mp-safe-area>
```

For on-demand imports, load `@maple-design/ui-vue/safe-area/style`. Auto-import resolvers handle styles automatically.

### 2. Override when the app supplies insets

Pass CSS pixels still needing avoidance within the WebView content viewport, not physical device pixels or keyboard height.

```ts
import { SafeArea } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

SafeArea.setInsets({ top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 34, left: 0 })
SafeArea.setInsets(null) // Remove overrides; restore browser/inherited values
```

`0` is valid. Each call replaces all four target-edge overrides; omitted edges inherit/browser-default. App adapters own initial snapshots, rotation/resume updates and unsubscription. Clear global overrides when removing adapters. Without native data, keep browser defaults.

### 3. Local containers and popups

```vue
<mp-safe-area :edges="[]" :insets="{ top: 0, bottom: 20 }">
  <!-- Supply local insets without adding padding at this layer -->
  <YourContent />
</mp-safe-area>
```

Insets inherit along actual DOM. Body-teleported popups leave local containers: use root overrides or a `popup-container` with correct insets. `SafeArea.setInsets(insets, hostElement)` updates only that host. Iframes must load styles in their own document.

## Avoid duplicate spacing

- `edges`: padding `edges` at this layer; `[]` adds none.
- `insets`: effective subtree `insets`; omitted edges inherit, `0` means no avoidance needed.
- `consume`: `true` by default; used edges reset to 0 on direct element children, inherited by descendants.

Choose one avoidance layer per content path. If a bottom bar uses `safe-area`, do not duplicate its padding outside. Use `consume=false` only when descendants need independent compensation. Viewport-fixed elements need explicit hosts/insets; ordinary-flow ancestor compensation is insufficient.

| Component | Enable through | Behavior |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Popup | `safe-area-inset-top/right/bottom/left` | Add padding to specified edges |
| Picker / ActionSheet / NumberKeyboard | `safe-area` | Delegate bottom, left and right spacing to Popup |
| TabBar / FloatingPanel | `safe-area` | Add bottom, left and right padding |
| Fab | `safe-area` | Respect the vertical and horizontal safe areas at the corner selected by position |
| Form popup editor | Automatically handle bottom/left/right insets | Inherit the actual popup host without changing draft confirmation |

## Common questions

**Why no spacing in desktop browsers?** Without device safe areas, `env()` is usually 0. Examples use local simulated values for visibility.

**Should bottom change when the keyboard opens?** Do not treat keyboard height as safe-area inset. WebView resizing, overlays, input scrolling and fixed action bars depend on host policy.

**Does changing themes reset safe areas?** No. Themes manage appearance; SafeArea manages environment insets. Simulators check layout, but status bars, keyboards and rotation require actual iOS/Android WebView tests.

## API

### SafeArea Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| ------- | -------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
| edges | `SafeAreaEdge[]`<br>`SafeAreaEdge: 'left' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'top'` | `['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left']` | Physical edges receiving spacing; [] compensates none and does not represent position or expansion direction |
| insets | SafeAreaInsets | undefined | Local CSS-px overrides; 0 is valid, omitted edges inherit |
| consume | boolean | true | Clear already-consumed edges for descendants |
| tag | string | div | Container element |

Default slot is content; no new events.

`SafeArea.setInsets(insets, target?)`: insets is SafeAreaInsets or null; target defaults to document.documentElement. Replaces four-edge overrides while retaining other target CSS, without registering native listeners. Safely returns during SSR without document. Component insets can render in SSR without writing request data into global modules. Values must be finite/nonnegative or throw TypeError; DOM stays unchanged until every value validates.

## Types

```ts
import SafeArea from '@maple-design/ui-vue/safe-area'
import type { SafeAreaProps, SafeAreaInstance, SafeAreaEdge, SafeAreaInsets } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
import type { SafeAreaProps as SubSafeAreaProps } from '@maple-design/ui-vue/safe-area'
const options: SafeAreaProps = { edges: ['bottom'], insets: { bottom: 0 } }
SafeArea.setInsets({ bottom: 0 })
```

SafeAreaEdge is the top/right/bottom/left union, and SafeAreaInsets maps those edges optionally to numbers. SafeAreaInstance represents a component instance without a setInsets method. setInsets is static on the component object; do not call it on a template ref.

## CSS Variables

These are runtime-environment values, not Alps/Firefly brand-theme values. Use ThemeProvider for brands and SafeArea for app adaptation; neither clears the other.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-safe-area-bottom` | `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` (`html`) | `margin-bottom`, `padding-bottom` |
| `--mp-safe-area-left` | `env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px)` (`html`) | `inset-inline-end`, `margin-left`, `padding-left`, `width` |
| `--mp-safe-area-right` | `env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px)` (`html`) | `inset-inline-end`, `margin-right`, `padding-right`, `width` |
| `--mp-safe-area-top` | `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` (`html`) | `margin-top`, `padding-top` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-safe-area-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

# Search

Start with keyword submission, then field models, then controlled history and presentation. Requests stay in application code.

### Intro

Search is used to enter keywords and trigger queries in lists, result pages, or top toolbars. It includes a search icon, clear button, and optional cancel action.

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Example source: src/search/example/demos/en-US/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('')
function handleSearch(result) {
  console.log('search', result)
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-search v-model="value" label="Address" placeholder="Search" @search="handleSearch" />
</template>
```

### Field Select

Example source: src/search/example/demos/en-US/fields.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { SearchResult } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const field = ref('name')
const model = ref<Record<string, unknown>>({ name: 'Device A', tenant: 'demo' })
const accepted = ref(true)
const history = ref(['Device A', '42'])
const result = ref<SearchResult>()
const fields = [
  { value: 'name', label: 'Device name', placeholder: 'Enter name' },
  { value: 'id', label: 'Device ID', placeholder: 'Enter ID' },
]
function updateModel(proposal: Record<string, unknown>) {
  if (accepted.value) {
    model.value = proposal
  }
}
function updateField(proposal: string) {
  if (accepted.value) {
    field.value = proposal
  }
}
function search(next: SearchResult) {
  result.value = next
  history.value = next.recentSearches
}
</script>
<template>
  <div class="search-demo">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="accepted">Accept updates (uncheck to demonstrate controlled rejection)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-search
      :model="model"
      :model-field="field"
      :fields="fields"
      :recent-searches="history"
      edit-mode="direct"
      search-button
      button-text="Search"
      clearable
      @update:model="updateModel"
      @update:model-field="updateField"
      @search="search"
    />
    <mp-button variant="text" @click="model = { name: 'External value', tenant: 'demo' }"
      >Replace model externally</mp-button
    >
    <div>Accepted model：{{ model }}</div>
    <pre v-if="result">{{ JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) }}</pre>
  </div>
</template>
<style scoped>
.search-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 12px;
  max-width: 100%;
}
.search-demo pre {
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
</style>
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { SearchResult } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const keyword = ref('')
const popup = ref(false)
const history = ref(['Project A', 'Device B'])
const lastAction = ref('No search yet')
function recordSearch(result: SearchResult) {
  history.value = result.recentSearches
  lastAction.value = result.modelValue ?? ''
}
function recordAction(result: SearchResult) {
  lastAction.value = result.modelValue ?? ''
}
</script>
<template>
  <div class="search-demo">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="popup">popup fullscreen search (uncheck for inline)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-search
      v-model="keyword"
      :edit-mode="popup ? 'popup' : 'direct'"
      :recent-searches="history"
      label="Resource"
      placeholder="Enter resource name"
      clearable
      show-action
      action-text="Cancel"
      @cancel="lastAction = 'Cancelled'"
      @search="recordSearch"
    />
    <mp-search
      v-model="keyword"
      search-button
      :button-props="{ variant: 'outline' }"
      placeholder="Custom button slots"
      @search="recordAction"
    >
      <template #button-icon><span aria-hidden="true">⌕</span></template>
      <template #button-default>Find</template>
    </mp-search>
    <div>Last action：{{ lastAction }}</div>
  </div>
</template>
<style scoped>
.search-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 12px;
  max-width: 100%;
}
</style>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading-mode="line"` uses FieldDecorator's shared loading line; default mode retains the component's existing indicator. Loading does not imply disabled or readonly.

### Native form and popup ownership

The active keyword input exclusively owns its configured id. References and cached closed editors use distinct internal ids and leave the accessibility/Tab order. Visible labels associate with their input; ariaLabel takes precedence over label text. Field selectors describe field choice, while keyword inputs have their own accessible name.

The reference supplies one native FormData name/value. Popup edits immediately update the same model without duplicating name submission. To use native required and other HTML constraints inside the popup, give the form an id and explicitly associate inputAttrs.form. Closing releases editor constraint ownership so cached inputs cannot block later submission.

Popup input immediately updates v-model. cancel ends the history interface; business code cancels its own requests. A nonempty recent-searches list is required to open history. Switching to reading releases history state. Business state controls loading: editing stays available and repeat searches are blocked. Ordinary search/change listener Promises do not control waiting.

Example source: src/search/example/demos/native-form.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref, useId } from 'vue'

const uid = useId()
const formId = 'native-search-form-' + uid
const inputId = 'native-search-query-' + uid
const helpId = 'native-search-help-' + uid
const form = ref()
const query = ref('report')
const waiting = ref(false)
const loadingMode = ref('default')
const searchEvents = ref(0)
const submitted = ref([])
function submit() {
  if (waiting.value || !form.value) {
    return
  }
  submitted.value = [...new form.value.ownerDocument.defaultView.FormData(form.value).entries()]
}
</script>
<template>
  <section>
    <p>编辑历史弹层后提交，关键词只提交一份。Edit in history, then submit one native keyword value.</p>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button html-type="button" @click="waiting = !waiting">切换等待 / Toggle waiting</mp-button>
      <mp-button html-type="button" @click="loadingMode = loadingMode === 'default' ? 'line' : 'default'"
        >切换加载布局 / Toggle loading layout</mp-button
      >
    </mp-space>
    <form :id="formId" ref="form" @submit.prevent="submit">
      <mp-search
        v-model="query"
        label="关键词 / Keywords"
        edit-mode="popup"
        :recent-searches="['report', 'invoice']"
        :loading="waiting"
        :loading-mode="loadingMode"
        :input-attrs="{ id: inputId, name: 'keyword', form: formId, required: true, 'aria-describedby': helpId }"
        @search="searchEvents++"
      />
      <p :id="helpId">
        输入即时更新；HTML 必填校验关联此表单。Edits update immediately; native required validation belongs to this
        form.
      </p>
      <mp-button html-type="submit" :disabled="waiting">记录原生表单 / Capture native form</mp-button>
    </form>
    <p>阅读预览 / Reading preview</p>
    <mp-search :model-value="query" read-pretty :loading="waiting" :loading-mode="loadingMode" />
    <pre class="native-search-results" role="status">{{
      JSON.stringify({ submitted, searchEvents, query, waiting, loadingMode })
    }}</pre>
  </section>
</template>
<style scoped>
.native-search-results {
  max-width: 100%;
  overflow-x: auto;
}
</style>
```

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Search Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------- |

| `default-field` | Uncontrolled default field | _string_ | `-` |
