The following CSS variables support customization with [ThemeProvider](#/en-US/theme-provider).

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-background` | `var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay)` | `background`, `background-image` |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-border-radius` | `var(--mp-time-picker-border-radius, 4px)` | `border-radius` |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-column-label-height` | `var(--mp-internal-temporal-panel-column-label-height)` | `height` |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-next-day-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-secondary)` | `color` |
| `--mp-time-range-title-font-size` | `var(--mp-picker-title-font-size, 16px)` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-time-range-title-text-color` | `var(--mp-picker-title-text-color, #555)` | `color` |
| `--mp-time-range-toolbar-height` | `var(--mp-picker-toolbar-height, 44px)` | `height` |
| `--mp-time-range-toolbar-padding` | `var(--mp-picker-toolbar-padding, 0 4px)` | `padding` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-time-range-picker-background: var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- Source: src/time/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/time -->

# Time

If a parent keeps the popup open after confirmation, repeated confirmation without a new selection is deduplicated. A fresh time selection starts a new transaction and can be confirmed again.

While expanded, the native combobox uses `aria-controls` to identify its own named popup. Closing updates the state and removes the link. `aria-label` and `aria-describedby` reach the native input. Custom selected/trigger slots must preserve accessible names, keyboard operation and state associations.

In clock and wheel modes, min/max are inclusive same-day bounds. A minute stays selectable when some of its seconds are available. Second constraints compare the complete clock value, not seconds from a different hour. Use TimeRange show-next-day for overnight ranges, rather than reversed min/max.

Installing Time also registers TimePicker, which is available through the static member `Time.Picker`.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

```vue
  <mp-space direction="column" size="lg">
    <mp-time v-model="time" format="HH:mm" placeholder="Select a time" clearable />
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Compare Input, Button, Select, date/time fields and other single-line controls at the same size. Field variants share the height scale; Button uses outline here. DatePicker/TimePicker are panels; this example uses Date/Time fields. The example includes selected and clearable values, removable tags and long multiple selections. Select/Cascader keep the same size height with tag-nowrap. Long tag text uses ellipsis while removal icons remain available; tags scroll horizontally while clear and arrow controls stay outside the scrolling area. Hover, focus or tap truncated tag text to read its full content; dismiss with an outside click or Escape without changing the selected value. Restore values after clearing to repeat the comparison. Multiline text and wrapping multiple selections can grow with content.

```vue
            edit-mode="direct"
            :size="size"
            :variant="variant"
            :options="selectedCascaderOptions"
            multiple
            tag-nowrap
            clearable
            placeholder="Cascader long values"
          />
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  </section>
</template>
```

### Field appearance and nested options

hint controls the floating label (both Cedar and Maple default to false) and is suppressed by an outer Form label. line defaults to true; text-color/focus-color/blur-color accept optional color strings. An unset error inherits Form state; explicit false overrides it. TimeRange separator defaults to `~` and accepts an empty string. Cedar and Maple fields both default to outline; filled and standard remain explicit options.

The field owns values, defaults, open state, format, steps, bounds, disabled rules and readonly/disabled state. Set these directly on the field, not inside timePickerProps/timeRangePickerProps. Nested options customize presentation only; model/select/confirm listeners cannot replace the field flow. Types reject owner properties and runtime filtering removes them, even when a top-level constraint is unset.

Maple pickerProps accepts visual options such as optionHeight/optionCount, not columns, fieldNames, selection, toolbar or open state. popupProps accepts positioning, appearance and lifecycle callbacks, but not open/defaultOpen or open-update listeners. Top-level popupContainer (including false) takes priority. Nested options in standalone time panels follow the same ownership rules.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/field-appearance.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:00')
const hint = ref(false)
const error = ref(false)
const line = ref(true)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="hint">Floating hint</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="error">Explicit error state</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="line">Border / underline</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm"
      variant="outline"
      placeholder="Choose time"
      :hint="hint"
      :error="error"
      :line="line"
      focus-color="#6750a4"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Field interactions use one local controller: select stages a draft; confirmation validates current rules before commit and Form change notification. Clearing uses the commit path with undefined, followed by clear; it is blocked when readonly/disabled or not clearable. Readonly fields remain focusable; repeated focus/blur notifications are deduplicated. A pending controlled close request cannot repeat a commit.

The panel owns one draft and confirmation flow; presentation content only renders that state. The example above counts valid confirmations and shows the extra slot. Reconfirming an unchanged value emits confirm without an extra change event.

### Visible wheel fields

`time-fields` controls time columns and their order on fields and standalone panels. Range endpoints share the configuration.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `time-fields` | readonly TimePickerField[]<br>`TimePickerField: 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | According to the time format | Controls time wheels, including those embedded in calendars. |

Lists must be nonempty and unique. Explicit lists determine columns and order; only omitted props use defaults. Date and time fields cannot be mixed. Edits preserve hidden units in the full draft. Changing fields does not submit the model. Nested presentation props cannot override root field configuration.

Time format retains its string parsing/display/output protocol. time-fields changes columns only and retains hidden units represented in the model. Twelve-hour hour columns automatically include AM/PM.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/time-fields.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import type { TimePickerField } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const props = defineProps<{ range?: boolean }>()
const preset = ref('hour-minute')
const fields = computed<TimePickerField[]>(() =>
  preset.value === 'minute-hour' ? ['minute', 'hour'] : preset.value === 'second' ? ['second'] : ['hour', 'minute'],
)
const time = ref('09:30:17')
const times = ref(['09:30:17', '18:00:23'])
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" align="stretch">
    <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="Visible wheel fields">
      <mp-radio-group
        v-model="preset"
        aria-label="Visible wheel fields"
        :options="[
          { label: 'Hour / minute', value: 'hour-minute' },
          { label: 'Minute / hour', value: 'minute-hour' },
          { label: 'Second only', value: 'second' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </mp-form-item>
    <mp-time-range v-if="props.range" v-model="times" :time-fields="fields" format="HH:mm:ss" />
    <mp-time v-else v-model="time" :time-fields="fields" format="HH:mm:ss" />
    <p>Hidden fields retain their values: {{ props.range ? times : time }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Hour/minute/second steps

With 12-hour display and a 5-hour step, hours remain anchored to midnight: 0/5/10/15/20, not restarted at noon. AM offers 12/05/10 and PM offers 03/08. Selecting 03 PM commits 15:30:00 because this Demo retains HH:mm:ss as its model format. Changing the rules preserves the old 09:30:00; cancellation does not commit aligned candidates. Only confirmation writes the selected value. Enable Disable 15:00 to combine disabled-hours with the step: 03 PM is unavailable while 08 PM still means 20:00. Turning off Accept controlled updates records proposals without changing the business value; re-enable it before confirming an accepted value. Proposal counts are not acceptance counts. Other non-dividing steps and physical touch remain separate coverage.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/step.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:30:00')
const coarse = ref(false)
const fiveHours = ref(false)
const blockAfternoon = ref(false)
const accept = ref(true)
const proposals = ref(0)
const disabledHours = () => (blockAfternoon.value ? [15] : [])
function update(next) {
  proposals.value++
  if (accept.value) {
    value.value = next
  }
}
const step = computed(() => ({ hour: fiveHours.value ? 5 : 1, minute: coarse.value ? 30 : 15, second: 10 }))
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space class="time-step-demo" direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="fiveHours">12-hour display with a 5-hour step</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="coarse">Use 30-minute intervals</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="blockAfternoon">Disable 15:00 (03 PM)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="accept">Accept controlled updates</mp-checkbox>
    <p>Confirmation validates the current step. Changing a rule does not change the committed value.</p>
    <mp-time
      :model-value="value"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      :use12-hours="fiveHours"
      :step="step"
      :disabled-hours="disabledHours"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
      @update:model-value="update"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
    <span role="status">Proposals：{{ proposals }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Time bounds

After tightening the minimum to 10:30:40, the field retains 10:30:38 but the panel cannot confirm it. Selecting and confirming the inclusive maximum 10:31:02 updates the model. Editing seconds to 00 and canceling keeps seconds 02.

`min` / `max` are optional strings, with no bound by default. Use 24-hour `HH:mm` or `HH:mm:ss`, independently of format/use12Hours. Both endpoints are inclusive; omitted seconds mean 00. Range endpoints are validated individually; showNextDay does not make the bounds wrap across midnight. Reversed bounds allow no commit; unparseable bounds are treated as unset.

Changing bounds does not rewrite the external model. Commits must satisfy bounds, steps and disabled callbacks. Hidden seconds are validated as 00. Coarse list columns are disabled when their whole hour/minute is out of bounds; confirmation validates the complete time. Use hide-disabled-options to hide disabled choices.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/bounds.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('10:30:38')
const narrow = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <p>
      Inclusive bounds: 10:30:38–10:31:02. Narrowing the bounds preserves the current model but prevents invalid
      confirmation.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="narrow">Move minimum to 10:30:40</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time v-model="value" format="HH:mm:ss" :min="narrow ? '10:30:40' : '10:30:38'" max="10:31:02" />
    <mp-time-picker v-model="value" format="HH:mm:ss" :min="narrow ? '10:30:40' : '10:30:38'" max="10:31:02" />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Wheel constraints

```vue
<script setup>

const locked = ref(false)
const disabledHours = () => (locked.value ? Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, hour) => hour) : [])

      confirmation.
    </p>
    <mp-button @click="locked = !locked">{{ locked ? 'Restore choices' : 'Block all hours' }}</mp-button>

      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      panel-type="picker"

      max="11:30:02"
```

### Panel confirmation and disabled options

For a pending single-value draft, enabling readonly, hiding disabled hours or switching to immediate mode does not submit the old draft. Unlocking does not submit it either; the next valid selection commits once. Maple wheel updates preserve the same draft without updating the parent model. Mouse/keyboard checks do not establish physical touch-inertia behavior.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/panel-behavior.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:30')
const immediate = ref(false)
const confirmations = ref(0)
const hideDisabled = ref(false)
const readonly = ref(false)
const disabledHours = () => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="immediate">Commit without confirmation</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="hideDisabled">Hide disabled hours (00–07)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="readonly">Read-only (including confirmation)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-button variant="outline" @click="value = '13:45'">Replace externally with 13:45</mp-button>
    <mp-time-picker
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm"
      :disable-confirm="immediate"
      :hide-disabled-options="hideDisabled"
      :readonly="readonly"
      :disabled-hours="disabledHours"
      @confirm="confirmations++"
    >
      <template #extra><p>Changing presentation keeps the draft; extra content uses the same slot.</p></template>
    </mp-time-picker>
    <span>Valid confirmations: {{ confirmations }}</span>
    <span>Committed value: {{ value }}</span>
    <p>With confirmation enabled, selection only changes the draft. The value above changes after confirmation.</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

The standalone panel owns its draft and commit state directly. External model replacement resets the draft without emitting selection or change events. Read-only and disabled states block selection and confirmation. Cedar renders lists; Maple renders wheels. These views do not create a second draft.

## Input and state control

### Interaction state comparison

### Text entry

`input-editable` defaults to `false` (Cedar: `true`). When enabled, tap the input to type; use the clock button or ArrowDown to open the picker/clock panel. Enter or blur commits; Escape cancels. Parsing, steps, bounds and disabled rules match panel selection. Invalid or rejected controlled edits restore the model value. Disabling editing, readonly or disabled state discards drafts. IME composition and moving between range inputs do not commit.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/text-entry.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:00')
const editable = ref(true)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="editable">Allow text entry</mp-checkbox>
    <p>
      Enter or blur to commit; Escape to cancel. Allowed range: 08:00–18:00. Use the clock button or ArrowDown to open
      the panel.
    </p>
    <mp-time v-model="value" :input-editable="editable" format="HH:mm" min="08:00" max="18:00" clearable />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Intro

Form time **field** that opens `TimePicker` in a bottom popup. Interaction matches Select picker mode: Cancel discards the draft; Confirm writes `v-model`.

For time ranges, use [`TimeRange`](llms/en-US/time-range.md). For panel-only, use [`TimePicker`](en-US/time-picker). For time range panel, use [`TimeRangePicker`](en-US/time-range-picker).

### Default and controlled values

`defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled fields/panels once; subsequent edits are retained locally. `modelValue` is authoritative when provided. `defaultOpen` initializes field visibility once. Controlled `open` requires the parent to accept `update:open`; `open-change(open: boolean)` reports requests. `clear` has no arguments. Panels support `disabled` for both range endpoints.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/default-state.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:00')
const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <p>Uncontrolled initial value</p>
    <mp-time :default-value="'09:00'" format="HH:mm" clearable />
    <p>Controlled value and visibility</p>
    <mp-time v-model="value" v-model:open="open" format="HH:mm" clearable />
    <span>{{ value }} / {{ open }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Selection and commit

On the mobile trigger, Enter / ArrowDown opens, Space opens on key release, and Escape cancels. Tab requests closure without blocking native navigation; inline uses an anchored popover and outside clicks discard its draft. Keys are scoped to the trigger, not window; composing input and custom interactive controls are ignored.

Field `focus` and `blur` events have no arguments and fire once per transition. Moving between range endpoints stays within one field. Readonly fields remain focusable but cannot open for editing; disabling a focused field releases its focus state and notifies blur.

Fields and standalone panels revalidate the current format, steps and disabled rules at commit time. Cedar text input follows the same rules. Changing constraints does not rewrite committed values. Reversed ranges are accepted only when `show-next-day` is enabled; otherwise a red footer message is shown and confirmation is disabled. Endpoints are never swapped. Clearing commits `undefined` regardless of candidate restrictions, but still respects readonly/disabled state.

`select(value, date)` reports user draft selection; `change(value, date)` reports a committed value. Both single and range fields clear to `undefined`, with an undefined date argument and a no-argument `clear` event. Date arguments represent local clock times (not next-day calendar arithmetic). Fields default to explicit confirmation; `disable-confirm` commits a valid choice immediately and requests close. Range confirmation rejects reversed endpoints unless `show-next-day` is enabled. Controlled `open` still requires parent acceptance. Standalone panels also default to confirmation; disable-confirm commits immediately without closing the panel.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/selection-events.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:00')
const immediate = ref(false)
const readonly = ref(false)
const disabled = ref(false)
const events = ref([])
function record(name, value, dates) {
  const times = Array.isArray(dates) ? dates.map((date) => date?.toLocaleTimeString()) : dates?.toLocaleTimeString()
  events.value = [JSON.stringify({ event: name, value: value ?? null, time: times ?? null }), ...events.value].slice(
    0,
    5,
  )
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="readonly">Read-only: focus allowed, edits blocked</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="disabled">Disabled: focus released, edits blocked</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="immediate">Commit immediately on selection</mp-checkbox>
    <p>Select records drafts. Change records commits. Cancel leaves the model unchanged. Clear returns undefined.</p>
    <mp-time
      v-model="value"
      :disable-confirm="immediate"
      :readonly="readonly"
      :disabled="disabled"
      format="HH:mm"
      clearable
      @select="(value, dates) => record('select', value, dates)"
      @change="(value, dates) => record('change', value, dates)"
      @clear="record('clear')"
      @click="record('click')"
      @open-change="(open) => record('open-change', open)"
      @focus="record('focus')"
      @blur="record('blur')"
    />
    <span>Model: {{ value === undefined ? 'undefined' : value }}</span>
    <mp-button variant="outline" @click="value = '15:30'">Replace model externally</mp-button>
    <small>External replacement updates the display without emitting select or change.</small>
    <div v-for="(event, index) in events" :key="index" style="overflow-wrap: anywhere">{{ event }}</div>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Replacing the model from the parent resets the draft without emitting `select` or `change`. The example includes an external-update button; confirming a user selection remains a separate action.

### Multiple independent fields

The example displays each field's model separately. Cancel discards only the current draft, and clear affects only the current field. Fields do not share models or drafts.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/multiple-fields.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const lastEvent = ref('—')
const readonly = ref(false)
const start = ref('09:00:00')
const end = ref('18:00:00')
const range = ref(['09:00:00', '18:00:00'])
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="readonly">Readonly fields remain focusable</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-input placeholder="Press Enter here: time popups should not open" />
    <small aria-live="polite">{{ lastEvent }}</small>
    <div aria-live="polite">
      <div>Start model: {{ start ?? 'undefined' }}</div>
      <div>End model: {{ end ?? 'undefined' }}</div>
      <div>Range model: {{ range ?? 'undefined' }}</div>
    </div>
    <p>Open and cancel each field in sequence. Drafts remain independent.</p>
    <mp-time
      v-model="start"
      :readonly="readonly"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      placeholder="Start"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
      @focus="lastEvent = 'start: focus'"
      @blur="lastEvent = 'start: blur'"
    />
    <mp-time
      v-model="end"
      :readonly="readonly"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      placeholder="End"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
      @focus="lastEvent = 'end: focus'"
      @blur="lastEvent = 'end: blur'"
    />
    <mp-time-range
      v-model="range"
      :readonly="readonly"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
      @focus="lastEvent = 'range: focus'"
      @blur="lastEvent = 'range: blur'"
    />
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

`format` it parses string models and controls display and emitted strings. The default is `HH:mm:ss`; with `use12-hours` and no explicit format it is `hh:mm:ss a`. Use `HH:mm` to serialize minutes, and time-fields to hide wheel seconds, `hh:mm A` for uppercase AM/PM, and `[Time] HH:mm` for literal text. Models accept formatted strings, local Date objects, or millisecond timestamps; output is always a formatted string (an array for ranges). Invalid input is not normalized or written back. `min`/`max` remain 24-hour `HH:mm[:ss]` strings, and disabled callbacks always receive actual hours 0–23.

Disabled callbacks match Cedar: disabled-hours, disabled-minutes and disabled-seconds. Both views respect inclusive same-day min/max. Overnight ranges use show-next-day. Hidden seconds are evaluated as zero. Opening a field aligns its draft to a valid candidate without writing the external model; confirmation validates again. Empty or invalid drafts cannot be confirmed after rules change.

Use open-trigger-target to control pointer opening independently. In icon mode, clicking, focusing and typing do not automatically open the panel. input-editable / filterable still controls editing or search. The suffix button, explicit keyboard commands and controlled open can open it.

### Intro

Form field: [`Time`](llms/en-US/time.md). Time range field: [`TimeRange`](llms/en-US/time-range.md). Time range panel: [`TimeRangePicker`](en-US/time-range-picker).

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`; direction changes do not modify time or commit drafts. Hour, minute and second columns follow reading order, with Left/Right moving focus visually between columns. Cedar Up/Down and Home/End move focus within the current column, Enter/Space selects, and disabled options are skipped. Maple wheels retain Up/Down and Home/End selection behavior. Existing confirmation configuration determines immediate commits. Popovers inherit source field direction.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `popup` and opens an editor when the value area is clicked. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

Inline date/time fields retain existing confirmation policies. In popover/popup, pure panels hide confirmation tools and the editor provides one confirm/cancel pair. Standalone DatePicker/DateRangePicker/TimePicker/TimeRangePicker retain panel APIs/confirmation without inheriting Form field presentation.

Mobile date fields use `panel-type` to select calendar/wheel content; `edit-mode` controls only field editing. Standalone panel content follows each panel API and is not controlled by the field `edit-mode`.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Panel actions

Mobile wheels use a rounded selection band. Single-time panels show no top summary. Field popups and independent panels share appearance.

Single-time Now sits left of confirmation tools and updates the draft under format/step/disabling rules without committing/closing. Even with `disable-confirm`, Now and later wheel edits still require confirmation; cancel discards them. Hide it with `:show-now-button="false"`. Custom `actions` can use `selectNow()`/`nowDisabled`.

Wheel headers follow actual hour/minute/second format, adding AM/PM in 12-hour mode, matching the range panel.

Panel style variables:


### Forwarded configuration boundaries

The time field manages open/defaultOpen, disabled, trigger, closeOnClickReference, preventFocus and visibility updates. An explicit top-level popup-container takes precedence over nested configuration; popupClass is merged. Inline presentation fixes popupOffset=4, and Maple also fixes unmountOnClose=true, so those nested fields may not control the final values.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

During deferred editing, clearing retains the configured valid empty-value and confirmation submits that empty value; null is not replaced by midnight. A newly created empty wheel panel may initialize a visible candidate without selecting or committing a model. Later explicit empty drafts in that panel are not automatically refilled. Reopening and cancelling does not publish another value.

### Defaults and format

Inherited, format-derived and effective-step defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props may be undefined. Without format, the default is HH:mm:ss, or hh:mm:ss a with use12Hours=true. Bounds use 24-hour clock times, separate from Date-family valueFormat/time-zone rules.

### Explicit save guard

beforeCommit(payload, done, context) belongs to field saving. payload contains value/previousValue; context has signal and optional event. Returning undefined waits for done, while boolean/Promise results settle by their result. FormItem validates candidates first; failure retains draft. Ordinary select/change/confirm/click listener returns do not use this task protocol.

## API

### Panel Events

Pure-panel business events are update:modelValue, change, select and confirm. select reports candidates; valid confirmation notifies confirm, while update:modelValue/change only occur for an actual value change. Field opening, clearing and focus events do not belong to pure panels.

Complete panel actions scope below; extra has no arguments.

```ts
import type { TimeValue } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
type PanelActionsScope = { confirm: () => boolean; canConfirm: boolean; value: TimeValue | undefined; selectNow: () => boolean; nowDisabled: boolean }
```

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

`popup-props` configures the anchored Trigger popover on both platforms. It cannot replace field open/disabled/trigger ownership. Top-level popup-container, including false, takes precedence. Panel and popup options are separate. `click(event)` fires once for an enabled field; readonly fields notify but do not open. Use `open-change(false)` for close requests, not proof that a controlled state changed. 

`suffix-icon` receives `focus: boolean` and `popupOpen: boolean`, replacing arrow-icon. `focus(index = 0)` focuses an endpoint without committing; `blur()` removes focus and requests closing.

### Pure-panel event and slot boundaries

`TimePicker`/`TimeRangePicker` do not manage fields/popups. Pass `open`, `size`, `variant`, clearing and popup configuration to `Time`/`TimeRange`.

- `select(value, date)`: edit the draft.
- `change(value, date)`: valid confirmation with a changed value; updates the model.
- `confirm(value, date)`: every valid confirmation, including unchanged values. `disableConfirm` also emits it on valid selection commits. Disabled, readonly or invalid drafts do not emit it.
- `extra`: additional explanatory content.
- `actions({ confirm, canConfirm, value })`: replace default tools. `value` is the draft; call `confirm()` to commit and disable buttons according to `canConfirm`.

Single-time events carry formatted strings and Date objects; range events carry corresponding arrays. Use field `open-change` and `update:open` to manage the popup, and field `clear` for clearing the value.

Panels edit a draft and commit on confirmation. Cancellation or closing does not commit, while clearing commits an empty value and closes immediately. Mobile time fields do not open the software keyboard. See the combined field examples in the Date documentation.

## Types

### Value types

```ts
export type TimeValue = string | number | Date
```

### Field notifications and public types

Field update:modelValue/change use TimeModelValue (TimeRangeModelValue for ranges). Normal selections commit formatted strings; explicit clears retain configured null, timestamps, Date objects or range arrays accepted by the property. Auxiliary dates may be undefined; clearing a range to an empty array also yields an empty auxiliary array. Clear does not emit select. Select remains a formatted user draft, which may be incomplete for a range.

Exports TimeEmits, TimeModelValue, TimeReadScope, TimeSuffixIconScope, TimeSlots, TimeActionsScope and TimeExpose, plus TimeRangeEmits, TimeRangeModelValue, TimeRangeReadScope, TimeRangeSlots, TimeRangeActionsScope and TimeRangeExpose. Import each from the root or its component entry. Instances include the public Expose contract.

Field read receives { value, text } with a nullable model; suffix-icon receives { focus, popupOpen }; clear-icon receives a guarded clear(event?). Range fields also support separator. Cedar direct mode supports a default custom trigger, while Maple does not. Neither platform currently forwards field loading-icon, so types do not promise it. actions/extra operate on panel drafts: Cedar forwards them in direct mode; Maple forwards them during deferred editing, not direct mode. Inner confirm is not the outer final-save entry.


<!-- time-contract:start -->

### Field event and slot parameter types

Events notify only; listener Promises are not collected. update:modelValue and change include null, 0, Date or range arrays allowed by the clearing policy. select reports formatted draft rather than saving. Field update:open/open-change are opening requests; initialization does not notify automatically.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimeModelValue` |
| `change` | `TimeModelValue, Date \| undefined` |
| `select` | `string \| undefined, Date \| undefined` |
| `clear` | `()` |
| `click` | `Event` |
| `focus` | `()` |
| `blur` | `()` |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |
| `open-change` | `boolean` |

Field focus(index?)/blur() target the actual input or trigger without changing model. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?). prefix, selected, suffix and extra are unscoped; ranges also have separator. Cedar direct mode has a custom default trigger slot; Maple does not.

actions/extra belong to panel draft: Cedar direct forwards them, Maple direct does not, and deferred editing forwards them. Panel confirm() is not the outer field final-save entry point. Pure panels have actions/extra, without field read/clear-icon/loading-icon slots. Standalone panels expose no ref.confirm() method; custom confirmation uses actions.confirm.

### Panel event parameter types

Arguments are tuples from the corresponding public event type. Date arguments are parsed from formatted clock times and do not promise to preserve an input Date calendar day.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `TimePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `TimePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `TimePickerEmits['confirm']` |

```ts
import { Time, TimePicker, type TimeProps, type TimeEmits,
  type TimeSlots, type TimeInstance, type TimePickerProps,
  type TimePickerEmits, type TimePickerSlots } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
```

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.


Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

# Timeline

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `reverse`: Whether reverse order

Example source: src/timeline/example/demos/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div :style="{ marginBottom: '40px' }">
    <span :style="{ verticalAlign: 'middle', marginRight: '8px' }"> Reverse </span>
    <mp-radio-group v-model="isReverse" :style="{ marginBottom: '30px' }" @change="onChange">
      <mp-radio :value="false">No Reverse</mp-radio>
      <mp-radio :value="true">Reverse</mp-radio>
    </mp-radio-group>
  </div>
  <mp-timeline :reverse="isReverse">
    <mp-timeline-item label="2017-03-10">The first milestone</mp-timeline-item>
    <mp-timeline-item label="2018-05-12">The second milestone</mp-timeline-item>
    <mp-timeline-item label="2020-09-30">The third milestone</mp-timeline-item>
  </mp-timeline>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const isReverse = ref(false)

const onChange = (bool) => {
  isReverse.value = bool
}
</script>
```

## Content and presentation

### Pending

Preview configuration: `align="center"`, `orientation="horizontal"`, `:checked="!!pendingProps.reverse"`, `:checked="!!pendingProps.pending"`.


Example source: src/timeline/example/demos/pending.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-row align="center" :style="{ marginBottom: '24px' }">
    <mp-checkbox
      :checked="pendingProps.orientation === 'horizontal'"
      @change="(v) => onChange({ orientation: v ? 'horizontal' : 'vertical' })"
    >
      horizontal &nbsp; &nbsp;
    </mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox :checked="!!pendingProps.reverse" @change="(v) => onChange({ reverse: v })">
      reverse &nbsp; &nbsp;
    </mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox
      :checked="!!pendingProps.pending"
      @change="(v) => onChange({ pending: v ? 'This is a pending dot' : false })"
    >
      pending &nbsp; &nbsp;
    </mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox :checked="!!pendingProps.hasPendingDot" @change="(v) => onChange({ hasPendingDot: v })">
      custom pendingDot
    </mp-checkbox>
  </mp-row>
  <mp-timeline v-bind="pendingProps">
    <template v-if="pendingProps.hasPendingDot" #dot>
      <mp-icon-fire :style="{ color: '#e70a0a' }" />
    </template>
    <mp-timeline-item label="2017-03-10" dotColor="#52C419"> The first milestone </mp-timeline-item>
    <mp-timeline-item label="2018-05-12" dotColor="#F5222D"> The second milestone </mp-timeline-item>
    <mp-timeline-item label="2020-09-30">The third milestone</mp-timeline-item>
  </mp-timeline>
  <mp-timeline>
    <template #pending>Waiting for the next milestone</template>
  </mp-timeline>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { IconFire as MpIconFire } from '@maple-design/icons-vue'

const pendingProps = ref({})

const onChange = (newProps) => {
  pendingProps.value = {
    ...pendingProps.value,
    ...newProps,
  }
}
</script>
```

## API

### Timeline Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | :----------: |
| reverse | Whether reverse order | `boolean` | `false` |
| orientation | Horizontal/vertical axis of the timeline line, default vertical; constrains valid item sides | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'vertical'` |
| mode | The display mode of Timeline | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'alternate'` | `'left'` |
| pending | Append a pending item; true has no text, and a string is displayed as its content. | `boolean\|string` | `-` |
| label-position | Position of label text | `'relative' \| 'same'` | `'same'` |

### Timeline Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------ | :------: | ---- |
| default | Timeline items | - |
| dot | Pending item icon | - |
| pending | Pending item content; adding this slot appends an item and takes precedence over the pending prop text | - |

### TimelineItem Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | :-------: |
| dot-color | Node color | `string` | `-` |
| dot-type | Node type: outlined/filled circle | `'hollow' \| 'solid'` | `'solid'` |
| line-type | Timeline line style: solid/dashed/dotted | `'solid' \| 'dashed' \| 'dotted'` | `'solid'` |
| line-color | Timeline color | `string` | `-` |
| label | Label text | `string` | `-` |
| content-placement | Current per-item side relative to the timeline in alternate mode: left/right for vertical and top/bottom for horizontal. Constrained by mode and orientation | `TimelineItemContentPlacement`<br>`'left' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'top'` | `-` |

Use `content-placement` for the physical side of the content: top/bottom in horizontal layouts and left/right in vertical layouts. `mode` controls the arrangement.

### TimelineItem Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop | Version |
| ------ | :--------: | ---- | :----- |
| default | Item content | - |  |
| dot | Custom node | - |  |
| label | Custom label | - | 2.50.0 |

## Types

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { TimelineProps, TimelineItemProps, TimelineSlots, TimelineItemSlots, TimelineMode, TimelineLabelPosition, TimelineDotType, TimelineLineType, TimelineItemContentPlacement, TimelineInstance, TimelineItemInstance } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
```

## Reading direction and keyboard interaction

Timeline inherits its container's reading direction. Horizontal nodes and connectors follow LTR/RTL. `reverse` independently controls visual reversal; direction changes do not mutate node data or automatically change `reverse`.

Explicit vertical `mode="left"` / `mode="right"` and item physical sides retain their meaning; `alternate` continues alternating. Labels and custom content inherit text direction normally.

| `--mp-timeline-label-relative-margin` | `100px` | `margin-left`, `margin-right` |
| `--mp-timeline-label-relative-max-width` | `100px` | `max-width` |
| `--mp-timeline-label-text-color` | `var(--mp-color-text-3)` | `color` |
| `--mp-timeline-line-bg` | `var(--mp-sys-color-border-default)` | `border-color` |
| `--mp-timeline-size-line-width` | `1px` | `border-left-width`, `border-top-width`, `height`, `width` |
| `--mp-timeline-vertical-margin-content-bottom` | `4px` | `margin-bottom` |
| `--mp-timeline-vertical-margin-content-left` | `16px` | `margin-left`, `margin-right`, `padding-left`, `padding-right` |
| `--mp-timeline-vertical-margin-line-bottom` | `4px` | `bottom` |
| `--mp-timeline-vertical-margin-line-top` | `4px` | `top` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-timeline-content-text-color: var(--mp-color-text-1);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Tooltip

SSR limitation: a trigger slot node using both `v-for` and `v-memo` can make server rendering fail. Remove `v-memo` from that slot node when rendering on the server; ordinary `v-for` remains supported. In Vue 3.5.13, a standalone dynamic `v-memo` can also fail in this slot. The same limitation can affect the `content` slot; remove `v-memo` there for server rendering.

Provides a short description for a control, icon, or truncated text. It responds to hover and keyboard focus by default. Use Popover for interactive content.

## Usage notes

### Configuration

These are actual :root defaults. Prefer component variables for business customization; internal positioning variables are not public API.

With Teleport, variables must be in the actual popup scope, for example through `popup-style`. Trigger-button variables do not automatically inherit into popups.

## API

Tooltip inherits Trigger positioning, container, controlled state, and `close` policies. Its defaults are `hide-empty=true` and `auto-fit-transform-origin=true`; an omitted `animation-name` uses the Tooltip animation. Empty content hides only the tooltip and does not change `open`; component nodes count as content even when they render no content, producing an empty tooltip and description relationship. Conditionally render the component node in the slot when its content may be empty. The instance exposes seven methods: `open`, `close`, `resize`, `allowClose`, `getReference`, `focusReference`, and `setReference`.

### Tooltip Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v-model:open | Controlled open state | `boolean` | — |
| default-open | Initial uncontrolled state | `boolean` | `false` |
| content | Hint content | `string` | — |
| status | Panel intent | `default \| primary \| info \| success \| warning \| danger` | `default` |
| size | Implemented sizes | `xs \| md` | `md` |
| color | Background color | `string` | — |
| text-color | Custom text color | `string` | — |
| trigger | Interaction | `TriggerEvent \| TriggerEvent[]`<br>`TriggerEvent: 'manual' \| 'focus' \| 'hover' \| 'click' \| 'contextMenu'` | `['hover', 'focus']` |
| placement | Preferred popup side relative to the trigger, default top. With the default auto-fit-position enabled, Trigger may flip and constrain it to the viewport when space is limited; this is not a fixed final position | `TriggerPlacement`<br>`'left' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'top-start' \| 'top-end' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-end' \| 'left-start' \| 'left-end' \| 'right-start' \| 'right-end'` | `top` |
| show-arrow | Show the arrow | `boolean` | `true` |
| popup-offset | Main-axis distance | `number` | `10` |
| popup-translate | Additional screen-axis translation | `[number, number] \| Record` | — |
| popup-container | Render target; false renders locally | `string \| HTMLElement \| false` | `body` |
| reference | External trigger element | `string \| HTMLElement \| SVGElement` | — |
| disabled | Prevent opening | `boolean` | `false` |
| unmount-on-close | Unmount after close | `boolean` | `true` |

### Tooltip Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| update:open | Requests a controlled open-state change |
| open-change | Requests any open-state change |
| open | Opening starts |
| opened | Enter transition completes |
| close | Closing starts |
| closed | Leave transition completes |
| click-outside | Clicked outside the popup |

### Tooltip Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Trigger element |
| content | Tooltip `content`; falls back to `content` |

### Tooltip Methods

`open()`、`close()`、`resize()`、`allowClose()`、`getReference()`、`setReference()`、`focusReference()`。

Tooltip content has role="tooltip". While open, its ID is added to the actual reference aria-describedby without duplicating existing descriptions. Closing, changing references or unmounting removes only that tooltip ID and preserves other descriptions. Use color for backgrounds and text-color for text; backgroundColor and boolean xs props are not supported.

## CSS Variables

All built-in themes use opacity 1. Colored solid text follows Button on-dark in both light/dark modes. Maple dark mode retains 4px radius, 14px font and 8px/16px vertical/horizontal padding. Neutral surfaces remain dark in both modes. `color` sets content/arrow backgrounds; `text-color` sets text. Explicit content-style/arrow-style override their respective nodes. Recheck custom colors/opacity.

<!-- Source: src/trigger/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/trigger -->

# Trigger

SSR limitation: a trigger or `content` slot node using both `v-for` and `v-memo` can make server rendering fail. The trigger slot can fail even while the popup is closed; the `content` slot can fail when the popup is open or `unmount-on-close=false`. Remove `v-memo` from that slot node when rendering on the server; ordinary `v-for` remains supported. In Vue 3.5.13, a standalone dynamic `v-memo` can also fail in the trigger slot. With Vue 3.5.45, a standalone dynamic `v-memo` rendered correctly in both slots. The same-node loop limitation also reproduces in a plain Vue component that reads the slot as VNodes.





Replacing or clearing the popup reference, or unmounting the component, removes the old window scroll listeners.

After closing or unbinding, pending positioning and scroll-close tasks do not affect a popup opened later.

mouse-enter-delay / mouse-leave-delay are interaction delays, separate from CSS enter/leave duration. Cancel, replacement, KeepAlive deactivation and unmount invalidate dequeued commits; retained requests cannot schedule while inactive or disposed. Reactivation accepts new requests without replaying old delays. Controlled open remains caller-owned.

Clicking another independent reference closes the previous top layer before opening the new one. Nested popups remain inside their parent. Controlled open state only receives a close request; the owner may reject it.

### Introduction

A style-agnostic floating-layer primitive for interaction, positioning, teleporting, stacking and open state. Prefer Tooltip, Popover or Menu for end-user features; use Trigger directly when building another floating component.

```vue
        <div class="trigger-demo__panel">Trigger 只负责浮层行为，面板外观由使用者决定。</div>
      </template>
    </mp-trigger>
  </div>
```

## Interaction and control

### Controlled state and offset

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | `hover/click/focus/contextMenu/manual`, or an array | Controlled state and offset |
| `placement` | Preferred popup side relative to the trigger, default bottom. With the default auto-fit-position enabled, Trigger may flip and constrain it to the viewport when space is limited; this is not a fixed final position | Controlled state and offset |
| `popup-offset` | Outward main-axis distance | Controlled state and offset |
| `popup-translate` | Screen-axis translation or placement map | Controlled state and offset |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


`popup-offset` moves outward on the placement main axis. `popup-translate` adds a screen-axis x/y translation.

The demo accepts requests through `v-model:open` and displays the parent's value. External controls update that value; Enter/Space activates the native trigger button, while Escape and outside clicks request closing. It does not demonstrate rejected controlled requests. Trigger is listed in the component menu so its right-side preview shows these demos instead of the home page.

Example source: src/trigger/example/demos/controlled.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="trigger-controlled-demo">
    <mp-space>
      <mp-button @click="open = true">外部打开</mp-button>
      <mp-button variant="outline" @click="open = false">外部关闭</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <mp-trigger
      v-model:open="open"
      trigger="click"
      placement="bottom-start"
      :popup-offset="10"
      :popup-translate="[16, 0]"
    >
      <mp-button variant="text">受控触发元素</mp-button>
      <template #content
        ><div class="trigger-controlled-demo__panel">open = {{ open }}</div></template
      >
    </mp-trigger>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.trigger-controlled-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--mp-sys-space-8);
  padding: calc(var(--mp-sys-space-8) * 2) var(--mp-sys-space-6);
}

.trigger-controlled-demo__panel {
  padding: var(--mp-sys-space-5) var(--mp-sys-space-6);
  color: var(--mp-sys-color-content-primary);
  background: var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay);
  border: 1px solid var(--mp-sys-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--mp-sys-radius-sm);
}
</style>
```

## Triggers and positioning

### Popup placement

placement is the preferred side; auto-fit-position defaults to true and can change the final side. It is not a position coordinate. top-start describes anchor placement and alignment, whereas top-left is a container corner. Top/bottom start and end mirror with reading direction; left/right remain physical, and vertical start/end remain top/bottom.

## Usage notes

### Configuration

These are actual :root defaults. Prefer component variables for business customization; internal positioning variables are not public API.

With Teleport, variables must be in the actual popup scope, for example through `popup-style`. Trigger-button variables do not automatically inherit into popups.

### Reduced motion

`allowClose()` restores the internal closing gate; there is no public counterpart to disable closing, and this method cannot prevent closure.

## API

### Trigger Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | Controlled open state | _boolean_ | `-` |
| `default-open` | Initial uncontrolled state | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `trigger` | `hover/click/focus/contextMenu/manual`, or an array | _TriggerEvent \| TriggerEvent[]_<br>`TriggerEvent: 'manual' \| 'focus' \| 'hover' \| 'click' \| 'contextMenu'` | `hover` |
| `disabled` | Prevent opening | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `reference` | External reference element | _string \| HTMLElement \| SVGElement_ | `-` |
| `placement` | Preferred popup side relative to the trigger, default bottom. With the default auto-fit-position enabled, Trigger may flip and constrain it to the viewport when space is limited; this is not a fixed final position | _TriggerPlacement_<br>`'left' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'top-start' \| 'top-end' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-end' \| 'left-start' \| 'left-end' \| 'right-start' \| 'right-end'` | `bottom` |
| `strategy` | Positioning strategy | _absolute \| fixed_ | `absolute` |
| `cover` | Cover the reference on the main axis | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `popup-offset` | Outward main-axis distance | _number_ | `0` |
| `popup-translate` | Screen-axis translation or placement map | _[number, number] \| Record_ | `-` |
| `align-point` | Position at the pointer | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `popup-container` | Mount container; false renders in place. When switching within a document or between accessible same-origin iframes, focus restoration is attempted for native inputs and buttons that have not been transferred, including equivalent elements in open Shadow DOM. Opaque hosts that may contain closed Shadow DOM are not restored automatically. | _string \| HTMLElement \| false_ | `body` |
| `auto-fit-position` | Flip and shift into the viewport | _boolean_ | `true` |
| `auto-fit-popup-width` | Match reference width | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `auto-fit-popup-min-width` | Match reference minimum width | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `auto-fix-position` | Reposition when the reference changes size or when a CSS transition or animation on the reference or its ancestors ends or is canceled. On touch devices an open element-anchored popup also follows page movement. Popup, positioning parent and window resize handling remain active when disabled | _boolean_ | `true` |
| `update-at-scroll` | Reposition while scrolling | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `scroll-to-close` | Close after the scroll threshold | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `scroll-to-close-distance` | Close threshold | _number_ | `0` |
| `show-arrow` | Render the decorative arrow | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `hide-empty` | Skip a directly empty content slot; a component node counts as nonempty even if it renders nothing | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `prevent-focus` | Prevent positioning-layer mousedown from stealing focus | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `unmount-on-close` | Unmount after leave | _boolean_ | `true` |
| `animation-name` | Vue Transition name | _string_ | `trigger-fade` |
| `duration` | Transition duration | _number \| object_ | `-` |
| `auto-fit-transform-origin` | Derive transform origin from final placement | _boolean_ | `false` |
| `opened-class` | Merge into the first default-slot node when open; external references do not receive this class | _string \| array \| object_ | `-` |
| `reference-attrs` | Attributes applied to the actual reference or a function of open; original attributes are restored when removed, replaced or unmounted | _TriggerReferenceAttrs \| ((open: boolean) => TriggerReferenceAttrs)_ | `-` |
| `popup-class` | Custom positioning-layer classes | `ClassName` | `-` |
| `popup-style` | Custom positioning layer styles | `CSSProperties` | `-` |
| `content-class` | Custom content layer classes | `ClassName` | `-` |
| `content-style` | Custom content layer styles | `CSSProperties` | `-` |
| `arrow-class` | Custom arrow classes | `ClassName` | `-` |
| `arrow-style` | Custom arrow styles | `CSSProperties` | `-` |

Interaction timing and dismissal props also include `mouse-enter-delay`, `mouse-leave-delay`, `focus-delay`, `popup-hover-stay`, `blur-to-close`, `close-on-click-reference`, `click-outside-to-close`, `esc-to-close`, and `restore-focus`.

### Trigger Events

`update:open`、`open-change`、`open`、`opened`、`close`、`closed`、`click-outside`、`resize`。

### Trigger Slots / Methods

default provides the reference; `content` supplies popup `content`. Exposes `open()`, `close()`, `resize()`, `allowClose()`, `getReference()`, `setReference()`, `focusReference()`, `isTopLayer()`.

### Accessibility

`trigger="focus"` supports keyboard focus; Escape closes only the topmost popup. Trigger does not define business `role`/ARIA relationships; semantic wrappers supply them.

With focus triggers, one outside pointer interaction that causes both blur and click requests closing once. If controlled state rejects the request, a later independent click can request closing again; `click-outside` continues to report outside click events.

## Native event modifiers on reference elements

Native `click`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`, `focusin`, `focusout`, `contextmenu` listeners and `.once`, `.capture`, `.passive` modifiers bind to the actual reference element, not the popup. `.once` follows the native element's listener lifetime. Replacing a callback does not reactivate a consumed listener; replacing the reference or removing and readding a listener starts a new lifetime. Deactivation/unmount unbind listeners. Listeners only notify; returned Promises do not drive opening/loading, and errors enter Vue's event error chain.

`aria-describedby` from `reference-attrs` is merged and deduplicated with existing reference descriptions; cleanup or reference replacement restores the original attribute.

When the first reference in the default slot is a native element, its server-rendered HTML includes the supplied `aria-*` and `data-*` attributes. For an external reference, Trigger applies the attributes to that element after mounting.

When several triggers share an element, their description IDs are combined. Removing one trigger drops the IDs contributed only by that trigger. Removing the last trigger restores the latest value supplied by the application.

Fixed positioning uses the actual `fixed` containing block when an ancestor has a transform, filter, perspective, or containing CSS property. Axis-aligned scaling is accounted for; rotated or skewed coordinate systems are not guaranteed. For accessible same-origin iframe references, the reference and popup documents share coordinate conversion and event handling; cross-origin or unrelated browsing contexts are not supported. With `update-at-scroll`, scrolling either document or a scrollable ancestor updates the popup.

When the popup is mounted inside a closed ShadowRoot in the same document, Trigger distinguishes clicks inside the popup from outside clicks. Clicks passing through the closed-root host are classified in a later task; account for this if application behavior depends on dismissal event timing.

When a reference is slotted into a scroll container inside a closed ShadowRoot, the outer Trigger cannot access the slot or container and cannot listen to its scrolling automatically. The closed component can call the Trigger instance's `resize()` on internal scroll or slot changes. For scroll-to-close behavior, call `close()` internally using an application-specific threshold, and remove listeners on unmount.

A popup mounted inside an iframe remains clipped by that iframe's viewport. Content outside the iframe is invisible even when cross-document coordinate conversion is correct.

## CSS Variables

Tooltip/Popover define arrow appearance themselves. Override their component variables rather than Trigger arrow-background.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-trigger-arrow-background` | `var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay)` | `background-color` |
| `--mp-trigger-arrow-radius` | `var(--mp-sys-radius-sm)` | `border-radius` |
| `--mp-trigger-arrow-size` | `var(--mp-sys-space-4)` | `height`, `width` |
| `--mp-trigger-transition-duration` | `var(--mp-sys-motion-duration-fast)` | `transition` |
| `--mp-trigger-transition-easing` | `var(--mp-sys-motion-easing-standard)` | `transition` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-trigger-arrow-background: var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

### Reduced motion

Built-in CSS transitions follow `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Removing transitions does not change final visibility, selected/expanded state or event semantics. Applications control custom animations inside slots.

# Typography

### Intro

Cedar (PC) ships a full typography utility set (alignment, type scale recipes, size, family, weight, line-height; prefix `c-`).  
Maple (Mobile) **does not** duplicate that pack: mobile type is covered by components and `--mp-font-size-*` tokens; use [Atomic CSS](#/en-US/atomic-css) Uno / TW presets when you need atomic classes.

Shared semantic text-color utilities remain in Utilities: `mp-text-1` … `mp-text-4` (`--mp-color-text-*`).

### Related

- [Utilities Overview](#/en-US/utilities)
- [Atomic CSS](#/en-US/atomic-css)
- [Utility Spec](#/en-US/utilitySpec)

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/typography/example/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { onThemeChange } from '@maple-design/cli-vue/client'

onThemeChange()
</script>

<template>
  <div class="demo mp-px-16 mp-py-16">
    <div class="mp-text-1 mp-mb-8">mp-text-1 主文案</div>
    <div class="mp-text-2 mp-mb-8">mp-text-2 次级</div>
    <div class="mp-text-3 mp-mb-8">mp-text-3 辅助</div>
    <div class="mp-text-4">mp-text-4 弱化</div>
    <div class="mp-text-3 mp-mt-24">PC 排版工具类见 Cedar Typography；Mobile 用 token / 原子化 CSS。</div>
  </div>
</template>

<style lang="less">
@import '../../style/theme/css-variables.less';
@import '../../utilities/style/utilities.less';
</style>
```

# Updates and migration

Check package versions and release notes before upgrading. Review affected props, events, types and theme variables, keep the dependency lockfile and verify critical workflows. Do not assume API compatibility without migration guidance.

## Changelog

[Read the full Changelog](https://github.com/loca-spirit/maple-design-mobile/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for features, fixes and breaking changes. Unreleased entries are not necessarily included in the current npm package.

## Upgrade checks

1. Identify your installed and target versions and read the changes between them.
2. Update affected props, events, types and theme variables.
3. Update the lockfile and verify builds and critical interactions before releasing your application.

# Upload

Select files by clicking or dragging, with image lists, previews and controlled uploads. Examples use local files and simulated requests.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Choose one or more local files and remove them from the list. Without action / custom-request, files are read locally without requests.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/read-only.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { UploadFileItem } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-upload v-model="files" multiple />
</template>
```

### List types

Switch between text, picture and picture-card using the same file list. Add or remove files, then switch layouts without losing the selection.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/list-type.vue

```vue

      'data:image/svg+xml,' +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="160" viewBox="0 0 240 160"><rect width="240" height="160" fill="#e0e7ff"/><circle cx="180" cy="42" r="20" fill="#fbbf24"/><path d="M0 160L80 50L150 140L190 90L240 160Z" fill="#6750a4"/></svg>',
      ),
    status: 'success',
    percent: 100,
  },
])
const listType = ref<UploadListType>('picture')
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space class="upload-list-type-demo" direction="column">
    <mp-form>
      <mp-form-item label="List type">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="listType" aria-label="List type">
          <mp-radio value="text">text</mp-radio>
          <mp-radio value="picture">picture</mp-radio>
          <mp-radio value="picture-card">picture-card</mp-radio>
        </mp-radio-group>

      available.

</template>
```

### File validation

Accept images only, up to 3 files and 2 MiB per image. Rejections show a reason; remove an image to make room for another.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/picture-limits.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { UploadFileItem, UploadRejectedFile } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([])
const feedback = ref('')
const reasons: Record<string, string> = {
  accept: 'Images only',
  'max-files': 'Up to 3 images',
  'max-file-size': 'Up to 2 MiB per image',
}
function handleRejected(items: UploadRejectedFile[]) {
  feedback.value = items.map((item) => `${item.file.name}: ${reasons[item.reason] || item.reason}`).join('; ')
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>Choose up to 3 images, each no larger than 2 MiB. Remove an image to add another.</p>
    <mp-upload
      v-model="files"
      list-type="picture"
      accept="image/*"
      multiple
      :max-files="3"
      :max-file-size="2 * 1024 * 1024"
      @rejected="handleRejected"
    />
    <p role="status">{{ feedback }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Readonly, disabled and reading mode

Switch the same data between editable, readonly, disabled and reading modes. Readonly keeps preview; disabled blocks interaction; reading mode shows the value without the upload editor.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/states.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

    name: 'landscape.svg',

      ),
    status: 'success',
    percent: 100,
  },
])
const state = ref('editable')
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-form
      ><mp-form-item label="State">
        <mp-radio-group v-model="state" aria-label="State">
          <mp-radio value="editable">Editable</mp-radio>
          <mp-radio value="readonly">Readonly</mp-radio>
          <mp-radio value="disabled">Disabled</mp-radio>
          <mp-radio value="reading">Reading</mp-radio>
        </mp-radio-group>
      </mp-form-item></mp-form
    >
    <mp-upload
      v-model="files"
      list-type="picture"
      accept="image/*"
      multiple
      :readonly="state === 'readonly'"
      :disabled="state === 'disabled'"
      :read-pretty="state === 'reading'"
    />
    <p role="status">Selected files: {{ files.length }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Upload workflow

### Manual upload, progress and retry

Choose files or add a sample, then start uploading. Cancel active uploads and retry a simulated first failure. A local timer simulates requests without sending files.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/manual-upload.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, onDeactivated, ref } from 'vue'
import type { UploadCustomRequest, UploadFileItem, UploadInstance, UploadProgressEvent } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([])
const uploader = ref<UploadInstance>()
const failOnce = ref(false)
const timers = new Set<ReturnType<typeof setInterval>>()
const attempts = new Map<string, number>()
const pending = computed(() => files.value.some((file) => ['ready', 'error', 'canceled'].includes(file.status)))
let sequence = 0
function addSample() {
  const file = new File(['Local upload example.'], `example-${++sequence}.txt`, { type: 'text/plain' })
  files.value = [
    ...files.value,
    { uid: `sample-${sequence}`, name: file.name, size: file.size, type: file.type, file, status: 'ready', percent: 0 },
  ]
}
const request: UploadCustomRequest = ({ file, onProgress, onSuccess, onError }) => {
  const attempt = (attempts.get(file.uid) ?? 0) + 1
  attempts.set(file.uid, attempt)
  const reject = failOnce.value && attempt === 1
  let percent = 0
  const stop = () => {
    clearInterval(timer)
    timers.delete(timer)
  }
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    percent += 10
    onProgress({ percent } as UploadProgressEvent)
    if (percent >= 100) {
      stop()
      if (reject) {
        onError(new Error('Simulated upload failure; retry to continue'))
      } else {
        onSuccess({ ok: true })
      }
    }
  }, 150)
  timers.add(timer)
  return { abort: stop }
}
function cleanup() {
  uploader.value?.abort()
  timers.forEach((timer) => clearInterval(timer))
  timers.clear()
}
onBeforeUnmount(cleanup)
onDeactivated(cleanup)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="failOnce">Fail the first attempt</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-upload ref="uploader" v-model="files" multiple :auto-upload="false" :custom-request="request" />
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="addSample">Add a sample</mp-button>
      <mp-button :disabled="!pending" @click="uploader?.submit()">Start upload</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p role="status">Completed: {{ files.filter((file) => file.status === 'success').length }} / {{ files.length }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Confirm before removing

Removing a file opens a confirmation Dialog. Cancel keeps the file; confirm removes it.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/remove-confirm.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, ref } from 'vue'
import type { UploadFileItem } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([
  {
    uid: 'sample-image',
    name: 'landscape.svg',
    type: 'image/svg+xml',
    url:
      'data:image/svg+xml,' +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="160" viewBox="0 0 240 160"><rect width="240" height="160" fill="#e0e7ff"/><circle cx="180" cy="42" r="20" fill="#fbbf24"/><path d="M0 160L80 50L150 140L190 90L240 160Z" fill="#6750a4"/></svg>',
      ),
    status: 'success',
    percent: 100,
  },
])
const open = ref(false)
const name = ref('')
let resolveRemoval: ((allow: boolean) => void) | undefined
function beforeRemove(file: UploadFileItem) {
  name.value = file.name || ''
  open.value = true
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
    resolveRemoval = resolve
  })
}
function finish(allow: boolean) {
  const resolve = resolveRemoval
  resolveRemoval = undefined
  open.value = false
  resolve?.(allow)
}
onBeforeUnmount(() => finish(false))
</script>

<template>
  <mp-upload v-model="files" list-type="picture" accept="image/*" multiple :before-remove="beforeRemove" />
  <mp-dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    title="Confirm removal"
    @confirm="finish(true)"
    @cancel="finish(false)"
    @closed="finish(false)"
  >
    <p>Remove file {{ name }}?</p>
  </mp-dialog>
</template>
```

### Externally managed upload state

Manage progress and results through the read event. Add a sample and complete it to see the controlled list update; no built-in request is used.

Example source: src/upload/example/demos/en-US/external-state.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const files = ref([])
const hasUploading = computed(() => files.value.some((file) => file.status === 'uploading'))
const hasRetryable = computed(() => files.value.some((file) => ['error', 'canceled'].includes(file.status)))
let sequence = 0

function read(file) {
  file.status = 'uploading'
  file.percent = 40
}

function addExample() {
  const file = new File(['Local external upload demo.'], `external-${++sequence}.txt`, { type: 'text/plain' })
  const item = {
    uid: `external-${sequence}`,
    name: file.name,
    size: file.size,
    type: file.type,
    file,
    status: 'ready',
    percent: 0,
  }
  read(item)
  files.value = [...files.value, item]
}

function complete() {
  files.value = files.value.map((file) =>
    file.status === 'uploading' ? { ...file, status: 'success', percent: 100 } : file,
  )
}

function retry() {
  files.value = files.value.map((file) =>
    ['error', 'canceled'].includes(file.status) ? { ...file, status: 'uploading', percent: 40 } : file,
  )
}
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <p>Application-managed progress and results. Add local sample items without choosing a file or making a request.</p>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="addExample">Add external upload item</mp-button>
      <mp-button :disabled="!hasUploading" @click="complete">Complete externally</mp-button>
      <mp-button :disabled="!hasRetryable" @click="retry">Retry externally</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <mp-upload v-model="files" edit-mode="direct" :show-retry-button="false" @read="read" />
    <p>Queue：{{ files.map((file) => `${file.name}: ${file.status} (${file.percent}%)`).join('；') || 'Empty' }}</p>
  </div>
</template>
```
